title: Jalon Daniels: "Dream come true" to be starting QB for the Buccaneers today
summary: The undrafted rookie will start today against the Packers with Baker Mayfield out.
full_text: During his six-year college career at Kansas, Jalon Daniels was never viewed as a sure thing to make it to the NFL. He certainly wasn't viewed as a prospect who was likely to be a starting quarterback in the NFL as a rookie. But that's exactly what Daniels is today: The starting quarterback for the Buccaneers against the Packers. Baker Mayfield is out, and Daniels, an undrafted rookie, is the next man up. He says he's ready. "I don't even know if I can put it into words," Daniels said. "It's a dream come true. It's a dream come true to even play for an NFL organization. To be able to go out there and have my first NFL start, it means everything." As is usually the case for an undrafted rookie, Daniels had taken very few practice reps with the first-string offense until last week, when Mayfield was injured. But he says he has prepared like a starter. "Every single week I prepare as if I'm going to get the starting reps," Daniels said. The 0-3 Buccaneers desperately need a win. If Daniels can get it done, it will be one of the most surprising stories of this NFL season.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Deion Sanders, Colorado lose third in a row
summary: After a 2-0 start to the 2026 season, Deion Sanders and the Colorado Buffaloes have lost their third game in a row.
full_text: '' After a 2-0 start to the 2026 season, Deion Sanders and the Colorado Buffaloes have lost their third game in a row. The latest loss came at home to No. 10 Texas Tech, 29-7. Colorado led at the half, 7-3. The Red Raiders pulled away after intermission. The Buffaloes had turnovers on four straight possessions. Colorado scored on its opening drive of the game and didn't score again thereafter. Isaac Wilson, the brother of NFL quarterback Zach Wilson, started at quarterback over Julian Lewis. Wilson threw three interceptions on the night. For the Buffaloes, the season-opening win at Georgia Tech is a fading memory. Next up for Colorado are games against No. 13 Utah and No. 19 Oklahoma State. Which means that 2-3 could become 2-5. If the current trend continues, it's fair to wonder whether Deion will return for a fifth season in 2027.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jeremiah Smith: "I'm the best player in the country"
summary: After his latest phenomenal performance of the 2026 season, Ohio State receiver Jeremiah Smith stated the obvious.
full_text: After his latest phenomenal performance of the 2026 season, Ohio State receiver Jeremiah Smith stated the obvious. "You've just got to [let] the Heisman voters or whoever it is know that I’m the best player in the country ," Smith said, via Adam Rittenberg of ESPN. "I've got to be there." In the Buckeyes' 31-14 win over Iowa, Smith broke the Ohio State record for career receptions with 207 and career touchdown catches with 36. He also tied the program record with his 15th career 100-yard game. In five games this season, Smith has 44 catches for 617 yards and nine touchdowns. Against the Hawkeyes (not the Hawks), Smith had 11 catches for 206 yards and two touchdowns. Smith NIL deal surely requires him to keep playing. As it relates to his NFL prospects, however, the hay is in the barn. He could stop playing right now and still be one of the top picks in the 2027 draft.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bill Belichick and UNC fall to 2-2 with loss to Notre Dame
summary: Bill Belichick's second season at North Carolina started at 2-0.
full_text: Bill Belichick's second season at North Carolina started at 2-0. After losses to Clemson and Notre Dame, he's now 2-2. The Irish beat the Tar Heels on Saturday, 37-26. After North Carolina returned the opening kickoff of the second half for a touchdown cut the score to 21-20, Notre Dame pulled away. With seven minutes left, Notre Dame extended its lead to 37-20. North Carolina faces 5-0 Pitt next Saturday at Acrisure Stadium. It's the site of two of Belichick's AFC Championship wins, in 2001 and 2004 with the Patriots. The Tar Heels then play Duke, Syracuse, Miami, Connecticut, Louisville, Virginia, and NC State.
author: Mike Florio

title: Yale QB Dante Reno has big performance after his father (and former coach) dies
summary: Yale quarterback Dante Reno had a performance on Saturday he'll never forget, for many reasons.
full_text: Yale quarterback Dante Reno had a performance on Saturday he'll never forget, for many reasons. Reno threw for 298 yards and four touchdown passes in a come-from-behind win over Merrimack. The game happened one day after Yale announced the passing of former football head coach Tony Reno, who was Dante's father. "This one's for you pops," Dante Reno said on Twitter. Merrimack led Yale 21-7 in the second quarter. Fueled by Dante Reno's performance, the Bulldogs outscored Merrimack 34-3 to win the game. Tony Reno, who coached his son in 2025, stepped down in February 2026, citing health reasons. Tony Reno won the second-most games in Yale history, with 83. He coached Yale from 2012 through 2025, winning five Ivy League titles. "Dad, you are my role model, my best friend and my coach," Dante Reno wrote when his father stepped down. "I love you so much. The last 15 years you have been the best head coach I have ever seen. From your first year to playing with you last year, you have put your heart and soul into coaching. Your legacy will last forever." Tony Reno was 52 years old.
author: Mike Florio

title: Tyson Bagent is expected to start for the Bears on Sunday vs. Jets
summary: Case Keenum will take a seat on the bench, after beating the Eagles on Monday night.
full_text: The Bears are deferring to their depth chart. Despite Monday night's win by third-string quarterback Case Keenum over the Eagles, the Bears will apparently turn to second-stringer Tyson Bagent on Sunday against the Jets. Via Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Bagent is expected to start the game . Although the Bears have tried to keep the identity of the starter a secret , the signs have pointed to Bagent . He took the first-team reps during practice on Wednesday and Thursday — and possibly Friday. Coach Ben Johnson hasn't announced a starter for the Week 4 game. Does he need to? Bagent is listed as the backup to starter Caleb Williams. Bagent didn't play on Monday night, given that he was able to practice all week while in the concussion protocol. Keenum got the Week 3 start against the Eagles. With Bagent cleared, the Bears have decided not to ignore the preordained configuration of quarterbacks, even though Keenum managed to engineer a 27-7 win over the Eagles. Undrafted out of Shepherd, Bagent started four games in 2023, his rookie year. He has made eight appearances since then. Most recently, he replaced Williams in the fourth quarter of the Week 2 loss to the Vikings. Bagent nearly pulled off the victory.
author: Mike Florio

title: Patrick Mahomes looks to extend mastery of Raiders, AFC West
summary: When the Chiefs play in Las Vegas on Sunday, Kansas City quarterback Patrick Mahomes will be looking to extend his mastery of the Raiders — and of their division.
full_text: When the Chiefs play in Las Vegas on Sunday, Kansas City quarterback Patrick Mahomes will be looking to extend his mastery of the Raiders — and of their division. Via NBC Sports research, Mahomes has a career record of 13-2 against the Raiders. In those 15 games, Mahomes has thrown 36 touchdown passes against five interceptions. Mahomes is also 7-0 on the road against the Raiders, with 20 touchdown passes and two interceptions in those games. Against the AFC West, Mahomes has a record of 37-8. The 82.2 percent winning rate is the best for any quarterback since the merger against division rivals, based on a minimum of 25 starts. This year could be different. The Raiders are 3-0, as are the Chiefs. The winner will move to 4-0 and take early control of the division.
author: Mike Florio

title: Eagles elevate Zach Ertz, Josiah Deguara
summary: The Eagles added a pair of tight ends to the roster for Sunday's game against the Rams.
full_text: The Eagles added a pair of tight ends to the roster for Sunday's game against the Rams. Zach Ertz has been summoned from the practice squad for the second straight week. Ertz rejoined the Eagles last month and he caught one pass for nine yards in last Monday's loss to the Bears. They have also elevated Josiah Deguara. He also signed to the practice squad last month, but this is the first time he's been added to the active roster. Deguara and Ertz will help fill out a tight end group that's still without Dallas Goedert as he recovers from a knee injury. E.J. Jenkins and Johnny Mundt are the other tight ends for Philadelphia.
author: Josh Alper

title: Mack Hollins fined twice on the same play, losing $34,441
summary: The NFL fined Patriots receiver Mack Hollins $34,441 for his actions on the same play against the Jaguars.
full_text: '' The NFL fined Patriots receiver Mack Hollins $34,441 for his actions on the same play against the Jaguars. Hollins was docked $11,941 for taunting and $22,500 for unnecessary roughness involving his helmet. With 13:32 left in the fourth quarter, Hollins caught a 9-yard pass on third-and-10. Officials threw a flag for taunting after he gestured toward Jaguars safety Eric Murray. He was not penalized for illegal use of the helmet. Hollins led the Patriots with six catches for 87 yards. After a January 2025 game against the Broncos, the league fined him twice for taunting. He lost $11,255 for stepping over cornerback Patrick Surtain and $6,736 for standing over receiver Marvin Mims after a punt.
author: Charean Williams

title: Bucs elevate QB Easton Stick from practice squad
summary: The Buccaneers elevated linebacker Caden Fordham and quarterback Easton Stick from the practice squad for Sunday's game against the Packers, the team announced.
full_text: '' The Buccaneers elevated linebacker Caden Fordham and quarterback Easton Stick from the practice squad for Sunday's game against the Packers, the team announced. This is the first elevation for both Fordham and Stick. Stick will serve as the backup to rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels, who is set to make his NFL starting debut in place of Baker Mayfield. Mayfield will miss at least three weeks with a dislocated right thumb. Stick signed with the Buccaneers' practice squad on Aug. 31. Fordham signed with the Buccaneers as a rookie free agent in May and initially made the team's 53-player roster. The Bucs, though, waived him Sept. 2 after claiming cornerback Kevin Knowles off waivers from Kansas City. Fordham then signed back to the practice squad.
author: Charean Williams

title: Bears OT Braxton Jones lands on injured reserve
summary: The Bears are going to have a new left tackle for Sunday's game against the Jets and for several other games in the weeks to follow.
full_text: The Bears are going to have a new left tackle for Sunday's game against the Jets and for several other games in the weeks to follow. Braxton Jones was ruled out on Friday due to a knee injury and the Bears announced on Saturday that he has been placed on injured reserve. Theo Benedet will start against the Jets. Ozzy Trapilo could also factor into the left tackle plans while Jones is out of commission. Trapilo closed out last season as the starter and has been working his way back from a torn patellar tendon. The Bears also elevated defensive lineman Marcus Davenport and defensive back Nick McCloud from the practice squad on a temporary basis. They'll revert back after Sunday's game.
author: Josh Alper

title: 49ers elevate DE Matt Judon for Sunday's game
summary: Veteran defensive end Matt Judon is set for his 49ers debut.
full_text: '' Veteran defensive end Matt Judon is set for his 49ers debut. Judon signed to the team's practice squad on September 28 and the 49ers elevated him to the active roster for Sunday's game against the Broncos. He will revert back after the contest. Judon has 72 career sacks and the 49ers will look for him to help fill the void left by Nick Bosa's absence on the defensive line. The 49ers also elevated wide receiver Malik Turner as they wait to make a call on Mike Evans's availability for this week. Evans is dealing with a rib injury. In addition to those moves, the 49ers signed defensive lineman Sebastian Valdez off of the practice squad and waived defensive lineman Viliami Fehoko.
author: Josh Alper

title: Seahawks place RB Jadarian Price on IR
summary: Seahawks running back Jadarian Price not only will miss Sunday's game but at least the three games after that.
full_text: Seahawks running back Jadarian Price not only will miss Sunday's game but at least the three games after that. On Saturday, the Seahawks announced they placed Price on injured reserve with a chest injury. Price initially injured his chest in Week 2 before aggravating it in Wednesday's practice. The final pick of the first round started each of the team's first three games but has only 119 yards on 28 carries with two lost fumbles. He played 35.8 percent of offensive snaps while splitting time with Emanuel Wilson and George Holani. The Seahawks will get Zach Charbonnet back at some point, having opened his 21-day practice window this week. Seattle signed running back Velus Jones Jr. off the practice squad on Saturday. The Seahawks also elevated cornerback Trevon Diggs and safety Maxen Hook from the practice squad for Sunday's game.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jaylen Waddle was fined $14,926 for dice roll, too
summary: Do as we say, not as we profit from.
full_text: '' Do as we say, not as we profit from. Like Broncos guard Quinn Meinerz, who was fined $14,926 for a forbidden celebratory dice roll, Broncos receiver Jaylen Waddle was fined the same amount for the same celebration on the same play. The moment came after Waddle caught a third-quarter touchdown pass in Denver's eventual win over the Rams. The description of the infraction in the league's weekly announcement of fines is "[i]llegal celebrations and vulgar acts." It the latest example of the NFL's sudden return to its No-Fun-League ways. Indeed, the NFL had no issue with former Steelers receiver Martavis Bryant pretending to roll dice after scoring a touchdown in 2017 — and that was before the Supreme Court opened the floodgates for legalized sports betting and the NFL decided to abandon its loathing of gambling and open its arms to grab as much cash as it can. This season, the league is grabbing cash from players for doing things that used to be OK. Undoubtedly, the players will aggressively appeal. The only good news is that the fine money, if collected, goes to charity.
author: Mike Florio

title: Ravens put Jovaughn Gwyn, Ethan Pocic on IR
summary: The Ravens lost centers Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic to long-term injuries in last Sunday's win over the Ravens and both players were moved to the injured reserve list on Saturday.
full_text: The Ravens lost centers Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic to long-term injuries in last Sunday's win over the Ravens and both players were moved to the injured reserve list on Saturday. Gwyn fractured his fibula and Pocic hurt his knee after replacing him. Danny Pinter is also on injured reserve, so the team turned to first-round pick Vega Ioane last Sunday and he's expected to remain at the position for this Sunday's game against the Titans. Andrew Vorhees replaced Ioane at right guard against Dallas. The Ravens did not fill either roster spot, but they have elevated guard Kyle Hergel from the practice squad. Hergel signed with the Ravens this week and he played for offensive coordinator Declan Doyle in Chicago last season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Week 3 featured three fines for blindside blocks, two fines for hip-drop tackles
summary: The NFL's announcement of fines for Week 3 featured six infractions for player safety fouls that qualify toward possible suspensions.
full_text: '' The NFL's announcement of fines for Week 3 featured six infractions for player safety fouls that qualify toward possible suspensions. Two of those fouls were hip-drop tackles. 49ers linebacker Fred Warner and Rams safety Kam Curl were each fined $17,911. Warner was also fined $23,882 for illegal use of his helmet in a tackle. Texans linebacker Jamal Hill, Giants tight end Isaiah Likely, and Steelers linebacker Cole Holcomb were each fined for blindside blocks. Texans linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair was fined for a hit on a defenseless player. Any player with three fines for any one of those infractions will be suspended for one game. The same potential penalty applies to fouls for launching or horse-collar tackles. No player has been fined more than once for any of the qualifying infractions yet this season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Joey Porter Jr. will play for Cowboys, who elevate two DBs off practice squad
summary: The Cowboys elevated defensive backs Reddy Steward and Juanyeh Thomas from the practice squad to the active roster for Sunday's game against the Texans.
full_text: The Cowboys elevated defensive backs Reddy Steward and Juanyeh Thomas from the practice squad to the active roster for Sunday's game against the Texans. Thomas signed with the practice squad this week. The Cowboys will get help this week with the returns of safety Malik Hooker (forearm) and cornerback Shavon Revel (knee/ankle). Both players fully practiced on Friday and do not have an injury designation. In addition, new Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. will make his 2026 debut. Porter, who the Cowboys acquired from the Steelers this week, was not on the injury report and will play. Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones said on 105.3 The Fan on Friday that Porter "is going to get some snaps" against the Texans.
author: Charean Williams

title: Panthers put Xavier Legette on injured reserve
summary: Panthers wide receiver Xavier Legette missed last week's loss to the Browns with a knee injury and he'll miss several more games as well.
full_text: Panthers wide receiver Xavier Legette missed last week's loss to the Browns with a knee injury and he'll miss several more games as well. Legette was ruled out for Sunday night's home game against the Lions on Friday and the Panthers placed him on injured reserve on Saturday. Legette will have to miss at least four games before he'll be eligible to return to action. Legette was injured during a 55-yard catch in Carolina's Week 2 win over the Falcons. His only other catch on the season was a nine-yarder in the same game. The Panthers also announced that they have elevated wide receiver Ja'seem Reed and cornerback Robert Rochell from the practice squad. Reed provides depth with Legette out and Jalen Coker listed as questionable due to a quad injury. The Panthers placed both of their starting corners on injured reserve this week, which created the need to call Rochell up for Sunday night.
author: Josh Alper

title: Josh Harris doesn't rule out a permanent return of the spear to the Commanders helmet
summary: The Commanders have an alternate helmet that adds a spear to the W.
full_text: '' The Commanders have an alternate helmet that adds a spear to the W. Speaking to reporters on Saturday in London, Commanders owner Josh Harris didn't rule out making the spear a permanent part of the helmet. "Obviously, everyone is enjoying what we're doing, it's just embracing the past as much as we can in a respectful way, and we're gonna keep looking at, you know, how we keep doing that," Harris said, via John Keim of ESPN. "I like the spear. I mean, what can I say? You know, it brings everything together a little bit. It brings, you know, obviously, the special forces and Native Americans and the Roman gladiators, of course. So, I like the spear. And, you know, obviously, we had it on our helmet way back." It remains to be seen whether a revised logo will consist of the W with a spear in it, or just a spear. Regardless, the franchise continues to move toward the name and logo it abandoned in 2020. The only question is whether they'll eventually decide to bring back the name and/or the logo.
author: Mike Florio

title: Saints rule out Kaden Elliss, Carl Granderson for Monday night's game
summary: Linebacker Kaden Elliss moved from the Falcons to the Saints as a free agent this offseason, but he won't be playing against his former team on Monday night.
full_text: Linebacker Kaden Elliss moved from the Falcons to the Saints as a free agent this offseason, but he won't be playing against his former team on Monday night. Elliss was ruled out on Saturday after missing practice all week with a calf injury. Elliss, who spent three seasons with the Falcons after opening his career with the Saints, has 24 tackles this season. The Saints will be down two starting linebackers as they also ruled out Carl Granderson (ankle) and they could be missing a third. Pete Werner is questionable with a shoulder injury. Neither Granderson nor Werner practiced at all this week. Reserve linebacker Anfernee Jennings (knee) is also out and tight end Noah Fant (abdomen) joins Werner with a questionable tag.
author: Josh Alper

title: Falcons list Divine Deablo, Samson Ebukam as questionable for Monday night
summary: The Falcons have released their final injury report for Monday night's game in New Orleans and it includes three of the team's linebackers.
full_text: The Falcons have released their final injury report for Monday night's game in New Orleans and it includes three of the team's linebackers. Divine Deablo and Samson Ebukam were limited participants in practice all week and both of them have been listed as questionable to play against the Saints. Both players are dealing with hamstring injuries. Deablo has 11 tackles and a fumble recovery in three starts this season while Ebukam had three tackles and a half-sack in the first two weeks of the season. He did not play in last week's win over the Packers. Yasir Abdullah (illness) is also questionable. He was a full participant on Saturday.

title: Victor Wembanyama will "never" promote gambling
summary: One of the benefits of a no-travel Saturday is that it gives me a chance to revisit topics that flashed across the radar screen during a week of non-stop NFL news.
full_text: One of the benefits of a no-travel Saturday is that it gives me a chance to revisit topics that flashed across the radar screen during a week of non-stop NFL news. Here's something not from the NFL but highly relevant to it. At a time when many leagues (including the NFL), teams, players, and media organizations are gladly grabbing the bag of cash that comes from assisting in the normalization of gambling, San Antonio Spurs superstar Victor Wembanyama has drawn a clear line in the sand. Via Brandon Contes of Awful Announcing , Wembanyama was asked this week whether he'd ever accept a deal to promote gambling. “ Absolutely not ," he said. "I will never do that. Honestly, I think it’s very sad to see some players promote it, in my opinion. Everybody does whatever they want, but without me.” Wembanyama has many opportunities to convert his skyrocketing fame into money for nothing. He won't do it just to increase his net worth. “I’ve refused much much more money than I’ve made for things that were not to my values," Wembanyama said. "And now I want to promote things that have a good impact, have a good influence, with whom I can share messages with, and values. Obviously, we earn millions and millions, this is not our biggest strength. Our biggest strength is inspiring, and we can inspire in a good or a bad way. I want to inspire in a good way.” Yes, it's legal in most states to gamble with sportsbooks (and in all states to essentially gamble through prediction markets). But the proliferation of unregulated advertisements has enticed many young men who aren't yet able to figure out how it all works to think they can beat a system that is, in plenty of ways, rigged against them. Many of them dig a hole. When they realize their predicament, many of them keep digging. As I've said many times, gambling is fine as long as it's done with a clear understanding of how it works, and with a firm commitment to treat the money devoted to it as an entertainment expense. It's not a way to get rich. It's not a way to pay the bills. And we respect anyone who chooses not to shrug and say, "Everyone else is getting paid to promote gambling. Why shouldn't I?" For someone like Wembanyama, who could parlay his name, image, and likeness into a stack of cash nearly as tall as he is, the commitment to his values should be amplified, and admired.
author: Mike Florio

title: Vinod Khosla takes issues with reporters accurately quoting him, again
summary: New Seahawks owner missed the layup in his Axios interview. Then, he took to Twitter and missed it again.
full_text: It's time for another cleanup on Aisle 12. New Seahawks owner Vinod Khosla, who previously complained about the media focusing on his claim at his first press conference in August that he was and is a Steelers fan (and still watches all of their games), now takes issue with the reasonable reaction to on-the-record quotes he recently gave to Axios . "To all @Seahawks fans and @12s," Khosla said on Twitter, "we have no plans to move the team, have never discussed it, haven’t even thought about it. End of story. I've said repeatedly we have no plans to change anything. Feel sad for the reporters looking for views and clicks who distort my answer out of context and sent an entire city into a spiral for no reason." Where's the distortion? He gave a quote. The quote was noticed, given its obvious implication. And the quote was repeated. That's how this entire business works. Here’s the question that Khosla was asked by Axios : "You've talked about being a steward of the Seahawks and preserving what Paul Allen built. But I don't think you've formally committed to keeping the team in Seattle long-term. Will you make that commitment?" Here's his response: "I will never say never. Will this team be in Seattle 500 years from now? But I have no current plans to change anything about the team, including the coach, president, operation or Lumen Field. It all functions well." Khosla chose the words he uttered. He could have said, "The team will never move as long as I own it." He's smart enough to know that would have harmed his leverage to get as much free money as possible when it's time to renovate or to replace Lumen Field. And that's fine. Still, he can't have it both ways. But it's not his fault for saying it. It's our fault for saying that he said it. On top of all of that, he had yet another chance to say, "The team will never move as long as I own it." Instead, he said in his tweet, "We have no plans to move the team." Plans change, all the time. Hiding behind the phrase "no plans" creates flexibility to devise a different plan later. Frankly, the city was "sent into a spiral" because Khosla missed the layup. And then went back to the line, dribbled to the hoop, and missed it again. Khosla also told Axios that "he know[s] very little about running a team." We'll add this, with all due deference and respect: And it shows.
author: Mike Florio

title: Vikings close in on record for consecutive four-sack games
summary: The Vikings have won eight games in a row (3-0 this season) thanks to a defense that has at times been dominant.
full_text: The Vikings have won eight games in a row (3-0 this season) thanks to a defense that has at times been dominant. It has consistently been getting to the quarterback before he can throw the ball. Via NBC Sports research, Minnesota's six-game streak of four or more sacks is two short of the all-time record. The Colts set it in 1975, with eight straight games of four-or-more sacks. Three teams have done it seven games in a row: the 1986 Broncos, the 1969 Lions, and the 1963 Giants. The current streak is the longest since the Giants did it in 2001. The Vikings lead the NFL with 14 sacks. Dallas Turner has 3.5.
author: Mike Florio

title: Derrick Henry, Josh Allen chase a record rushing TD start
summary: Both Ravens running back Derrick Henry and Bills quarterback Josh Allen have scored six rushing touchdowns through three games.
full_text: Both Ravens running back Derrick Henry and Bills quarterback Josh Allen have scored six rushing touchdowns through three games. Via NBC Sports research, they each have a chance to tie the record for the most rushing touchdowns through the first four games of a season. The current mark is nine, shared by Hall of Famer Jim Brown (1958), Hall of Famer Emmitt Smith (1995), and Stephen Davis (1999). So it's three to tie, and four to beat the record. Henry's opportunity comes in his first game against his former teams, the Titans. Allen's comes in the first home game in the new Buffalo stadium against their biggest rivals, the Patriots. If Henry scores at least two, he'll take over fourth place on the list of all-time games with multiple touchdowns. He's tied with Hall of Famer Randy Moss at 37 such games. Smith had 39, Hall of Famer LaDanian Tomlinson had 44, and Hall of Famer Jerry Rice had 46. A pair of rushing touchdowns also would allow Henry to match Hall of Famer Marshall Faulk (Colts and Rams) and Hall of Famer Marcus Allen (Raiders and Chiefs) with 40 or more rushing touchdowns with multiple teams. There are a lot of Hall of Famers mentioned in this blurb. Inevitably, Henry and Allen will have that distinction attached to their names, too.
author: Mike Florio

title: Dolphins sign RB Carlos Washington, elevate DL Mazi Smith
summary: The Dolphins have added a running back to their active roster.
full_text: The Dolphins have added a running back to their active roster. They announced the signing of Carlos Washington off of the practice squad on Saturday. Washington will flesh out a backfield that lost De'Von Achane for the season to a torn ACL. Washington played in two games for the Falcons over the last two seasons. He signed with the Dolphins in May. The Dolphins also announced that they have elevated defensive lineman Mazi Smith and defensive end Rodney McGraw for Sunday's game against the Vikings. Smith was a 2023 Cowboys first-round pick and he signed with the Dolphins last month. McGraw signed with the Dolphins after going undrafted this year.

title: Bengals vs. Jaguars prediction: Joe Burrow, Trevor Lawrence duel in battle of AFC contenders
summary: Everything you need to know to tune into the AFC showdown
full_text:
The Jacksonville Jaguars and Cincinnati Bengals are both 2-1 and meeting in an AFC clash at Paycor Stadium.
The Bengals are coming off a 30-27 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers that went right to the very end, while the Jaguars are coming off a dominant 35-6 victory over the shaky New England Patriots . The Jaguars' lone loss came in Week 2, a 20-13 defeat to the Denver Broncos .
While the Bengals' record shows a solid start, the teams they beat (Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Houston Texans) are 0-6. Facing the Jaguars will be a good temperature check to see where they rank among early AFC contenders.
Cincinnati has the challenge of playing in a division with the 3-1 Cleveland Browns ( who might just be good ), 2-1 Baltimore Ravens and the Pittsburgh Steelers, who sit at .500 but came a few plays away from 3-1. Jacksonville, on the other hand, is the only AFC South team with a winning record. It shares the division with 1-2 Indianapolis and the winless Tennessee Titans and Houston Texans.
It's early in the season, but these two teams have real playoff possibilities, and this game could prove to be very meaningful when the postseason comes around, whether that's for getting in or for seeding.
Date: Sunday, Oct. 4 | Time: 1 p.m. ET Location: Paycor Stadium (Cincinnati, OH) TV: CBS | Stream: Paramount+ Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bengals -2.5 ( via DraftKings )
Bengals defense: Cincinnati's defense was by far its weak spot last season, but this year the unit has improved a lot — except for last week. It had its worst showing of the season in the loss and needs to step it up this week against a Jaguars offense that seems to be building confidence by the week.
Jags defense vs. Chase, Higgins: Tee Higgins ranks ninth in receiving yards through three games (244), while Chase ranks 27th (185). The Jaguars defense allowed Jaylen Waddle to have a 100-yard game last week and have a challenge ahead of them to stop the WR duo. Jacksonville did a good job shutting down Patriots receivers last week, only allowing 178 passing yards and no touchdowns. Plus, they stopped all three red zone tries.
Burrow vs. Lawrence by the numbers: Burrow has a 70.9 completion percentage (sixth most), 743 yards (12th most ), six touchdowns, one interception and seven sacks taken. Lawrence has a 66.7 completion percentage, 616 yards, seven touchdowns, two interceptions and four sacks taken. The Jaguars could work on their passing game, but they have a stronger run game than their Week 4 opponent. Both quarterbacks are playing at a high level so far, so this battle should be a fun one to watch. These two have a history as well. They faced each other in the 2020 National Championship, when Burrow's LSU defeated Lawrence's Clemson.
I think this one could be close, but I think the Jaguars will take it. They look like one of the teams to beat in the AFC, and I think they will continue their winning streak against the Bengals.

The Falcons impressed last Thursday in blowing out Green Bay on the road. Getting Michael Penix back at quarterback matters. They will continue to give it to Bijan Robinson in this one. The Saints will get theirs behind Tyler Shough . It's high scoring, and the Falcons will win it.
Pick: Falcons 33, Saints 30
Can you believe this is a big game in the AFC North? Both teams are 2-1 and the Browns are one of the surprise teams so far. The Steelers looked good last week, beating the Bengals , but the Browns have played well against them in Cleveland. Upset special. Browns get to 3-1.
Pick: Browns 21, Steelers 20

title: Last-minute best bets for NFL Week 4: Cowboys welcome Joey Porter Jr. with upset win, Rams edge out Eagles
summary: Why the Rams, Packers, Cowboys, Seahawks and Vikings are the five teams to back in Week 4
full_text:
The NFL is coming off one of its craziest weeks in recent memory, as Week 3 tied a league record for the number of one-score games. Judging by the Cleveland Browns upset win over the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday, Week 4 promises to continue the madness as we flip the calendar to October and close out the first month of the regular season.
Of course, between work, daily chores, and craziness that is life, it's hard to keep pace with all that's happening across the NFL. For instance, you might not have realized that a massive trade popped up midweek, in which the Cowboys acquired standout corner Joey Porter Jr . from the Steelers. Or, from a scheduling standpoint, we have early morning football on Sunday, with the Commanders and Colts kicking off from London.
So, as you get ready for another Sunday of full-fledged NFL action, we want you to be as informed as possible before you line up any wagers you may make. With that in mind, here's a look at some last-minute Week 4 picks, including five best bets.
NFL odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook.
Both clubs enter Week 4 after rather demoralizing losses on the road. Case Keenum sliced Philly up on "Monday Night Football," and they now have to turn around and square off against the Matthew Stafford-led Rams on a short week. Meanwhile, L.A. lost a heartbreaker in Denver, which dropped the preseason "superteam" to 1-2 through the first three weeks. Each of these teams has yet to live up to their lofty expectations so far this year, but I think the Rams are in a better spot to pull off the win here, especially with the return of wideout Puka Nacua .
At first glance, you might be eager to take the Eagles as a home dog, but they've historically not been kind to bettors in this setting. Since 2021 (Sirianni's first season as head coach), Philadelphia is 0-5 straight up (1-4 ATS) as a home underdog.
When watching them this season, it's clear their offense is still a work in progress. The Eagles have yet to score in the first quarter this season (the only team in the NFL yet to score) and have the highest three-and-out rate (29%) since 2025. When you pair that with a defense that has yet to generate a turnover and has registered just three sacks, there's an opportunity for the Rams to get out to an early lead and never look back. As we saw on Monday night, when you get the Eagles into a pass-heavy game script, it's not exactly "The Greatest Show on Turf," and they'll try to win in Week 4 without top wideout DeVonta Smith (hamstring).
Projected score : Rams 26, Eagles 20 The pick : Rams -3.5
It's a make-or-break game for each of these NFC squads, but I'd argue it's most important for the Packers . Sure, the Bucs are teetering with a 0-3 record and just lost Baker Mayfield (thumb) for the next few weeks, but a loss here would be a straight-up embarrassment for Green Bay. I don't care if the offensive line has any many holes as a Cheesehead, if the Packers can't beat a Baker-less Bucs team that'll be quarterbacked by undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels , the entire operation needs to be in question. Jordan Love has struggled this season with the second-highest off-target rate (19.4%) and second-lowest completion percentage (52.4%) in the NFL. However, he's also been under siege quite a bit, facing the third-highest amount of pressure (44.7%). The offensive line for the Packers is still a massive question, but Love might get a little more time in the pocket this week with the Bucs logging the second-lowest pressure rate (28.3%) in the league. Tampa Bay is also on a 12-game coverless streak, which is the longest ATS losing streak since 1970.
Projected score : Packers 27, Buccaneers 20 The pick : Packers -3.5
The Texans are 0-3 for the second year in a row, and I don't believe they'll resurrect themselves as they did in 2025. Houston's offensive line remains a monumental weakness, and it's affecting all facets of the offense. In pass protection, they're allowing the third-most pressures (52) and are tied for the second-most sacks (10) allowed. On the ground, the Texans average just 3.6 yards per carry, which is tied for the fifth-lowest in the NFL. Their 2.15 yards after contact per rush are the second-lowest.
So, while the Cowboys ' defense has remained abysmal, they might actually find some success against the Texans' defense. That's particularly true if Dallas' offense continues to put points on the board. This season, the Cowboys have the highest drive-scoring rate (61.5%) in the league. If Dak Prescott and company build up a lead, C.J. Stroud will be forced to pass and test newly acquired corner Joey Porter Jr., who appears set to make his debut following this week's trade.
Meanwhile, I also wonder how much of a home-field advantage Reliant Stadium will be and how many Dallas fans will make the trip to Houston/already be in the area.
Projected score : Cowboys 27, Texans 23 The pick : Cowboys +3
We're going back to the well and laying a touchdown with the Seahawks against an inferior team. It burned us last week against Marcus Mariota and the Commanders, but it doesn't change the logic. Seattle is arguably the best team in the NFL, and they just got their Super Bowl-winning quarterback back. Sure, he threw two interceptions (including a pick-six), but Sam Darnold also completed 31 of 45 for 379 yards and four passing touchdowns. At home, I think we get a much cleaner and more prolific showing from him.
Even if he does turn it over again, these Chargers have shown us that they can still lose despite winning the turnover battle. They are +4 over the Bills in turnover margin and still found a way to lose. Los Angeles looks absolutely lost as an organization, especially on offense where they are averaging 14.7 points per game (fourth-fewest in the NFL). I don't expect the unit to suddenly revive itself against a Mike Macdonald-led defense that is allowing the third-fewest points per game (16.7) and fewest total yards per game (228.7).
Projected score : Seahawks 33, Chargers 20 The pick : Seahawks -7
To put it delicately, it's been a rough go of it for the Dolphins . We knew they weren't going to be competitive this season, but after watching them through the first three weeks, it stands to reason they won't even win a game in 2026. To make matters worse, they just lost star running back De'Von Achane , their most prolific offensive player.
Now, a bad offense gets even worse and faces Brian Flores' defense. Flores, who currently serves as Minnesota's defensive coordinator, was the head coach of the Dolphins for three seasons (2019-2021) before being fired. Surely, he'd like to stick it to his former team and will do so by continuing to blitz the quarterback. The Vikings have the highest blitz rate (71%) in the NFL. That'll be quite the mismatch for a Miami team that is tied for the third-most sacks allowed (9). Sure, Minnesota won't have No.1 receiver Justin Jefferson (ankle) for this game, but it might not matter with Flores pulling the levers on defense.
The overall trends look favorable for a Vikings win/cover as well. Miami is 0-3 ATS this season and was a double-digit underdog in all of those prior contests. Meanwhile, Minnesota is 8-0 straight-up and 7-1 ATS over its last eight games. This feels like a blowout.
Projected score : Vikings 27, Dolphins 10 The pick : Vikings -10.5

Cardinals at Giants Projected score : Cardinals 27, Giants 23 The pick : Cardinals -2.5

Jets at Bears Projected score : Bears 27, Jets 24 The pick : Jets +3.5
Titans at Ravens Projected score : Ravens 33, Titans 16 The pick : Ravens -11.5
Broncos at 49ers Projected score : Broncos 23, 49ers 21 The pick : Broncos +3

title: Panthers vs. Lions prediction: Explosive offenses poised for potential 'Sunday Night Football' shootout
summary: Injury-riddled defenses will have trouble getting off the field in this clash between high-scoring squads
full_text:
Fans of offense should be in for a treat when the Carolina Panthers host the Detroit Lions on "Sunday Night Football." The Week 4 clash pits two high-flying offenses against defenses that struggled to stop anyone through their first three games. Bryce Young is turning into a standout quarterback in real time, and the Lions feature the best wide receiver-running back tandem in the NFL with Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown . Points ought not to be hard to come by in this primetime battle.
Detroit scored exactly 31 points in all of its games thus far and came away with a pair of victories. The Panthers were off to a similarly prolific start but hit an unforeseen road block a week ago with their 21-18 loss at the Cleveland Browns . This is a difficult spot to find a bounce back, but Dave Canales' team upset two playoff teams a year ago and are built to hang with the league's third-highest-scoring squad.
With a win, the Lions would remain within close striking distance of the NFC North lead. The Panthers need a victory to avoid falling into a 1-3 hole and slipping behind in an NFC South that should be up for grabs until season's end.
Carolina will have no answers for Amon-Ra St. Brown without its top two cornerbacks, and Jahmyr Gibbs has never seen a defense he cannot torch. And on the other side of the ball, the Lions own a beleaguered secondary of their own, and there is no reason to believe the league's worst pass defense will keep Bryce Young in check — especially if wide receiver Jalen Coker returns to the lineup. The Panthers posted 37 points in their Week 1 home shootout with the Chicago Bears and could outdo that number against an even leakier defense. In a game where one stop might be the difference, the home team holds the edge.
Pick: Panthers 38, Lions 34
author: Carter Bahns

title: NFL Week 4 player prop bets: Raiders' Brock Bowers among best anytime TD bets
summary: These five players could capitalize on their matchups and find the end zone during Sunday's NFL action
full_text:
This Sunday in the NFL , the Indianapolis Colts and Washington Commanders will battle in London, we have a Texas-sized showdown in Houston between the Texans and the Dallas Cowboys , plus Trevor Lawrence and Joe Burrow face off in Cincinnati. Oh, and Derrick Henry will look to run all over his former team in the Tennessee Titans . That's a must-watch revenge game.
Let's discuss some anytime touchdown bets. These have become popular wagers among football fans because of their longer odds. Even when it comes to an expected TD scorer, they make for a fun parlay leg. Last week, we hit on Tee Higgins at +175 and tight end Harold Fannin Jr . at +235. Let's see what we have cooking up for Week 4.
Below, we will break down five anytime TD bets to consider. These will not be predictable choices like a Jahmyr Gibbs or Bijan Robinson score that offer zero value, but they won't be wild long shots such as a team defense. Let's begin with a tight end who looked incredible last week in his 2026 debut.
Odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook.
The Las Vegas Raiders have a massive matchup against Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs this week. The Raiders are off to a surprising 3-0 start, although we can't ignore the fact that they've played the easiest strength of schedule in the NFL up to this point, as their first three opponents have won one game combined.
Raiders star tight end Brock Bowers made his season debut last week against the New Orleans Saints , and he looked magnificent. He caught a game-high 10 passes for 116 yards and a touchdown in a 35-27 win, and will be important if the Raiders want to score an upset victory over their rivals. With how good Bowers looked last week, I'll sprinkle on him again in this spot as Kirk Cousins ' new clear-cut "WR1."
James Cook of the Buffalo Bills is one of the best running backs in the NFL, and he's on a bit of a heater right now. He rushed 21 times for 135 yards and a touchdown in Week 2 vs. the Detroit Lions , and then 24 times for 154 yards and another touchdown last week against the Los Angeles Chargers .
Now, the flailing New England Patriots come to town, and they are missing two important defenders in Christian Barmore and Christian Gonzalez . They lost by 29 points to the Jacksonville Jaguars last week, and I'm sure Joe Brady and the Bills want to do something similar to the team that won their division last year. A -140 price isn't value, but I can tell you I was surprised by this listing.
Like James Cook, this line doesn't offer much value. But consider that the Miami Dolphins have allowed six touchdowns to running backs through three games. The Minnesota Vikings are favored by double-digits over Miami, which makes sense because the Dolphins just lost De'Von Achane for the year, while Brian Flores is going to look to DESTROY his former team from a defensive standpoint. That means Aaron Jones is going to get plenty of touches. He hasn't scored since Week 1, but will in Week 4.
I was a fan of Braelon Allen in the 2024 draft process because he's big at 6-foot-1, 235 pounds, and was the youngest player in the entire class. He actually racked up 482 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns as a rookie, but an injury held him to four games played last year. Now, he's making his third career start with Breece Hall sidelined by a quad injury.
When the New York Jets get in the red zone against the Chicago Bears , Frank Reich is going to call his number.
This game is on Monday night, but I had to mention it. The Saints are hosting the Atlanta Falcons in the 20th anniversary of the "Rebirth Game," where the Saints returned to the Superdome for the first time following Hurricane Katrina. The legendary Steve Gleason blocked a punt on the opening drive of the game, which set the tone for an emotional 23-3 Saints victory. I can't imagine what the environment will be like on Monday night.
Travis Etienne is out with a hamstring injury, opening the door for franchise legend Alvin Kamara . He's not as productive as he used to be, but it makes too much sense for him to score in this game.
Derrick Henry faces the team that selected him No. 45 overall in the 2016 NFL Draft this Sunday. Henry and the Titans didn't have some dramatic breakup, but Henry wanted to win football games and the Titans were about to suffer an embarrassing fall to the bottom of the league, so a mutual parting of ways made sense.
It used to be a debate if Henry was a future Hall of Famer. Not anymore. The ageless wonder leads the NFL with 3,817 rushing yards and 38 rushing touchdowns since signing with the Baltimore Ravens in 2024. Those are more rushing yards and more rushing touchdowns than the entire Titans offense since he left.
Derrick Henry to find the end zone at -210 is probably a parlay leg, but what about two touchdowns at +250? He's averaging two touchdowns a game this year as it is!
author: Jordan Dajani

title: NFL Week 4 picks and score predictions: Texans get first win, Bengals edge Jaguars
summary: Here's your weekly dose of John Breech's NFL picks
full_text:
I'm not saying the NFL should cancel Week 4, but Roger Goodell might at least want to think about postponing it a few days so we all have time to recover from the craziness of Week 3. There were 12 games decided by one score, which was tied for the most of any week ever in NFL history.
There were some highs in Week 3, there were some lows, and then there was whatever the Packers did in that Thursday night game against the Falcons. I would say it was the worst performance of the week, but then the Eagles showed up on Monday night and got torched by a third-string quarterback in Case Keenum. In related news, Case Keenum now has more TD passes (2) on the year than Drake Maye.
If you didn't know that Keenum was still in the NFL, don't worry, I think that describes almost everyone. Speaking of everyone, I would now like to share my picks with everyone, so let's get to them.
Actually, before we get to the picks, here's a quick reminder that you can check out the weekly picks from every CBSSports.com NFL expert by clicking here , but you were probably already well aware of that since I mention it every week.
One thing that I don't mention every week is that I also write an NFL newsletter for CBS Sports and if you want so subscribe to it, you just need to go here and enter your email . If you sign up, you'll be getting an email to your inbox twice a week that will be full of football news and maybe some cat photos.
Alright, I'm going to stop begging you to sign up for things so that we can get to the picks.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
I never thought I would say this about the Cleveland Browns, but they might be the most underrated team in the NFL. Two months ago, we were all laughing at their QB battle, but now, Todd Monken is laughing at us. And if he's not, he should be, because the QB he gave the job to has the Browns TIED FOR FIRST IN THE AFC NORTH heading into Week 4.
I can't remember the last time I used the words "Browns" and "First place" in the same sentence, but I have to think it was before COVID. I can't be sure, because I don't really remember anything before COVID. Any time the Browns are in first place, even if it's early in the season, it's still worth mentioning, because this team hasn't won a division title since 1989.
Do you know who was born in 1989? Taylor Swift. Do you know who once sang the national anthem at a Steelers game? Taylor Swift. And the Steelers lost that day ... you know what, I have no idea where I was going with that point, so let's move on.
On paper, the Steelers feel like the better team in this game, but I haven't used paper in three years, so I'm not sure that fact actually means anything to me.
When I'm trying to make a pick in a Steeles-Browns game, the only thing I care about are trends, and there are two trends telling me to pick the Browns to win.
First, the Steelers are possibly the worst Thursday night road team the NFL has ever seen. If the Steelers had to play 17 Thursday road games, they would go 0-17. Since the AFL-NFL merger in 1970, the Steelers are 3-16 in Thursday road games, and it actually gets worse: They're 0-9 in divisional road games that are played on a Thursday.
They had a chance to end the streak in 2024 with a game in Cleveland against the 2-8 Browns, but they lost. They had a chance to end the streak in 2025 with a game against JOE FLACCO, but they lost to the Bengals. Flacco had only been on the Bengals' roster for nine days when he faced the Steelers and he still managed to throw for 342 yards and three touchdowns in a Bengals win.
The Thursday road losing streak against divisional opponents started in 1980 with a loss to the Houston Oilers, and it's now been going on for 46 years. This streak has been going on for so long that the Steelers have played two divisional games against opponents who aren't even in their division anymore (Jaguars and Oilers/Titans).
The other trend here is that the city of Cleveland has basically been a black hole for the Steelers. It's like they forget how to play football whenever they have to make the trip to Northern Ohio. The Browns have somehow won four straight home games against Pittsburgh.
And now, the Steelers have to send out their 42-year-old quarterback to start a game on just three days rest. If there's one thing no 42-year-old ever wants to do, it's play two NFL games in five days. I'm taking the BROWNS in an upset.
PICK: Browns (+2.5) 19-16 over Steelers
Sunday, 1 p.m. ET (Fox, Stream: Fubo -- try for free))
Jerry Jones might have a lot of friends in the NFL, but apparently, he's not friends with anyone in the NFL scheduling department, because that's the only way to explain what the Cowboys are dealing with this week.
The Cowboys spent Week 3 in Rio de Janeiro, which meant they had to fly 10 hours to South America and then 10 hours back. The one-way trip to Rio covered more than 5,200 miles. Every team that has ever had to fly that far for a game got a bye or extra rest the following week, but not the Cowboys. That's right: The Cowboys are the FIRST team in NFL history to fly at least 5,000 miles for a game and not get any extra rest for their next game. Not only do the Cowboys have to play in Week 4 without any extra rest, but they have to play ON THE ROAD.
Before this year, the NFL had held two games in Brazil and both of those games were played on a Friday. That gave the teams involved two extra days of rest before playing their next game, but the Cowboys won't be getting that.
Here's what Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer had to say about the schedule last week, "The schedule is the schedule, and we will play anybody anytime, anywhere, but it's a unique schedule for sure."
When an NFL coach uses the word "unique" in a situation like this, you can easily read between the lines. I think what Schottenheimer was trying to say is "It's a dumb schedule and I can't believe the NFL did this to us," but instead, he chose his words carefully.
And just in case you're wondering, the Ravens are in a similar situation, but not really. They're getting the Titans at HOME for their post-Brazil matchup. That seems slightly easier than a road game against the Texans.
The Texans are going to be desperate and they're going to be facing a tired Cowboys team that's going to be emotionally exhausted after losing a heartbreaker to the Ravens. Before this week, only two teams had to travel at least 4,400 miles for a game without getting any extra rest the following week: 2021 Dolphins and 2025 Broncos, who both went to London.
How did things go for those two teams after their long trips? With 11 minutes left in the fourth quarter, the Dolphins trailed their game 27-14 while the Broncos trailed 26-8. This means the two teams got outscored a combined 53-22 for the first 49 minutes of each game. That doesn't sound like good news for the Cowboys.
In the post-Brazil special, I fully expect the Cowboys to struggle in the first half before bouncing back in the second half only to lose. That seems like the most Cowboys thing possible that could happen this week.
PICK: Texans (-2.5) 23-20 over Cowboys
Sunday, 1 p.m. ET (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ )
You may not have noticed because it's the Jaguars and nobody ever seems to notice what they're doing, but Liam Coen is quietly building an unstoppable juggernaut in Jacksonville. The Jaguars have won 10 of their past 11 regular-season games, and those 10 wins have come by an average of 20.6 points per game.
The Jaguars are beating people so badly that Trevor Lawrence is regularly being benched well before the game is over.
Trevor Lawrence has been pulled early in seven of the #Jaguars last 11 games. Here’s how much time was remaining in each. - 4th Quarter (8:07) vs #Chargers - 4th Quarter (6:05) vs #Titans - 4th Quarter (7:08) vs #Colts - 4th Quarter (13:51) vs #Jets - 4th Quarter (13:17) vs…
If you have Trevor Lawrence in fantasy, you should probably just get rid of him since he doesn't even play the entire game…
author: John Breech

title: NFL Week 4 picks: Our experts face off on Cowboys vs. Texans, Rams at Eagles and more
summary: CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games
full_text:
Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season has plenty of storylines to watch. Derrick Henry is looking to run wild against his former team in the Tennessee Titans; the Indianapolis Colts and Washington Commanders battle from London; and Matthew Stafford and the Los Angeles Rams look to get back on track vs. the Philadelphia Eagles .
This season has been pretty unpredictable so far. Four teams enter Week 4 tied for the best record in their division after last-place finishes in 2025: The Las Vegas Raiders , Cleveland Browns , New York Giants and the New Orleans Saints . Which one of these teams could be a legitimate sleeper? And when could we see J.J. McCarthy take over at quarterback in New York?
Below, CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Sept. 29 over at DraftKings Sportsbook.
Advanced data courtesy of CBS Sports Research
Dajani (Colts -3.5): I think this matchup is about which defense stinks less. The Colts rank worst in total defense (417.3) and third-worst in scoring defense (30.3). The Commanders rank second-worst in scoring defense (30.7) and have allowed the highest opponent passer rating (124.4) and most passing touchdowns (11) this year. Marcus Mariota has definitely brought some magic to the lineup, as evidenced by last week's upset of the Seattle Seahawks , but I would argue the Colts are the better team.
Do you remember the last time the Colts played overseas? They defeated the Atlanta Falcons in overtime thanks to a ridiculous performance from Jonathan Taylor . The star running back rushed 32 times for 244 yards and three touchdowns, while also adding 42 yards as a receiver. He's already up to 325 total yards and four touchdowns through three weeks. I expect him to show out on Sunday for our friends across the pond.  … Prediction: Colts 27, Commanders 21
Dubin (Commanders +3.5): Marcus Mariota is a competent enough backup quarterback to keep this game close. He just went and beat the Seahawks, after all, and the Colts have a much friendlier defense. He should be able to keep the chains moving. I'm just not sure that'll be enough for the Commanders to actually win the game this time around. I think this is a big Jonathan Taylor game, even if Washington has been good on the ground so far and allowed just 44 rushing yards last week against Seattle. Plus. Washington's pass defense should give Daniel Jones and Co. a chance for their best game to date. … Prediction: Colts 23, Commanders 20
Dajani (Bengals -2.5): The Jacksonville Jaguars have been red-hot and just defeated the New England Patriots by a whopping 29 points. As for the Bengals, they just lost to Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers in a thrilling game. We thought the Cincy defense was reborn, only for Rodgers and Co. to drop 30 points on them. This is going to be a popular "upset" pick this week, but I'm actually going to take the Bengals. They are back at home after two road games and have covered the spread in six straight non-divisional contests. This Jaguars team isn't perfect, and you saw some issues during their Week 2 loss to the Denver Broncos . The offensive line could struggle with Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen , while this secondary will have their hands full with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . Don't overlook the fact that Joe Burrow is 3-0 vs. Trevor Lawrence dating back to the 2019 College Football Playoff Title game. … Prediction: Bengals 24, Jaguars 20
Dubin (Jaguars +2.5): I hate to be the guy that takes what Dajani described as the popular upset pick right after he called people out for it, but I'm going to do just that. The Jaguars should be 3-0 right now, but they fell apart in the second half against the Broncos in Week 2. The offense is firing on all cylinders. The defense has forced six turnovers in three games. Cincinnati's defensive improvement looked like a mirage in Week 3 against the Steelers and may have just been a function of playing dysfunctional offenses in the Buccaneers and the Nico Collins-less Texans . I think Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins can put up some points here, but I like the Jags to score even more.  … Prediction: Jaguars 30, Bengals 27
Dajani (Rams -3): The Eagles' loss to the Chicago Bears may stay with me forever. We had a 38-year-old quarterback dicing up a Super Bowl-caliber defense, as Ben Johnson put Vic Fangio in a proverbial chokehold on national television. Then, we had a former Super Bowl MVP quarterback looking completely lost. All that to say, how am I supposed to back Philly in this spot against an angry team that just lost in primetime?
If we are being honest with ourselves, the Eagles haven't looked very good at all this year. They were hardly dominant in the Week 1 victory over the Commanders or Week 2 win against the Titans. Philly is the only team that hasn't scored in the first quarter this season, and the defense is still waiting to force that first takeaway. The Eagles haven't even covered the spread this season, so I'll take the visiting Rams to get back on track.  … Prediction: Rams 26, Eagles 20
Dubin (Rams -3): The Rams have looked like the Rams we expected for six quarters this season, and very much like a different team for the other six quarters. Meanwhile, the Eagles have looked exactly like the Eagles we expected for eight quarters and like a disaster for four. How does that all net out? I think it nets out with Matthew Stafford having some success through the air against a somewhat surprisingly friendly Eagles pass defense that isn't getting as much pressure as you'd expect, and with Jalen Hurts and Co. continuing their stilted start to the season.  … Prediction: Rams 24, Eagles 20
Dajani (Texans -2.5): I've given the Texans the benefit of the doubt for an entire month with nothing to show for it. I can no longer wait for C.J. Stroud to get the offense off the ground or for the defense to become good again. With that said, there is one big reason why the Texans will get their first win this season, and that's Nico Collins . He's missed the past two games with a hamstring injury, but should return this week to face one of the worst defenses in the NFL. C.J. Stroud averages 10.7 yards per attempt when targeting Collins. That number drops to 7.7 when he targets any other receiver. In the one game Collins played in this season, he caught seven passes for 75 yards and a touchdown while Houston came one play away from defeating the Buffalo Bills … Prediction: Texans 30, Cowboys 26
Dubin (Texans -2.5): The Cowboys need their offense to be perfect in order to win games. Their defense once again seems like it's that bad, and it is also hemorrhaging players at linebacker and in the secondary. Offenses, generally, cannot be perfect against the Texans' defense. Houston should also be getting Nico Collins back here, so I think the Texans can actually move the ball for a change. … Prediction: Texans 24, Cowboys 21
Dajani (Broncos +3): Maybe I'm the Broncos expert? When Denver was down 16-0 to the Rams last Sunday night, I was telling everyone not to go to bed because the game was not over. Sure enough, the Broncos bucked back. Denver has the most comeback wins (14), second-half comebacks (11), fourth-quarter comebacks (7) and 14-point comebacks (3) over the past two seasons.
I'm leaning toward the Broncos again in this spot because of the San Francisco 49ers ' injuries. Nick Bosa is going to miss some time with knee/calf issues, wide receiver Mike Evans injured his rib, linebacker Dre Greenlaw sat out of practice Wednesday with a quad injury and we'll see what the status of left tackle Trent Williams is later in the week. Denver is 5-1 straight up in its last six games as an underdog, and Bo Nix is 10-0 in his past 10 games vs. NFC opponents.  … Prediction: Broncos 24, 49ers 23
Dubin (49ers -3): San Francisco is merrily rolling right along with the best offense in the NFL through the first three weeks despite…
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Seahawks place rookie Jadarian Price on injured reserve
summary: The rookie aggravated a chest injury and will miss at least four games, leaving Emanuel Wilson and George Holani to shoulder backfield duties during a grueling stretch
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks will have to move forward without their top running back for at least four weeks, as the team has placed rookie running back Jadarian Price on injured reserve. ESPN reports that Price aggravated the chest injury suffered in Week 2 vs. the Arizona Cardinals .
Price suited up for Seattle's Week 3 loss against the Washington Commanders , in which he rushed five times for 15 yards. He was listed as a limited participant in practice on Wednesday, but missed Thursday's and Friday's sessions, and was subsequently ruled out for Sunday's matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers .
Price is the Seahawks' leading rusher this season, having rushed 28 times for 119 yards. With him out of the lineup, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani will take over as Sam Darnold's partners in the backfield.
vs. Kansas City Chiefs (SNF)
Seattle did designate running back Zach Charbonnet to return to practice this week, as he continues to ramp up after tearing his ACL in the divisional-round win over the rival 49ers last year. It opened up a 21-day window where he can practice without actually counting towards the 53-man roster. Charbonnet rushed for a career-high 730 yards and 12 touchdowns last season.
"It's a matter of how many practices they need, roster spots and things like that. He's doing a great job and he's in a great position mentally, " Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said Wednesday. "It's just about what's the best time and how does that create the most opportunities to get them ready to play? We've got the Denver week. There's not a lot of great practice (opportunities) that week. How does that affect it? There are some other things going on that we've just got to work through, but we'll decide by tomorrow. He'll either practice tomorrow, or he won't."
Losing Price is still a hit to this Seahawks offense. The Notre Dame product was selected with the final pick in the first round of this year's draft. He was effective running behind Jeremiyah Love , rushing for 674 yards and 11 touchdowns in 2025, while averaging 6.0 yards per attempt. Price also led the FBS in kickoff return average (37.5) for players who registered at least 10 returns.

title: Who is Jalon Daniels? Buccaneers rookie quarterback went from undrafted to starting
summary: The undrafted Kansas product makes franchise history as he steps in for an injured Baker Mayfield with Tampa Bay searching for its first win
full_text:
Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield is expected to miss several weeks after dislocating the thumb on his throwing hand during the Week 3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings . That means it's Jalon Daniels time in Tampa.
The undrafted rookie out of Kansas will be thrown into the starting lineup this Sunday against the Green Bay Packers . He will become the first Kansas quarterback to start a game since Frank Seurer in 1987, and is actually the first undrafted rookie quarterback to start a game in Buccaneers history, per CBS Sports Research.
The Bucs have gotten off to a disappointing 0-3 start, and there's plenty of blame to go around for the issues with this team. With head coach Todd Bowles on what feels like an increasingly warmer seat, can this undrafted player come in and spark the offense against a beatable opponent? Let's take a look at who Jalon Daniels is.
Daniels was born in Lawndale, California, and attended Lawndale High School. As a recruit, 247Sports ranked him as a three-star prospect, the No. 61 dual-threat athlete in the country, and No. 298 overall player from the state of California. Daniels initially committed to Middle Tennessee State, but later decommitted and pledged allegiance to the Jayhawks.
Daniels was one of three Kansas quarterbacks who appeared during the season opener in 2020, which was played in an empty stadium due to the coronavirus pandemic. He got the start for his second collegiate game, and completed 19 of 33 passes for 159 yards while also rushing for 23 yards in a 47-14 loss to Baylor. Daniels was just 17 years old at the time.
It was a tough season for Daniels and the Jayhawks, as Kansas finished with a 0-9 record. The true freshman completed 50% of his passes for 718 yards, one touchdown and four interceptions in seven games played with six starts.
Kansas named Jason Bean its new starting quarterback for the 2021 season, but an injury forced Daniels back into the lineup. That first start came against the hated Texas Longhorns -- who were around 30-point favorites against Kansas. Daniels led the Jayhawks to a thrilling 57-56 upset victory in overtime, in which he threw for 202 yards, three touchdowns, and rushed for 45 yards and another touchdown.
Daniels showed off his ability as a magician on the game-winning two-point conversion.
Kansas beats Texas 57-56 on a crazy 2-point conversion in overtime! 🏈 pic.twitter.com/IJy6KZWjqL
Daniels was named the starter for the 2022 season, which was his junior year. Kansas started hot, winning its first five games before eventually falling to a ranked TCU team. Overall, the Jayhawks tallied their most victories in a single season (6) since 2008, while Daniels threw for 2,014 yards, 18 touchdowns and four interceptions.
Entering 2023, Daniels was named the Big 12 Preseason Offensive Player of the Year. The college football world was prepared to embrace him as the lovable legend of Lawrence, but a nagging back injury suffered prior to the start of the campaign held Daniels to just three games. Even without Daniels, Kansas went 9-4 and won its first bowl game in 15 years. Running back Devin Neal emerged as a star, rushing for 1,280 yards and 16 touchdowns that year.
Daniels announced on Nov. 16, 2023 , that he would be returning to Kansas for what would be his redshirt junior season in 2024.
"I'm going to be blunt. This season didn't go as planned," Daniels said. "But life comes at you fast, and sometimes your story's out of your control. But I guess that just means I have unfinished business. My dreams haven't changed, my goals are still there, and my vision for my future is clear. So you want something to talk about? Talk about this: I'm not done yet, and I'm not going anywhere. Rock Chalk."
Kansas had a rough start to the year, losing six of its first eight games. However, the Jayhawks rebounded to beat three ranked teams in a row in Iowa State, BYU and Colorado. Daniels threw for 2,454 yards, 14 touchdowns and a career-high 12 interceptions, but also recorded a career-high 439 yards rushing and six touchdowns.
Daniels then returned for his sixth year at Kansas thanks to COVID-19 and injury waivers.
"It's all about finishing where you started," Daniels told CBS Sports prior to the 2025 season. "I went to multiple high schools. I went to multiple middle schools. Kansas gave me a chance when no other Power Five school in the nation gave me a chance, and I feel like that has a big part to do with it."
Daniels registered his second-straight 5-7 season, and threw for a career-high 2,531 yards, a career-high 22 touchdowns and seven interceptions.
"My Kansas journey has kind of been just like my life; it's come with a lot of ups and downs, and it hasn't been easy at all," Daniels said. "When I felt like I've been performing at my greatest, trials and tribulations such as injuries have come about. It's always just been about being able to bounce back from it."
Daniels' Kansas story didn't go or end how everyone wanted it to. While he flashed star potential, he left Lawrence with a 19-26 record and questions about his future as a football player.
Daniels finished his collegiate career ranked second in program history in passing yards (9,282) and passing touchdowns (67), and was one of two Jayhawks to ever accumulate 10,000 yards of total offense , joining Todd Reesing. Draft pundits criticized his throwing mechanics, accuracy, and ability to diagnose coverages, but what he could do as a scrambler was enticing. It all led to Daniels going undrafted, but he found an opportunity with the Buccaneers.
In Tampa, Mayfield was established as the starter, and he had Jake Browning as a new No. 2. Browning was once viewed as a top backup in the NFL , as he won four of seven starts with the Cincinnati Bengals in 2023. However, Daniels found a way to unseat him. The rookie completed 61.4% of his passes for 239 yards, one touchdown and zero interceptions in three preseason games played and also rushed for 37 yards and another touchdown.
Now, Daniels is presented with a massive opportunity. From being an underrated recruit out of California, to the ups and downs at Kansas and his victorious fight to earn a roster spot on an NFL team , Daniels can add another chapter to his already-fascinating story by registering an upset victory in his first NFL start. Who's to say it's not possible? Quarterbacks who did not start Week 1 are a perfect 6-0.
"I think that one thing I learned in college was, you can't be the thermometer, you have to be the thermostat," Daniels said this week. "You have to be someone who comes in and is able to set the temperature of the room, not test the room and try to be able to blend in with it. If a team is low, I have to be able to pick it up to be able to make sure that they're even. If we're high, then I have to be able to be low to be able to make sure that we're even. I try to be as even-keel as possible. I think that being able to go out there and have that even-keeled feel, the team around you feels that."

title: Bears make starting QB decision for Week 4 matchup vs. Jets
summary: Ben Johnson turns back to his primary backup over veteran Case Keenum, who threw two touchdowns in a shocking upset over the Eagles on Monday night
full_text:
The Chicago Bears have reportedly made a decision on their starting quarterback with Caleb Williams still sidelined by a hamstring strain. The Athletic reports that Tyson Bagent will take over under center on Sunday when Chicago hosts the New York Jets .
Bagent was always viewed as the Bears' backup quarterback, but the veteran Case Keenum was forced to step in when Bagent spent most of last week in concussion protocol. The 38-year-old Keenum registered one of the most shocking upsets of this young season, as he threw for 247 yards and two touchdowns in the 27-7 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night. His performance made it a legitimate question of who would start in Week 4, but head coach Ben Johnson is going back to his original second-stringer.
"We'll have a discussion as a coaching staff, and we'll see where we need to go from here," Johnson said earlier this week. "But I said it last week, and I'll say it again. There was a reason why Tyson ended training camp as our No. 2 quarterback."
The Bears will become the third team to ever start three different quarterbacks through the first four weeks of the season, and the first since the 1997 Jacksonville Jaguars , per CBS Sports Research.
Bagent found his way to the Bears in 2023 after going undrafted out of Shepherd University -- a Division II school in Shepherdstown, West Virginia. He did enough in his first preseason to earn a spot on the final 53-man roster, and ended up making four starts as a rookie!
In Week 7 that year, Bagent won his first career start against the Las Vegas Raiders by throwing for 162 yards and one touchdown. He then lost back-to-back starts against the Los Angeles Chargers and New Orleans Saints before defeating No. 1 overall pick Bryce Young and the Carolina Panthers in prime time, 16-13.
Bagent hasn't made a start since his wild rookie season, but did earn a two-year, $10 million extension with the Bears prior to the 2025 campaign. It made him the first Bears quarterback to sign a contract extension since Jay Cutler did so in January 2014, according to The Athletic .
