title: 49ers vs. Broncos prediction: MVP favorite Brock Purdy and San Francisco look to stay undef
summary: What you need to know ahead of these teams facing off on Sunday
full_text:
The Denver Broncos and San Francisco 49ers are facing off on CBS this Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET at Levi's Stadium. Both teams are coming off wins, with Denver at 2-1, while the 49ers are one of the two undefeated NFC teams at 3-0.
The 49ers started the season strong, defeating the Rams , who were a Super Bowl favorite heading into the season. They then defeated the Miami Dolphins and, most recently, took down the Arizona Cardinals .
Denver began the year with a 31-10 divisional loss to the Kansas City Chiefs , then beat the Jacksonville Jaguars and the Los Angeles Rams.
The Niners have been hit hard by injuries, which we'll get into more below, but they've shown they can adapt and win with whoever is on the field. Their offense is a fun one to watch — remember the hook-and-ladder that allowed for Deebo Samuel to have a stat line of 0 receptions for 80 yards and a touchdown?
The Broncos have demonstrated that they can come from behind and win, as they did last week against the Rams.
Date: Sunday, Oct. 4 | Time: 4:25 p.m. ET Location: Levi's Stadium (Santa Clara, CA) TV: CBS | Stream: Paramount+ Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: 49ers -3 ( via DraftKings )
To say the Niners have been hit hard by injuries is an understatement. Wide receivers Ricky Pearsall , Demarcus Robinson , Christian Kirk and De'Zhaun Stribling ; tight end Jake Tonges ; running back Isaac Guerendo ; offensive linemen Austen Pleasants and Brett Toth ; defensive ends Sam Okuayinonu , Mikail Kamara and Andrew Farmer II; defensive tackles Alfred Collins and CJ West ; linebacker Nick Martin ; defensive back Darrick Forrest and cornerback Nate Hobbs , to name a few, have all been on the injured reserve or PUP list.
There are so many players injured that the team has to strategically pick who they put on injured reserve so they don't run out of space, and that brings us to this week's injury report. They had 10 players on Wednesday's report, including Mykel Williams , who began the season on the PUP list. Defensive lineman Nick Bosa was listed with a knee/calf injury and is expected to miss multiple weeks. He is not on IR likely because the team doesn't have the space.
Wide receivers Mike Evans (ribs) and KhaDarel Hodge (knee); linebacker Dre Greenlaw (quad); and defensive linemen James Thompson Jr . (ankle) and Keion White (hamstring) were all listed as non-participants in Wednesday and Thursday's practice. Running back Christian McCaffrey and tackle Trent Williams also did not practice on Wednesday, but were listed as "not injury related/resting player," and both returned as limited participants on Thursday.
MVPurdy: Let's pretend it's not too soon to start talking about who the MVP will be and instead talk about why the 49ers quarterback is off to an MVP start. The definition of who the MVP is varies across the league and among fans every year, whether you think it's for the player who performed best overall or who meant the most to their team. Whichever way you slice it, Mr. Irrelevant, if we can still call him that, is in the conversation. He ranks eighth in passing yards (789), is tied for first in touchdown passes (9), second in completion percentage among current starters (72.3) and third in yards per attempt (10.2). He hasn't been sacked yet, and the challenge for the Broncos' defense is that it isn't quick to get to the QB. Denver's secondary is tough and can force turnovers, but the 49ers are quick to give the ball up.
The run game: The 49ers offense excels in the run game, and the Broncos defense doesn't excel in stopping the run. San Fran is sixth in rushing yards (409) and fourth in yards per carry (5.1). Denver's defense has allowed the third most yards (431) and is tied for the second-most yards per carry (5.1). Denver will need to even up this mismatch as much as possible, or the Niners will run all over them (pun intended). The Broncos' run game is not their offensive strong suit, with the second-fewest rushing yards (243) and the second-most fumbles (2). The Niners' run defense is in the middle of the pack. Who can establish the run, and who can establish it early, will be huge in the outcome of this game.
The 49ers haven't given me a reason to believe they won't win this game, and while I think it will be competitive, I think they improve to 4-0. They have made it work with the number of injuries they're dealing with, but if the injury bug doesn't slow down soon, the holes will become more obvious than they are now.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: Bills vs. Patriots preview: Buffalo looks to stay perfect, New England looks to get right
summary: Everything you need to know to tune into the AFC East showdown
full_text:
Going into the 2026 season, the Week 4 matchup between the New England Patriots and Buffalo Bills was one I had circled as an even matchup. Now, with three weeks behind us, the story is a big different.
The Patriots desperately need this to be a reset, as the defending AFC Champions' season begins to crumble below them. But no one is happier to watch the Patriots struggle than the Bills. When it comes to AFC East titles, the last two decades, New England has personified a roadblock for the Bills. Even last year, when the Patriots were supposed to be rebuilding, a hat and t-shirt game should have been a little easier to obtain for the Bills. But it was deja vu all over again for Buffalo.
This season looks to be swinging back in the Bills' favor. The Patriots are their own worst enemy, the Miami Dolphins may have the worst roster in NFL history and the New York Jets are well... the New York Jets.
Let's dive deeper into the AFC East showdown.
Date: Sunday, Oct. 4 | Time: 1 p.m. ET Location: Highmark Stadium (Orchard Park, NY) TV: CBS | Stream: Paramount+ Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bills -7, O/U 48.5 ( via DraftKings )
The Patriots come into the game sitting at 1-2 with a laundry list of issues to fix. Their one win was a decent showing against the Pittsburgh Steelers , but even in the victory, cracks were shown. They are coming off a 35-6 loss against the Jacksonville Jaguars , in which Patriots quarterback Drake Maye threw two interceptions and had two fumbles, losing one. Maye has a league-high six interceptions and looks like a shell of the runner-up MVP we saw last season.
The Bills are in a different boat than New England at 3-0, though turnovers are something they struggled with last week as well. In their Week 3 24-16 win over the Los Angeles Chargers , they turned the ball over five times, with three fumbles lost and two interceptions. This was a prime example of the old adage that great teams find a way to win no matter what.
Patriots vs. Bills is a storied matchup, and New England owns the all-time series at 79-51-1.
Drake Maye drama: This week, reports surfaced that Maye and Vrabel are having issues. Both shut down them down quickly , and Vrabel said Maye is one of the reasons he chose the New England head coaching job. QB-HC issues are certainly not what this team needs. There also seems to be some questions on Maye's shoulder. Vrabel said earlier in the week that there were no issues with the area, while Maye was a little more vague answering questions, but he has said the shoulder isn't the reason for his poor play. Then comes Wednesday's injury report, and QB1 is on it, listed as a full participant with a right shoulder injury. This just raises even more questions about whether Maye can reach the level he was at last season, and it causes confusion about whether it was impacting him when Vrabel said it wasn't.
Turning point: The Patriots started the 2025 season by losing to the Las Vegas Raiders (who looked a lot different than they do this season at 3-0). The loss seemed like a sign of things to come. A month later, the Patriots were 2-2 going into a Week 5 battle against the Bills, and it was Buffalo's game to lose. The Patriots went on to beat Buffalo 23-20, and it ended up being a turning point for this season. Could that happen this year as well?
Bills' run game: I think a big key to this game will be Buffalo's run game. They are fourth-best in the league through three games with 465 yards and stand atop the league at eight touchdowns on the ground. The Patriots' run defense is in the middle of the pack and could have their work cut out for them against Allen and Co. Buffalo needs to come out strong early, because so far this hasn't been a Patriots team that shakes off early mistakes.
Logic, stats, and research show the Bills will win this one, but divisional games are always different and have a way of surprising us. I'd love to say I'm bold enough to pick the Patriots, because so few people will pick them that I'd look like a genius if New England pulls out a win. But it's hard to argue with what I've seen from the two teams so far. And what I've seen is a lost Patriots team, lacking identity and perhaps more issues than they're willing to admit. The Bills are once again a Super Bowl favorite —though if you ask me, that window is starting to close — and they are a complete and well-operated machine that finds multiple ways to win.

title: Inside Drake Maye's alarming 2026 slump one year after Patriots QB was MVP runner-up
summary: New England's franchise quarterback has six interceptions and an NFL-worst 58.6 passer rating as opposing evaluators question his confidence and pocket poise
full_text:
Through the Patriots ' first 20 games last season -- a combination of the regular season and the three playoff games leading into the Super Bowl -- there wasn't a single game that Drake Maye finished with more than one interception. It was a breakthrough year that saw Maye finish as MVP runner-up and catapult himself onto the short list of the NFL's best young quarterbacks.
Eight months later, the 24-year old is now coming off his third multi-interception performance in New England's last four games dating back to that Super Bowl loss to Seahawks .
It's part of a maddening run for Maye and the Patriots, who are off to a 1-2 start just a season after advancing to the Super Bowl. A large part of that has been regression from Maye that's surprised many around the NFL, including (based on grades from Pro Football Focus) the worst game of his career last week during the Patriots' 35-6 loss to the Jaguars . Maye finished with no touchdowns and two interceptions.
In all through the first three games of this season, the 2024 and 2025 Pro Bowl selection has six interceptions with just one touchdown, has yet to eclipse 208 passing yards in any individual game and has a QB rating (58.6) that ranks as the worst in the NFL among quarterbacks who've made more than two starts.
It's led to some in NFL coaching and front office circles starting to wonder whether Maye's confidence is on a downward spiral.
"When I when I studied him when he was coming out (of college), you saw the athletic ability and you saw the arm talent but, especially his last year at North Carolina, there were just a lot of the misses, and the missed throws were kind of alarming and some instinctual things too," a veteran NFL front office staffer told CBS Sports. "Then last year (in that second season in New England), he looked just a lot more comfortable and in command and like the game had slowed down for him. But now this year it almost looks like it's kind of sped up for him a little bit. And some of the misses, whether it be mis-read or missed throw, some of those things have just kind of popped up a little bit more and he's just not taking care of the ball all that well.
"He just doesn't look comfortable and confident out there right now, especially when he's in the pocket. You still see how much talent he has. It's just very up and down play in and play out."
Opposing team staffers also see teams having success generating pressuring on Maye and that impacting him.
In Super Bowl LX, the Seahawks had six sacks of Maye. Then in Week 1, Seattle again had success pressuring him, this time, as described by sources familiar with their gameplan, shifting to more zone blitzes instead of man-to-man pressures after the Patriots' offseason wide receiver additions. The Seahawks finished with three sacks and three interceptions.
The Steelers then had three sacks in Week 2 and the Jaguars followed that last week with three sacks too.
"He's a good quarterback obviously but we were able to pressure him early and I think that showed up later (impacting his play)," an opposing team staffer said.
Other opposing coaches have been critical of New England's offensive system as well and point to that as a primary issue. It also doesn't help that Maye and the Patriots have been without the team's main offseason acquisition, star wide receiver A.J. Brown, since Week 1 due to ankle injury. Without Brown, as one opposing defensive coach put it, "they don't have receivers that are getting open."
Either way, Maye and New England now head into a matchup against Josh Allen and the 3-0 Bills having yet to produce more than 13 offensive points in any of these first three games, a big dropoff in offensive success for the Patriots after ranking second in the NFL with an average of 28.8 points per game.
"He's got to be better at learning what defenses look like and where his relief's going to be, but the offensive system doesn't do him any favors in my opinion," an opposing coach, who's faced New England this season, said. "They only run a certain number of plays and it's the same plays they've been running for a long time. And if your quarterback's not Tom Brady, who's going to get you in the perfect call, or someone like Josh Allen who's (elite at) second-chance plays, that offensive system after a while starts to get real stale."
Last week, back when it was still unclear how much time Jayden Daniels would miss due to his injured left elbow, the Commanders star quarterback decided to get in front of his team and announce that he was going to bypass surgery and that he owed it to the team to get back as quickly as possible.
Within days, Daniels was already back doing light throwing. He then practiced this week on a limited basis. And while he won't play this week vs. the Colts in London, sources continue to classify him as truly being week-to-week.
Washington, which beat the Seahawks last week behind backup QB Marcus Mariota to move to 1-2, face the Giants next week and then play the 49ers .
For a second straight season already, the 49ers have had to deal with injuries to a number of key players.
There's some good news on that front, though, with a high level of confidence that 2025 first-round draft pick Mykel Williams , who's been out since an ACL injury last November, will be able to return to action and play next week when the 49ers face the Seahawks, sources tell CBS Sports.
The defensive end returned to practice this week after beginning the season on the PUP list. Williams, whom San Francisco selected with the No. 11 pick in last year's draft, started nine games for the 49ers last year before suffering the torn ACL.

Q: Are you satisfied with the team’s moves after the Jaxson Dart injury? Well, […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 21: Head Coach John Harbaugh of the New York Giants walks the field prior to the game against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on September 21, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Happy Saturday one and all. Ed Valentine, the longtime leader of Big Blue View was kind enough to bring out of retirement the “Five Questions with the Enemies” so lets get to know the New York Giants a little better. Enjoy. Q: Are you satisfied with the team’s moves after the Jaxson Dart injury? Well, I think the Giants were aggressive in trying to make the quarterback room the best it can be without the No. 1 guy. They used a fifth-round pick to acquire J.J. McCarthy. Now, there are a lot of opinions about McCarthy, and nobody knows if he will become Sam Darnold, Trey Lance, or something in-between. I think Giants fans should be heartened by the fact that the team was aggressive in addressing a problem. For the Giants, it still comes down to whether or not Jameis Winston can handle the job. They gave Winston a two-year, $13 million extension right before the season started. I have a hard time believing they will hurry to replace him, although there is already a lot of “when will McCarthy start?” chatter. Who is going to be counted on most to help negate the loss of Brian Burns? Well, former No. 3 overall pick Abdul Carter is going to have to assert himself. Kayvon Thibodeaux will play more. Maybe Arvell Reese will be used more as a rusher. It is going to be incumbent upon defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson, though to be more creative than he has been over the first three weeks to put rushers in better situations. Arvell Reese was a hotly debated prospect among Cardinals fans, what has he shown the first month of the season and how do you feel about his long term outlook? Reese is going to be a star. He isn’t there yet, but he will get there. This guy is absurdly physical. He can run. He can tackle in space. He can cover. He has pass rush potential. He wants to work at it and get better. It won’t be long before he is a dominant player. What is the overall feeling as the John Harbaugh era has gotten underway? Optimism. Harbaugh has brought professionalism, expectations, the ability and willingness to make players understand the hard work required. The Giants aren’t a “clown show” anymore. The Cardinals are slight road favorites, Is that more a concern about the Giants offense or defense in your opinion? I don’t know. It is a bit of a surprise to me. Still, the Giants have lost their quarterback and their best defensive player the past two weeks. It’s probably a bit of both. The Giants are coming off a game in which they scored only 12 points, so I get the concern on that side.

title: Falcons vs. Saints: A look at the series history going into 2026 Part 1
summary: The calendar in Week 3 is highlighted, marked and underlined as it always is when the Falcons square off against their arch nemeses the New Orleans Saints. This is the best rivalry in football and also one of those that’s just so tight within the margins as the Falcons lead it 58-56 through 114 historic […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - JANUARY 01: Michael Thomas #13 of the New Orleans Saints is tackled by Deion Jones #45 of the Atlanta Falcons after a catch during the first half at the Georgia Dome on January 1, 2017 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The calendar in Week 3 is highlighted, marked and underlined as it always is when the Falcons square off against their arch nemeses the New Orleans Saints. This is the best rivalry in football and also one of those that’s just so tight within the margins as the Falcons lead it 58-56 through 114 historic meetings since the founding of the Saints in 1967. New Orleans has spent the past two decades undoing a lot of the work Atlanta has done in the 40 years preceding that time period. A 26-14 mark for the Saints since the arrival of Sean Payton and Drew Brees, in 2006, plus subsequent success after their departure closed the gap in what felt like an insurmountable Falcon lead in the all time series up until then. That gap was actually all the way closed heading into last season, but the Birds completing their first sweep in this series since the 2016 season restored some semblance of order and has them ahead in the series once again. This matchup will be a special one, as it marks the 20th year anniversary of the 2006 re-opening of the Superdome on Monday Night Football following the events of Hurricane Katrina. That was the first game which sparked this era of Saints dominance over the Falcons. ESPN and the Falcons were in the building for the 10-year anniversary of that same event, in 2016, and Dan Quinn’s unit spoiled the festivities with a 45-32 victory. When these teams met last Just like they did in all those years in the old days of the ‘70s, ‘80s and ‘90s, the Falcons and Saints came into the grudge match with terrible records (Atlanta 3-7 and New Orleans 2-8) and faltering playoff hopes, but that didn’t take away from the importance which this game always presents. Kirk Cousins was back under center for the Birds following Michael Penix’s knee injury which would cost him the rest of the season, the week before. He matched up against rookie Tyler Shough who had taken over the reigns as the starter in New Orleans following Spencer Rattler’s poor season. Both offenses struggled throughout the first half. Cousins threw the only two touchdowns of the first two periods, but one was to each team. He first found defacto WR1 David Sills from nine yards out, but then threw a pick six to Justin Reid on the next drive. The Falcons did work the field enough to get in position for three Zane Gonzalez field goals to take a 16-7 lead into the break, as the Saints kept shooting themselves in the foot with two Blake Grupe missed field goals and a fumble from an aborted snap. The Saints kept up with the errors in the second half, in the form of a couple of turnovers on downs along with an intentional grounding on 3rd down from the Atlanta 1-yard-line, as the Falcons just kept biding their time until finally putting together a drive which culminated in a 49-yard Cousins to Darnell Mooney kill shot to extend the lead to two possessions in the fourth quarter, for the decisive 24-10 scoreline.

title: Gervon Dexter earns extension and delivers proof, not potential for Falcons
summary: The four-year, $78 million extension of Atlanta Falcons defensive tackle Gervon Dexter marks a potential turning point for the team’s front office. Dexter has been outstanding through his first three games in a Falcons uniform and is the latest player to get a major pay raise in recent months. However, his new deal signals a […]
full_text: Sep 13, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers offensive tackle Troy Fautanu (76) looks to block Atlanta Falcons defensive tackle Gervon Dexter Sr. during the secnd half at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The four-year, $78 million extension of Atlanta Falcons defensive tackle Gervon Dexter marks a potential turning point for the team’s front office. Dexter has been outstanding through his first three games in a Falcons uniform and is the latest player to get a major pay raise in recent months. However, his new deal signals a shift in philosophy: moving forward, the Falcons will reward proven production rather than bet on pure potential. This summer, I criticized the team’s decision to extend both Kyle Pitts and Matthew Bergeron because both players were relatively unproven in the new incarnation of the Falcons offense. Paying both, despite not knowing whether they’d blossom under new offensive coordinator Tommy Rees and offensive line coach Bill Callahan, felt like a continuation of the team’s trend of overrating itself with little to show over the last eight years of underachieving. Through three weeks, Pitts has barely produced, and Bergeron has been up and down . Three games isn’t a huge sample size, but in Dexter’s case, it’s been more than enough to show he can shine in a new defensive scheme under coordinator Jeff Ulbrich and the tutelage of position coach Nate Ollie. Dexter’s fast 2026 start prompts huge payday Dexter leads the Falcons with 14 pressures and has a l eague-leading pass rush win rate among interior defenders, per Pro Football Focus . With such a brilliant start to the season, the Falcons’ signing of Dexter now may have saved them money . Dexter’s $19.5 million-per-year AAV ranks 21st among interior defensive linemen, according to OvertheCap.com . However, the full details of his deal have not yet been revealed as of this writing. Reports of $46.5 million in guarantees align with the guarantees in contracts recently signed by Zach Allen, Milton Williams, and Vita Vea. All those players signed for over $25 million per year, so the Falcons’ new cap guru , Bryce Johnston, may have structured Dexter’s deal closer to the top of the market than the initial numbers suggest. Regardless of how Dexter’s pay stacks up among his peers, the main takeaway is that the Falcons waited even a few games to pay him after he proved himself on the field. Hopefully, that will be their guiding principle from here on. Falcons are building sustainable pass rush around Dexter and young core Dexter’s success is a great sign for Atlanta, showcasing the team’s ability to take underachieving talent elsewhere, plug them into their system, and reap greater results. General manager Ian Cunningham’s familiarity with Dexter from their shared days in Chicago was instrumental in diagnosing the latter’s breakout potential in Atlanta. With $114 million in projected 2027 cap space, Cunningham will have the flexibility to go on an offseason spending spree to find and polish more potential diamonds in the rough like Dexter. Dexter’s brilliant 2026 start also bodes well for the long-term outlook of the Falcons’ pass rush, which is currently among the NFL’s best. Depending on whose data you’re surveying, the Falcons sport the league’s top ( per TruMedia ), second ( per Next Gen Stats ), or third-best ( per ESPN ) pressure rate. Regardless, the Falcons’ dominance up front, despite effectively operating at half strength, is truly impressive. They are without edge rushers James Pearce ( suspension ) and Jalon Walker ( injury ). If and when both players return healthy and focused in 2027, it bodes extremely well for the Falcons to feature a dominant four-man unit alongside Dexter and Brandon Dorlus. Dorlus is the oldest of the group and is only 25, suggesting the Falcons can field a fearsome pass rush for years to come. Dexter delivers proof and a long-awaited shift in vibes It’s an exciting, unprecedented outlook for a team that has been allergic to sacks for the past two decades . Coupled with renewed optimism at quarterback thanks to Michael Penix’s impressive return last week against the Green Bay Packers , it drives legitimate hope that things are turning around for the Falcons. The vibes are finally good in Atlanta for the first time in months. Of course, the team will have to maintain this momentum, with Dexter and his teammates continuing to produce on the field and in the win column. But the Falcons are finally delivering proof, not just promises.

title: Ravens discussion: score prediction, X-factors for Week 4 vs. Titans
summary: The Baltimore Ravens (2-1) are hosting the Tennessee Titans (0-3) on Sunday afternoon in the hopes of winning their first home game since last November. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s game picks with score predictions and X-factors. Be sure to add yours in the comments section below! Nikhil Mehta I mean, Cam Ward has to figure […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 20: Matt Hibner #88 of the Baltimore Ravens runs in the backfield against the New Orleans Saints during an NFL football game at M&T Bank Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens (2-1) are hosting the Tennessee Titans (0-3) on Sunday afternoon in the hopes of winning their first home game since last November. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s game picks with score predictions and X-factors. Be sure to add yours in the comments section below! Nikhil Mehta I mean, Cam Ward has to figure it out sometime , right? Kidding. Last season, I souned the alarm bell that the Ravens were winning unconvincingly. But even with all of 2025’s injuries and chaos, Baltimore consistently still beat every bad quarterback they faced. Ward is undeniably struggling, and I do not think he will have a coming-out party against Jesse Minter’s defense. Lamar Jackson is playing at an extremely high level, but the Titans’ defensive line could be the great equalizer against Baltimore’s shuffled interior. But even if Jeffrey Simmons and Co. can hold serve against Jackson, Derrick Henry, and a fully-healthy Zay Flowers, it is hard to see Tennessee’s offense keeping up. If the Ravens defense is truly hungry for a get-right performance in front of the home crowd, they should have no problem stuffing Ward in the dirt and putting up their best game of the season. X-factor: Justice Hill’s pass protection. Between Tennessee’s D-line duo of Jeffrey Simmons and John Franklin-Myers and new starters at center and right guard, the Ravens’ interior O-line will be feeling the heat on Sunday. If Saleh uses inside linebacker blitzes as recent opponents have, Hill could play a major role in pass protection. Jackson only needs an extra split-second to make a play; can Hill give it to him when he needs it? Score prediction: Ravens 27, Titans 13 Frank Platko The Ravens have been starving for a convincing win at home, where they’ve now last four straight games dating back to last November. For many years, the Ravens had a reputation for playing dominant defensive football against young quarterbacks on their home turf. I think we see them perform in that mold this Sunday. The Ravens should be able to get pressure on Cam Ward and force multiple turnovers against this Titans’ offense, which lacks any matchup advantages versus Baltimore’s defensive units. The Titans’ biggest offensive strength is their running back duo of Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears, who are averaging nearly 100 combined scrimmage yards per game and each eclipsing 4.5+ yards per carry. Look for the Ravens to try to tighten up their run defense in this game and live with Tennessee’s passing attack trying to beat their secondary. X-factor: Vega Ioane. The first-round pick is set to make his first ever start at center following injuries to both of the team’s primary centers. Ioane looked good in limited action at center in Week 3 when he took over in the fourth quarter, but the sample size was very small. He’ll need to quickly adapt to the operations of the position and snapping the ball cleanly to avoid broken exchanges with Lamar Jackson. Ioane will have his hands full against Jeffery Simmons, who is one of the premier defensive lineman in the league. Score prediction: Ravens 30, Titans 13 Kevin McNelis The Ravens, in the midst of the second-longest home win drought in the NFL, host an 0-3 Titans squad that might be the most defeated-looking team I’ve seen in Week 4 of any season in recent memory. A stoppable force meets a moveable object, and I think around here, we’re all just hoping the Ravens can make it a little easier on themselves than they have the last two weeks. If you’ve followed the Titans over the last few weeks, vibes are bad, to say the least. Cam Ward sits dead last in passing yardage among starting QBs that have played all three games this season. Their top two running backs are banged up, and the team is in the bottom five in both rushing and passing. I get the sense that Tennessee’s offense will plod along in this one if it gets going at all, and I’m hopeful that the Ravens D gets a confidence boost from some successes. We’ve seen forced fumbles pay dividends, but I’d love to see a few picks or some sacks from the interior of the D-line. On the flip side, Baltimore is going to have to figure out what the heck to do along the O-line. Just a few days out from the game, we still don’t have a great idea of who lines up where, and they have the tough task ahead of trying to keep Jeffrey Simmons away from LJ. Based on Derrick Henry disclosing this week that he felt like the Titans unceremoniously shuffled him out of town, I’d put the ball in the big man’s hands and let him get his anger out on their defense, especially given how much better the line has looked in run blocking than in pass protection. X-factor: Matthew Hibner I felt like doubling down on King Henry here was cheating, so I’m going to give props to the rookie tight end. He showed up big time last game, and he’s looked confident as a short-yardage option for Lamar. Look for him to make another big play this week, and hopefully one that comes after the defense sets him up on a short field. Score prediction: Ravens 27, Titans 9 Dustin Cox If there was ever a week for the Ravens’ defense to start looking like the unit most people envisioned with Jesse Minter at the helm, then it is this week against a struggling Titans’ offense with a young quarterback. Baltimore has shown glimpses of what their defense can be in every game so far this season, but fourth quarter woes in particular have dragged the unit down. Tennessee does not have a Chris Olave, George Pickens, or CeeDee Lamb at wide receiver, so the Ravens should not have to play the deep pass as hard. Even without Trey Hendrickson, Baltimore’s front should be able to generate enough pressure on Cam Ward. Finishing sacks and avoiding missed tackles, especially on third down, will be key to finally having a dominant defensive performance this week. X-factor: Andrew Vorhees. It is expected for Vorhees to get the start at right guard as Vega Ioane moves to center. The interior offensive line has already been an issue for the Ravens’ offense through three weeks and Jeffery Simmons presents the biggest challenge yet for the group. Vorhees needs to hold up so that Vega does not have any extra pressure on him in the middle in his first start at center. Score prediction: Ravens 31, Titans 13 Now, it’s your turn! How do you think the Ravens’ Week 4 matchup will go? Give us your X-factor and score predictions in the comments!

title: 5 Questions with Pride of Detroit
summary: Week 4 of the young 2026 NFL season already has the Carolina Panthers and Detroit Lions trending in different directions. The Lions are playoff contenders and quiet Super Bowl hopefuls. Your 2025 NFC South champions, on the other hand, are just hoping that there are fewer injuries in the 13 weeks after their Week 5 […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OH - SEPTEMBER 27: Carolina Panthers wide receiver John Metchie III (13) celebrates with Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan (4) and Carolina Panthers tight end Tommy Tremble (82) after scoring on a 8-yard touchdown pass during the fourth quarter of the National Football League game between the Carolina Panthers and Cleveland Browns on September 27, 2026, at Huntington Bank Field in Cleveland, OH. (Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Week 4 of the young 2026 NFL season already has the Carolina Panthers and Detroit Lions trending in different directions. The Lions are playoff contenders and quiet Super Bowl hopefuls. Your 2025 NFC South champions, on the other hand, are just hoping that there are fewer injuries in the 13 weeks after their Week 5 bye than there were in the four weeks prior to it. That doesn’t mean that Lions fans are taking this week for granted or that the Lions themselves haven’t struggled with their more fair share of inuries. Ryan Matthews from Pride of Detroit answered five of my questions about the Lions to try to give us their side of this story. These answers were the sober, attentive reflections of a fan whose team has only very recently known success, at least relative to their history. In short, they did not fill me with confidence and optimism in the Panthers chances of catching Detroit in the midst of a cat nap. The Carolina Panthers are quite literally half the team they expected to be when they started training camp. How are the Lions faring with the injury bug this deep into the 2026 season? The Lions’ 2026 roster has bites going back to 2025 that have really put them in a bind on the backend of their defense. Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch, once considered to be the top safety duo in the NFL, suffered season-ending injuries last season, and they’re still on the PUP heading into this Week 4 matchup. Detroit’s secondary has been lit up three straight weeks in a row, and while the cornerbacks haven’t been playing their best ball, missing both Joseph and Branch in their respective safety positions has made for some tough viewing when the Lions defense takes the field. Avonte Maddox, a veteran defensive back, was re-signed to compete for a spot in Detroit’s secondary. He earned it in the summer. Maddox played some free safety, box safety, and in the slot as a nickelback to start the season, but he suffered an injury in Week 2 that put him on injured reserve for the foreseeable future. Thomas Harper is another player who played his way into a spot in the secondary, but he, too, suffered an ankle injury in Week 2’s game against Buffalo that put him on IR as well. That leaves Chuck Clark, a veteran on his fourth stop in as many seasons, to hold down the single-high safety looks for the most part, and safeties coach Jim O’Neil trusts him in that role. Alongside him is Christian Izien, a player who looked like he was shot out of a cannon in his season debut last week against the Jets. Izien had a groin injury crop up at the end of training camp, but he’s a guy who many expected to play the Branch role: box safety, in the slot, up near the line of scrimmage. Izien led the Lions in tackles (11) and finished second in defensive stops (4) against the Jets in Week 3. Unfortunately—or fortunately depending on how you’re looking at it—Panthers fans won’t get to see the return of Cade Mays this weekend in Carolina after he had a freak wrist injury near the beginning of camp. Otherwise, the Lions have been pretty fortunate with injuries! The Lions are already on their second offensive coordinator since Ben Johnson left for the Chicago Bears. What are your hopes and worries three games into the Drew Petzing era? For all the “Dan Campbell is a Ben Johnson merchant” and “Detroit sure misses Ben Johnson” talk, Drew Petzing’s offense has hung 31 points in three consecutive weeks. After a bit of a slow start in terms of opening drives and third-down efficiency, the early returns on Petzing are pretty promising. Jared Goff looks comfortable in the offense, getting into favorable checks and commanding the group. The offensive line dealt with some injuries in the first couple of weeks to their starting left guard—Christian Mahogany—and starting right tackle—rookie Blake Miller—but they looked like a really solid and steady unit when they returned in Week 3. Some mild concerns for me, and they’re admittedly a bit nitpicky, are play calls near the goal line. Last week, nearing the end of the half and the Jets with just one timeout remaining, Detroit called a designed rollout for Goff on first down that he effectively threw away and a fade route to Amon-Ra St. Brown that did result in a touchdown. It left the Jets with 1:36 on the clock and a timeout still at their disposal, but would’ve liked to see the Lions get to their bread and butter by running the football, forcing the Jets to burn their timeout, and playing with their aggressive, four-down approach on offense. Which seems to run counterintuitive to my second nitpick about the offense: the number of run plays on second-and-10. Petzing’s explanation referred back to Detroit’s four-down approach on offense, but against the Bills, it felt like Buffalo knew it was coming, but Detroit still stuck with it, leaving them in plenty of third-and-long situations. Again, early results are trending in a positive way, those concerns are mild at most, but the Lions feel like they’re in a much better spot on offense than they were a season ago. What’s with barely beating the Saints and the Jets? I thought y’all were supposed to be a good team. Is the suggestion here that the Saints and Jets aren’t good football teams? Because New Orleans went into Baltimore and took home a victory, and then they nearly pulled out last week’s game against a 3-0 Las Vegas Raiders team. The Jets are some clock mismanagement away from being a 2-1 football team themselves, so I think Detroit has actually played some pretty tough teams that will challenge for the playoffs in their respective conferences. A rain game where one team is looking to establish a struggling rushing attack against another team that surrendered almost 300 yards in their last home game doesn’t sound like a good time. Any chance Jahmyr Gibbs is on vacation or enough of a Wizard of Oz style witch where he isn’t allowed to get wet? Jahmyr Gibbs figures to be available come rain, sleet, snow, or such poor field conditions that the NFLPA has to file a grievance . You’re going to predict a Lions win, there’s no doubt or shame in that. The interesting question is how big of a win do you think the Lions will have and does that differ from the expectations of the broader Lions fanbase? There’s no way Dan Campbell will have this Lions team overlooking this Panthers team, and I’m not going to either. Their passing attack is explosive, their run defense against running backs has actually been pretty solid the past two weeks, and they’re likely getting Devin Lloyd back for this one. While this one could very well become a shootout—weather permitting—it should be a more tightly contested game. It wouldn’t surprise me if the Lions win by less than one score, and it wouldn’t shock me if the Panthers pull off the upset as home underdogs coming off a disappointing loss in Week 3.

title: Panthers Reacts: Such early despair for a Week 4 fan poll
summary: Fans of the Carolina Panthers were riding high after embarrassing the Atlanta Falcons in Week 3. It rarely takes long in this league to be humbled, however. Week 4 against the Browns turned into a preseason game by the fourth quarter for Carolina, while Cleveland rode their relative health and more conservative coaching to an […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - SEPTEMBER 27: Bryce Young #9 of the Carolina Panthers attempts a pass against the Cleveland Browns during the second quarter at Huntington Bank Field on September 27, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Fans of the Carolina Panthers were riding high after embarrassing the Atlanta Falcons in Week 3. It rarely takes long in this league to be humbled, however. Week 4 against the Browns turned into a preseason game by the fourth quarter for Carolina, while Cleveland rode their relative health and more conservative coaching to an uneasy victory. Should Panthers fans be optimistic that they nearly beat an NFL team while missing so much talent? Maybe. Are they? Assuredly not. Bryce Young looked like vintage 2024 at times (though he ultimately played better than that lowly standard). The offensive line looked like a group of rookies playing together for the first time. The defense seemed like they got more injured with each passing drive. Asking them to cover or contain a mobile quarterback seemed like secondary goals to getting off the field under their own power The fact of the matter is that fan confidence rides wins and losses like a wave. The trough is bigger the better the won or worse the loss. Sunday’s loss, while understandable from one point of view, just felt bad. A loss to the Detroit Lions is expected. I wouldn’t expect another 30+% dip unless Bryce Young throws an interception so horrendous that he, Terairoa McMillan, and Derrick Brown all somehow land on IR just from that one attempt. Conversely, an upset win vould buoy spirits like little else. We’ll have to wait and see what happens. Checkout FanDuel , the official sportsbook partner of SB Nation.

summary: Sunday at Soldier Field (12:00pm CST), the Chicago Bears welcome the New York Jets to the gridiron in a contest where both teams have key players injured and sidelined. full_text: Nov 27, 2022; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; Chicago Bears tight end Cole Kmet (85) is tackled by New York Jets cornerback Michael Carter II (30) and linebacker C.J. Mosley (57) during the second half at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-USA TODAY Sports Sunday at Soldier Field (12:00pm CST), the Chicago Bears welcome the New York Jets to the gridiron in a contest where both teams have key players injured and sidelined. The Jets walk in at 1–2 without Breece Hall (quad), their dynamic running back, and the Bears will walk out once again without Caleb Williams (hamstring) under center. Additionally, the Bears will be without Braxton Jones (knee), and the Jets will be missing Adonai Mitchell (finger) and Dylan Parham (knee). While the Bears got an amazing game from third-string quarterback Case Keenum on Monday night, the consensus among the experts is that Ben Johnson is likely to hand the ball back to Tyson Bagent, who is back from the concussion protocol. That said, the Bears have not officially named a starter for the game. Whichever backup has the job on Sunday, the job remains the same: protect a 2–1 start against a New York offense that has been living on the run and is now without its best back. Below is our roundtable predicting the score, individual highlights like touchdowns, yardage, sacks, and the takeaways we think will decide the game this week. Josh Sunderbruch : I have this as Bears 24-Jets 17, but with the 17 padded by a garbage-time score. There’s a mix of playmakers on both sides, but Chicago’s coaching staff is going to manufacture the difference. This might be a breakout game for Thomas. Sam Householder: I don’t know if it’s Tyson Bagent or Case Keenum, and I don’t care. The Bears are the better team and will want to prove it. They have the advantage on the ground. I think the passing game will look worse regardless of who plays QB but Chicago grinds it out on the ground. Bears 24, Jets 14 Gary Baugher Jr .: I’m going 28-17, with the Bears in the drivers seat the most of the way, whether it’s Case or Tyson driving is another thing entirely, but I expect a gameplan close to what we saw with the Eagles. Run/Pass balance, short timing routes, and reliance on the run to bring us home as it wears down the Jets defense slowly. Tom Martin : 30-17 Bears. The Jets have pieces all over the field, but will be missing their glue guy in Breece Hall. Without him, they will struggle to consistently gain first downs against a jump-started Bears defense. Ben Johnson proved that his scheme can adapt to the QB, so whether it’s Keenum or Bagent, I expect the offense to continue to look efficient. Quick passes, smart running scheme, opportunistic defense. Bears roll. Gooch : 31-14 Bears. I don’t think the Bears miss a beat shifting from Old Man Keenum to young pup Tyson Bagent. While the Jets have been surprisingly competitive to start the season, and I expect Geno Smith to spam the Garret Wilson button, I don’t think they have enough against Dennis Allen’s defense, which, ever since that shootout in Carolina, has been stifling. Allen shuts down the Jets’ depleted rushing attack, forcing them into bad down-and-distance situations. Smith throws for a TD but hands the Bears two interceptions, one to Thineman that he takes to the house. Booker, Sweat, and Motivated Dayo add sacks. JVDB’s pressure forces one of the picks. On offense, Bagent throws for 250 yards and two touchdowns, while Monangai and Swift add TDs on the ground. Rome Odunze gets on the board with a touchdown and over 100 yards receiving in a breakout game. The Bears cruise to victory and are 3-1 going into the matchup against Green Bay. Superfans: We don’t give a ras ass if it’s Case Keenum, Tyson Bagent, Kyle Orton, or Henry Burris; this one is gonna have the same outcome… Da Bears!

title: Chicago Bears vs. New York Jets: Week 4 Players to Watch
summary: The NFL season is constantly evolving. Week 4 arrives with more optimism than expected in Chicago after an upset victory of the previously unbeaten Eagles on Monday night. In this weekly series, I’ll feature one player from the Chicago Bears opponent on each side of the ball who I think is integral to their team’s […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 20: T'vondre Sweat #99 of the New York Jets reacts to play against the Green Bay Packers during the first quarter of the game at MetLife Stadium on September 20, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL season is constantly evolving. Week 4 arrives with more optimism than expected in Chicago after an upset victory of the previously unbeaten Eagles on Monday night. In this weekly series, I’ll feature one player from the Chicago Bears opponent on each side of the ball who I think is integral to their team’s success. Like seasons past, you won’t see any quarterbacks, as the nature of the position always makes them critical for a team’s success. I’ll also try and mix in a few under the radar players from time to time. Let’s start with the New York Jets offensive player that I will be focused on. Offense: Armand Membou, #70 – RT My initial thought was to roll with RB2 Braelon Allen as he is filling in for the injured stud Breece Hall. But knowing how Saquon balled against us last week and Philly still failed to put up more than 7 points, my thought process shifted to the outside weapons. Garrett Wilson is an obvious problem, and without injured first-rounder Omar Cooper Jr. and Adonai Mitchell, their WRs are average at best. That brought me to Tight End Kenyon Sadiq, but our own Mongo Peanut already wrote up an excellent piece on the challenges he will present this week. Considering Sadiq is also Questionable to play in this game due to a leg injury, my focus finally settled on the line where Membou will have to not only lead the charge in the run game, but also protect the edge in the passing game to afford Geno Smith some time to sit back in the pocket and find his weapons. At 22 years of age, Membou is already one of the top RTs in the league – thanks in large part to his pass blocking. Much like our Wright tackle, Membou made a name for himself coming out of the SEC in college where he stonewalled the top pass rushers entering the draft. Unlike Darnell Wright, Membou has yet to develop into the bully in the run game, though he has the size (6’4”, 332lb) and athleticism (4.91 40 – fastest for his size since 2003) to get the job done. Not only will Membou look to keep Montez Sweat and Co. out of the pocket, but he will also be critical in establishing the run against a vulnerable Bears run defense. If he can do those things, Allen should keep the chains moving and Geno should have enough time to pick apart the secondary and get the ball to Wilson and Sadiq. Defense: T’Vondre Sweat, #99 – DT If you thought Membou was big, Sweat is even bigger. At 6’4”, 366 lbs, Sweat is a load in the middle of the defense that will give any interior offensive linemen trouble. Considering Garrett Bradberry struggles against beefier defensive linemen, Sweat could be a wrecking ball in this game. That said, Bradberry had his best game of the season last week against arguably the top DT tandem in the league in Jordan Davis and Jalen Carter. Davis, as a matter of fact, is no small human himself at 6’6”, 336 lb, but is more of a finesse player compared to Sweat. If someone over 330lb can be considered more finesse at anything, but I digress. Regardless of who lines up under center for Chicago, keeping the middle of the pocket clean will be paramount while also opening up holes in the run game for Swift and Monangai to run through. If Sweat can clog those lanes and push the pocket, it will force our QB out of the pocket where top 5 pick David Bailey and proven veteran Will McDonald will surely pounce. It will be hard to miss #99 in this one and if we can render him ineffective, we should successfully control the line of scrimmage and win this game. What about you? Which New York Jets players will you be focused on?

title: Chicago Bears Week 4 Flashbacks: Bengals Blowout, Hester sets a record, and more!
summary: It’s week 4, a week that has seen many a classic Bears games! Luckily we have some hallmark games from the past to uncover today. Climb aboard Gridiron Time Machine for a trip down memory lane! 1.) 1986, Bears @ Bengals: Chicago overwhelms Cincinnati in a 44-7 rout Coming off one of the most dominant […]
full_text: Chicago Bears wide receiver Devin Hester (23) runs back a kick-off return in the second quarter against the Carolina Panthers at Soldier Field in Chicago, Illinois, Sunday, October 2, 2011. The Bears defeated the Panthers 34-29. (Jose M. Osorio/Chicago Tribune/Tribune News Service via Getty Images) It’s week 4, a week that has seen many a classic Bears games! Luckily we have some hallmark games from the past to uncover today. Climb aboard Gridiron Time Machine for a trip down memory lane! 1.) 1986, Bears @ Bengals: Chicago overwhelms Cincinnati in a 44-7 rout Coming off one of the most dominant seasons in NFL history, the 1986 Bears entered Week 4 looking every bit like a team capable of doing it all over again. The unfortunate team standing in their way was the Cincinnati Bengals. Chicago jumped out to a 21-0 first-quarter lead behind a banged up Jim McMahon rushing touchdown and touchdown passes to Walter Payton and Willie Gault. McMahon would add another touchdown pass to Emery Moorehead in the second half, finishing with 211 yards and three scores through the air. Gault was the star through the air, hauling in 174 receiving yards, while the Bears piled up 476 yards of total offense and 222 yards on the ground. The defense was not exactly taking the afternoon off either. Chicago intercepted Boomer Esiason four times and forced five turnovers overall, holding Cincinnati to seven points in a 44-7 blowout. The win moved the defending champions to 4-0, continuing a start in which it looked like the rest of the NFL might once again be playing for second place. That eventually changed, but on this afternoon the Bears looked every bit as terrifying as the team that had just steamrolled its way through 1985. 2.) 2011, Bears vs. Panthers: Forte runs wild and Hester makes history The Bears entered Week 4 at 1-2 and badly needed a win after dropping back-to-back games to the Saints and Packers. Matt Forte and Devin Hester made sure they got one. Forte gashed Carolina from the start, including a 46-yard run on Chicago’s opening possession and a 17-yard touchdown in the second quarter. He would finish with a career-high 205 rushing yards while adding another 23 through the air, accounting for 228 of Chicago’s 317 total yards. Then there was Hester. With Chicago leading 17-10, Hester fielded a punt and raced 69 yards for a touchdown, giving the Bears a 24-10 advantage. It was the 11th punt return touchdown of his career, setting a new NFL record. The defense chipped in as well, with D.J. Moore returning a Cam Newton interception 20 yards for a touchdown in the first quarter (no not THAT D.J. Moore, but it is pretty interesting that Cam Newton has thrown touchdown passes to multiple people named “D.J. Moore). Carolina still piled up a franchise-record 543 yards of offense, but the Bears found enough big plays on defense and special teams to stay in front. Forte helped put the game away with a 40-yard run late in the fourth quarter, and Chicago escaped Soldier Field with a 34-29 victory. It was about as Bears of a victory as you could draw up. Run the football, steal a score on defense, then let Devin Hester do Devin Hester things. 3.) 2018, Bears vs. Buccaneers: Trubisky trounces the Bucs for 6 touchdowns There might not be another game that better sums up the highs of the Mitchell Trubisky era. Through the first three games of the 2018 season, Trubisky had thrown just two touchdowns, and questions were already starting to build about whether Matt Nagy’s new offense was actually going to unlock the second-year quarterback. Then Tampa Bay came to Soldier Field. Trubisky absolutely torched the Buccaneers. He threw five touchdown passes in the first half alone, becoming the first quarterback in Bears history to accomplish that feat. By the time his afternoon was over, Trubisky had completed 19-of-26 passes for 354 yards, six touchdowns and a 154.6 passer rating. Those six touchdowns went to five different receivers, with Tarik Cohen adding 121 receiving yards as the Bears built an absurd 38-3 halftime lead. Never forget when Mitchell Trubisky threw for 6 Touchdowns 🔥 https://t.co/94cvRmzhjG pic.twitter.com/LztG0LzjLg — Bears on Real (@BearsOnReal) May 17, 2025 The defense joined in on the fun against a Tampa Bay offense that entered the week leading the NFL in both total and passing yards. Khalil Mack recorded his fourth straight game with a strip-sack, while Chicago forced three turnovers and sacked Buccaneers quarterbacks four times. Chicago cruised to a 48-10 win, with Trubisky’s six touchdown passes finishing just one shy of Sid Luckman’s franchise record of seven set in 1943. The win moved the Bears to 3-1 heading into their bye week and gave us the first real glimpse of what Nagy’s offense could look like when everything clicked. Unfortunately, six-touchdown games never became the norm. But for one afternoon at Soldier Field, Mitchell Trubisky looked completely unstoppable. Gary Baugher Jr. is a second year contributor to WCG, bringing football insight backed by over 16 years of experience in organized football and more than 30 years as a passionate fan of the game. You can follow him on Twitter at @iamcogs .

title: Is front-office pride endangering yet another Bengals season?
summary: Pride comes before the fall. And if the Cincinnati Bengals keep refusing to make the changes they desperately need, that is exactly what is going to happen. The Bengals need a linebacker who can cover tight ends and running backs. Their pride is keeping them from getting one. Sunday’s 30-27 loss to Pittsburgh put that […]
full_text: Pride comes before the fall. And if the Cincinnati Bengals keep refusing to make the changes they desperately need, that is exactly what is going to happen. The Bengals need a linebacker who can cover tight ends and running backs. Their pride is keeping them from getting one. Sunday’s 30-27 loss to Pittsburgh put that weakness on display again. Aaron Rodgers’ first pass went to running back Jaylen Warren on a short crossing route and became a 30-yard gain. Where was the linebacker? By the end of the afternoon, Warren had three catches for 49 yards. Tight ends Darnell Washington, Pat Freiermuth and Robert Tonyan combined for six receptions and another 99 yards. That is nine catches for 148 yards from running backs and tight ends, which was more than half of Rodgers’ passing yardage. The Bengals cannot keep watching opponents exploit the same weakness and insist the answer is already in the building. Washington delivered the most expensive reminder. With the game tied in the fourth quarter, he turned a reception into a 47-yard gain on the possession that produced Pittsburgh’s winning field goal. Cincinnati needed to get someone on the ground. Instead, a tight end helped move the Steelers into scoring position. Some of that was tackling. Some of it was defending receivers in space. Both require attention, and neither gets corrected by pretending the current personnel simply need more time. A week earlier, Dalton Schultz caught 12 passes for 140 yards against the Bengals. Cincinnati won in Houston, but the result concealed a problem that Pittsburgh brought back into focus. A win does not turn a defensive weakness into a strength. The Bengals have enough evidence. What they need now is the willingness to admit their linebacker room needs help. That admission should not be difficult. Teams make personnel decisions, evaluate the results, and adjust. Bringing in a veteran does not require abandoning young players. It requires acknowledging that development and winning this season have to happen together. Instead, Cincinnati is letting pride protect its decisions while opposing offenses collect the benefits. There are options worth pursuing, starting with Shaq Thompson. Buffalo currently lists him on its practice squad, and PFF’s player page gives him a 69.2 coverage grade for 2025, 14th among 88 qualified linebackers. That is enough of a reason to make a call. Jerome Baker deserves consideration as well. He remains on the latest available free-agent list, and his 69.1 coverage grade last season makes him worth examining, even with the limitation of a smaller workload. Bring him in and find out whether he can help. These players are candidates, and the Bengals have work to do before deciding whether either belongs on their roster. They need to assess health, movement, and the ability to handle the assignments that are causing trouble: carrying a tight end through a route and staying with a running back coming out of the backfield. That work should already be underway. The standard cannot be whether a signing validates the Bengals’ offseason plan. The standard has to be whether it improves their defense. Cincinnati does not need to hand a veteran a starting job or promise him every snap. It needs to create competition for the passing-down assignments its current players are failing to handle consistently. If an available linebacker can do that job better, he should be on the field. Joe Burrow’s prime is too valuable to spend protecting the front office’s pride. The Bengals have a weakness, their opponents know it, and help is worth investigating. Admit the need. Make the calls. Give this team a better chance to win.
author: John Acree

title: Amarius Mims draws strong praise from offensive line guru
summary: If there was a true bright spot that has been consistent throughout the season so far for the Cincinnati Bengals, it would be right tackle Amarius Mims playing practically perfect. Mims has shut down every pass rusher he has gone against so far. That list includes the likes of Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter […]
full_text: If there was a true bright spot that has been consistent throughout the season so far for the Cincinnati Bengals, it would be right tackle Amarius Mims playing practically perfect. Mims has shut down every pass rusher he has gone against so far. That list includes the likes of Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter from the Houston Texans. It also includes T.J. Watt from the game on Sunday with the Pittsburgh Steelers. That performance caught the eye of Brandon Thorn — one of the best offensive linemen evaluators — who has high praise after Mims incredible start, calling him a top 5-to-6 right tackle in the NFL. Counted 12 true drop-back, 1v1 reps from Mims vs. Watt, who was shut down working high-side, down the middle and inside. This is a top 5-6 RT in just his 3rd season 📈📈📈 pic.twitter.com/AVGY5fApQ6 — Brandon Thorn (@BrandonThornNFL) September 28, 2026 “This is a top 5-6 RT in just his 3rd season,” said Thorn. The knock on Mims during the draft process was that he couldn’t stay healthy. That always seemed unfounded considering he never even had a major knee injury. Just some moderate to minor injuries that popped up near the end of his time in college and during the draft process itself. It also created a lack-of-experience concern, but he never had an issue in the SEC. That’s why the Bengals may have gotten the steal of the draft at No. 18 overall in the 2024 NFL Draft. He has hit what many called his high ceiling of potential. Those kinds of picks haven’t always worked out, but it is clear they nailed this one if Mims can stay healthy. The only question that comes now is if he eventually gets moved to left tackle. Orlando Brown Jr. has struggled a bit with some of the quicker rushers in the NFL, and it has showed up quite a few times over the years, but he is far from being an unacceptable starter. It may come down to whether they feel the move can be made, and how much exactly they end up having to pay him when that contract needs to be redone. Because he surely should push for elite tackle money, but left tackle will always get more in that area. That is a long-term discussion, though. We get to enjoy him as an absolute dominant offensive tackle right now.

title: Browns: Would they trade this veteran WR? Should they?
summary: The Cleveland Browns appear to be on the right track at wide receiver. After far too many years of bad draft picks (Jamari Thrash, Michael Woods II, Anthony Schwartz, Antonio Callaway, and Brian Robiskie, to name a few) and ill-conceived trades (Odell Beckham Jr.), general manager Andrew Berry appears to have hit on rookies KC […]
full_text: (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns appear to be on the right track at wide receiver. After far too many years of bad draft picks (Jamari Thrash, Michael Woods II, Anthony Schwartz, Antonio Callaway, and Brian Robiskie, to name a few) and ill-conceived trades (Odell Beckham Jr.), general manager Andrew Berry appears to have hit on rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston. Following Thursday night’s win over the Pittsburgh Steelers, Concepcion is tied for the team lead with 17 receptions, while Boston leads with 284 receiving yards. Together, the rookie duo has combined for 37 percent of the team’s receptions and 50 percent of the team’s receiving yards. Mix in tight end Harold Fannin Jr. (17 receptions and a team-high three receiving touchdowns), and the contributions from running backs Qunshon Judkins and Raheim Sanders (a combined 25 receptions for 169 yards), and that provides quarterback Deshaun Watson with a nice set of tools in the toolbox to work with. What’s that? There is one prominent name missing from the list? Oh right, Jerry Jeudy. The veteran of the group, the 2026 season has been an odd one for Jeudy, who was not targeted at all in the win over Carolina and only once in the victory over Tampa Bay. Jeudy picks up 17 The Browns are looking for the win. @PITvsCLE on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/qnLA8fM4ZE — NFL (@NFL) October 2, 2026 It was turning into another quiet night for Jeudy against the Steelers before he pulled in two passes on Cleveland’s game-winning drive in the fourth quarter. Those receptions brought Jeudy’s season total to five catches for 62 yards. There are a few ways to look at the situation: After posting career highs in receptions (90) and receiving yards (1,229) in 2024, Jeudy dipped to 50 receptions and 602 receiving yards in 2025. His slow start could be a sign that he is in decline. Watson is more focused on distributing the ball to whoever is open, rather than trying to force a pass to one particular player, which means Jeudy’s time will come, as it did in the fourth quarter on Thursday. Boston and Concepcion are simply better options, and the Browns consider Jeudy a role player. Head coach Todd Monken acknowledged that last point in his comments while crediting Jeudy for being there when the team needed him after the game on Thursday: “I’m so happy for Jerry. And it probably wasn’t enough for a game ball, but for a guy that really isn’t starting now, he’s a rotational player, that’s so cool for him. And it’s not easy for a veteran player to have young players kind of beat him out, but we needed it in a big time, and that was a big time catch.” That leads to the question of how much the Browns need Jeudy and whether or not they could look to trade him before the NFL trade deadline on November 10. ESPN’s Dan Graziano highlighted Jeudy as a trade candidate in his latest column on players who could be on the move in the next few weeks: Jeudy is still only 27 years old, and he’s signed through 2027. But the Browns’ wide receiver corps has been taken over by rookies, and Jeudy might no longer fit squarely into the plans. He’s owed about $23 million in salary and bonus for 2027, but it’s not guaranteed, so an acquiring team wouldn’t likely be deterred by that. It is always tricky when people start talking about trades. If Jeudy’s numbers are truly an indication that he is slipping, then why would another team want him? And how much value would the Browns receive for him? But if the numbers are simply based on Watson having better options and Jeudy is still putting in the work and not complaining, then the Browns are likely better off with him on the roster. Especially since they are only four games into the season and injuries are always a concern. Plus, as he showed against the Steelers, Jeudy can still make a play when the team needs him. So Berry may be hesitant to shake things up when the team is winning. What do you think, Browns fans? Would you look for a trade partner for Jeudy, or is he a nice insurance policy to have? Let everyone know in the comments!

It is an unexpected start for many Browns fans, especially after the struggles against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week One. This win makes it the first time the Browns have led in the AFC North since 2021. The Cleveland defense has continued to prove they are a strong unit. This group recorded two interceptions and five sacks in the matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers. They made crucial stops and continued to pressure the opposing offense. The Browns offense has been the biggest surprise of the season thus far. While not perfect, the group has multiple young players who are starting to stand out and show their value. In the matchup against the Steelers in particular, they put 21 points on the board in the second quarter alone, along with putting together the game-winning drive. Rookie Denzel Boston had 89 receiving yards and really stood out. Let me know what you think in the comments – The Browns Are Making Their Presence Felt in the AFC North

title: The Browns in the playoffs? Not so fast
summary: The Cleveland Browns find themselves at 3-1-0 in this young 2026 season. Three comeback wins have been featured so far and show that Cleveland has no quit. The win over division rival Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday Night Football placed the Browns in first place all alone atop the AFC North Division. RELATED: BROWNS WINNING GAMES […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns find themselves at 3-1-0 in this young 2026 season. Three comeback wins have been featured so far and show that Cleveland has no quit. The win over division rival Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday Night Football placed the Browns in first place all alone atop the AFC North Division. RELATED: BROWNS WINNING GAMES BECAUSE OF THE “AND” And that is all well and good. Everyone wants to win games and become fans of something they feel is relevant. It is easier to root for a team that is winning games than to be devoted to a club that continually rests in the basement on an annual basis. With the win, certainly Cleveland will obviously climb in the league power rankings. The league has five undefeated teams going into Week 4, and nine teams that are currently at 2-1-0 that could improve their standing once the smoke from the weekend subsides. Teams that begin their season 3-1-0 have made the playoffs 75% of the time since the NFL expanded its postseason format in 2020. Remember, the consensus for the Browns before the year began was a five-win season, six at most? It is a distinct possibility that Cleveland could be ranked in the Top 10. No, really. There are a few media outlets that are predicting a playoff spot for the Browns. So are numerous Facebook fan pages. Really? Let’s slow this down a bit and be more realistic. Jacob Robinson of The Athletic said this about Cleveland’s sudden ascension: “What about surprise 3-1 teams like these Browns? Projected before the season to win five games, Cleveland had Super Bowl odds of +15000, ranking 28th at the time. This start is very different from most.” For one, it’s just one win. A key division matchup, to be certain, but simply one game on the schedule. There are 13 remaining. Cleveland has beaten the 1-2-0 Carolina Panthers, the 0-3-0 Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and the now 2-2-0 Steelers. Nothing in this grouping screams potential Super Bowl champion. The only good team they faced was the Jacksonville Jaguars, who took Cleveland to the wood shed to the tune of a 34-10 beatdown. There is a saying: “It’s not what you are, but who you’ve played.” Now, don’t get this all wrong; the Browns have the opportunity to gain double-digit wins this year. No, really. Because they were at the bottom of the division last year, they are set up with what is called “the fourth-place schedule” this year. That means they are pitted against the majority of clubs that also finished dead last in their division in 2025. Playing last year’s crappy teams is a wonderful thing. On the schedule are the New York Jets, New Orleans Saints, Tennessee Titans, Las Vegas Raiders, Indianapolis Colts, New York Football Giants, and Atlanta Falcons. Seven wins from this group? Six? Even five victories place Cleveland at eight wins for the year. With seven playoff seeds in the AFC, getting into the postseason will require a minimum of 10 wins. 11 gets you in. But hold the phone. The Houston Texans were expected to be in the AFC Championship Game this year, and yet currently are 0-3-0. The Browns play Houston in Week 10. If Cleveland can split with every team in the division, that is another three wins. The victory over Pittsburgh is a direct indication that this could happen. The Browns are the only team in the division that has never won an AFC North Division crown. Back in the day, they captured the AFC Central many times, but so far, since the realignment, they have never won the division title now called the AFC North. This could happen. This year. And the playoffs could happen as well. Then again, the bottom could fall out. Lord knows the team collects penalties and allows a team like the Steelers to crawl back into the game after building a big lead. Robinson added: “Should we trust Cleveland? Naturally, fans are concerned. These Browns are also different in another way, as they’re 3-1 despite having a negative points margin (minus-14) on the season. But there’s good news there, too. The recent history of 3-1 teams with negative differentials is a reminder that a winning record is all you need.” Last year, the Arizona Cardinals began their season 2-0-0, and everyone started talking playoffs. The Cardinals are a 127-year franchise, and they ended their season 3-14-0. It was the greatest number of losses in a single season in team history. Yet, they began on top of the world. Let’s just enjoy the moment. When the Browns begin beating the really good NFL teams, like the Baltimore Ravens, then let’s start discussing the postseason. What would you put the odds of the Browns making the NFL playoffs this year? Join the conversation!
