title: Cowboys vs Texans: Writer predictions for Week 4
summary: Dallas returns from Brazil looking to respond quickly after the painful 34-31 loss to Baltimore, and the short trip to Houston presents an interesting matchup. The Cowboys are 1-2 but have shown they can move the football consistently, while Houston enters at 0-3 with an offense searching for answers. The problem for Dallas is that […]
full_text: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images Dallas returns from Brazil looking to respond quickly after the painful 34-31 loss to Baltimore, and the short trip to Houston presents an interesting matchup. The Cowboys are 1-2 but have shown they can move the football consistently, while Houston enters at 0-3 with an offense searching for answers. The problem for Dallas is that its defense continues to lose players, meaning this is another game where Dak Prescott and the offense may need to carry a large share of the workload. When Houston has the ball Houston should look at the Dallas defense and see an opportunity to finally get its offense moving. The Texans have averaged only 18 points through three games and managed just 223 total yards in Sunday’s loss to Indianapolis, including 70 on the ground. C.J. Stroud was held to 167 passing yards and sacked three times. Dallas, however, has allowed 1,161 total yards through three games, including 539 on the ground, so Houston has every reason to test a Cowboys defense that has struggled to consistently stop either phase of the offense. The easiest way to do that could be through the running game. David Montgomery and Woody Marks have not produced much behind Houston’s offensive line so far, but Dallas is allowing five yards per rushing attempt. Establishing the run would also help Stroud by creating shorter third downs and opening play-action rather than asking him to repeatedly sit in the pocket behind protection that has been inconsistent. Houston should also use quick passes and screens to prevent Dallas’ defensive front from attacking Stroud freely. When Dallas has the ball Dallas should continue putting the game in Dak Prescott’s hands. Prescott threw for 276 yards against Baltimore, while CeeDee Lamb finished with 112 receiving yards and George Pickens added 82. Even in defeat, Dallas moved the ball consistently and showed that Lamb and Pickens can put enormous pressure on a secondary when Prescott has enough time. Getting that time will be the biggest challenge of the afternoon. Will Anderson Jr. is already becoming one of the league’s most disruptive pass rushers and produced 2.5 sacks, a forced fumble and a recovery against Indianapolis. Danielle Hunter provides another dangerous rusher from the opposite side. Houston forced three turnovers against the Colts and held them to 300 yards, so its 0-3 record should not fool anyone into thinking this is an easy defense to face. Now onto the predictions from your BTB writers… Tom Ryle (1-2) I almost feel like Dallas is facing a trap game, especially with the news Nico Collins is back at practice. However, CJ Stroud is one of the most sacked QBs in the league. I think the Cowboys will get to him a few times and their offense will eliminate at least some of their mistakes. DAL 34, HOU 23 Brandon Loree (2-1) In the battle of Texas, it never feels like the Cowboys are 100% guaranteed to win. The Houston Texans are really struggling to find themselves three games into the season and are desperate for their first win. Their inconsistent offensive line should give Dallas a chance to really get sacks from their edge rushers on CJ Stroud. I think this ends up being a weird game where the Cowboys win 16-12 on one touchdown, and the rest is all field goals. Dyllan Rivers (2-1) While they still have a long way to go, the Cowboys defense has improved each week of the season. That trend will continue this week where we finally see some pressures converted into sacks against a less mobile QB in C.J. Stroud. The offense continues to roll and situational awareness doesn’t blow the whole thing up this time around. Dallas wins at Houston, 30-24 Matt Holleran (3-0) With all the injuries on the defensive side of the ball, I have no confidence in Dallas’ defense showing up on Sunday. If the Cowboys can block up Houston’s defensive front they should be able to move the ball, but slowing down their talented pass rush will be a tough test. I see this being a close game but the Texans’ defense proves to be the difference maker. Will Anderson gets a game-ending strip sack as Dallas falls to 1-3. Give me the Texans, 24-23. Mike Poland (1-2) I know, I know, my pure unfiltered optimism got me in trouble last week thinking Dallas would get the win in Brazil, but it almost happened! So I’m sticking with my unrelenting optimistic approach and say Dallas win this week. Houston is 0-3 on the year, and worse is they’re 0-2 at home. That means all the pressure is on them to deliver a win here. Dallas just needs to play smart, simple football to keep Houston chasing and make them one dimensional on both sides of the ball. Give me Dallas to win 31-20.
author: Mike Poland

title: The one matchup the Cowboys have to win on Sunday
summary: Similar to what we talked about in week two against the Washington Commanders, it’s hard to imagine calling a week four game a “must win” game, but this game certainly feels like it. The Cowboys sit in third in the division at 1-2. The Philadelphia Eagles take on the Los Angeles Rams this weekend, the […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images | Getty Images Similar to what we talked about in week two against the Washington Commanders, it’s hard to imagine calling a week four game a “must win” game, but this game certainly feels like it. The Cowboys sit in third in the division at 1-2. The Philadelphia Eagles take on the Los Angeles Rams this weekend, the New York Giants are playing the Arizona Cardinals, and the Washington Commanders do battle with the Indianapolis Colts. With a win in Houston, the Cowboys could potentially make up some ground in the division and gain a ton of momentum heading into week five. In order to do so, the Cowboys offensive line is going to have to show up. Despite the Texans struggles on defense this year (19th in EPA/play) the Houston pass rush is still near the top of the league. Will Anderson is playing like the best defensive end in the National Football League, ranking in the top 10 in both pass rush win rate and run stop win rate. Anderson moves around quite a bit in the Texans defense, but has played more on the left side of the defense through three games. That puts him across from Terence Steele on a majority of his snaps, making this a major mismatch for the Cowboys offense. While most of the attention will be put on slowing down Will Anderson, his running mate Danielle Hunter is no easy matchup either for Tyler Guyton. Both Hunter and Anderson can change games as pass rushers and run defenders, and despite the Texans 0-3 record and slower start to the year on defense, they have completely wrecked games in the 2026 season. While we are expected to see a heavy dosage of Anderson and Hunter (both playing right around 80% of the defensive snaps), old friend Jadaveon Clowney has been getting into the rotation as well and has flashed a similar skillset he showed with the Cowboys in 2025. He is questionable so we don’t know if he’ll play or not. With Anderson and Hunter being the workhorses up front for the Texans, the Cowboys need to be able to wear them down with long drives and do their best to stay out of third-and-long situations. Given the Texans ability to get after Dak Prescott, expect the ball to come out quick on early downs, with extra-men allocated to protection (limiting their pass catchers) when they decide to take their shot or they face third-and-longs. Similar to the week one game against the New York Giants, the Cowboys offensive tackles could make or break this game for the Cowboys. The Texans run defense has been stout through three weeks, so the Cowboys passing offense will likely need to have a big-game in order to come out victorious in a monster in-state week four matchup.

full_text: Photo by MAURO PIMENTEL / AFP via Getty Images | AFP via Getty Images We’ve mostly gotten over our disappointment and rage at losing in the last seconds to the Baltimore Ravens. The Dallas Cowboys had a game in hand, but let it slip away with some really questionable play-calling from head coach Brian Schottenheimer. After the game, the coach admitted making mistakes and vowed to learn and improve going forward. We all like to hear that optimism, but what is the reality from Schottenheimer? Earlier this week we asked you to grade coach Schottenheimer’s tenure in Dallas. Not just the Ravens game, but what he has accomplished since he was hired in 2025 as head coach. You guys voted and basically gave him a ’C/D’ grade. ‘C’ got 37% of the vote while ‘D’ got 34%. Looks like coach has some work to do, and he can start against the Houston Texans who are 3-point favorites over Dallas despite being 0-3. title: 4 Cowboys to buy/sell in Week 4 vs the Texans
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are heading into Week 4 with a 1-2 record, coming off a frustrating loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Brazil. They now face a Houston Texans team that is 0-3 but has plenty of talent on both sides of the football. There are a few players and position groups worth keeping an […]
full_text: Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are heading into Week 4 with a 1-2 record, coming off a frustrating loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Brazil. They now face a Houston Texans team that is 0-3 but has plenty of talent on both sides of the football. There are a few players and position groups worth keeping an eye on Sunday, but four stand out in particular. Here is this week’s buy/sell list. Buy: WR CeeDee Lamb It is getting harder to come up with reasons not to buy CeeDee Lamb right now. Through three games, Lamb has caught 20 passes for 309 yards and three touchdowns, averaging 15.5 yards per reception. He has also been targeted 25 times, giving him an 80% catch rate and making him one of the most consistently involved players in the Cowboys’ passing game. More importantly, Lamb has shown that he can produce regardless of what the Cowboys’ offense asks him to do. He had 69 yards and a touchdown against the Giants, exploded for 153 yards and two touchdowns against Washington and then added 112 yards against Baltimore. That last performance came in a game where Dallas was dealing with an unusual international environment and eventually lost despite putting up 415 total yards. Now Lamb gets a Houston defense that has allowed opponents to move the ball through the air while also dealing with an offense that has struggled to keep games under control. The Texans have allowed 326 yards per game through three weeks, and their defense has been much more effective at creating pressure than forcing turnovers. Houston also has Derek Stingley Jr., which makes this a legitimate matchup for Lamb rather than a situation where he should simply be expected to dominate because of the opposing secondary. Dallas needs its best offensive player to continue being its best offensive player, and there is little reason through three weeks to believe Lamb is slowing down. If Houston focuses too much attention on him, George Pickens, Jake Ferguson and the rest of the passing game should have opportunities. If Houston chooses to play Lamb straight up, Dallas has already shown that Prescott is willing to keep feeding him. Lamb has been too productive and too involved to not buy right now. DAK TO CEEDEE FOR 50 @BALvsDAL on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/LBD7eqKJ5t — NFL (@NFL) September 27, 2026 Sell: QB Dak Prescott Selling Dak Prescott this week does not mean expecting him to play poorly. It is more a reflection that this is probably one of the more difficult environments Dallas’ quarterback has faced so far this season. Prescott has been very good through three games. He has completed 73 of 105 passes for 730 yards, seven touchdowns and one interception, giving him a 69.5% completion rate and a 107.2 passer rating. Those are excellent numbers, and they are a big reason Dallas has been able to score 29.3 points per game despite its 1-2 record. The problem is that Houston presents a much different challenge than the defenses Dallas has faced recently. The Texans have already recorded 11 sacks through three games, which ranks fourth in the NFL, while Dallas has allowed only three sacks. Houston’s ability to generate pressure without needing to completely abandon coverage is what makes this matchup particularly interesting for Prescott. Will Anderson Jr. has been at the center of that pass rush, and Houston also has Danielle Hunter and other experienced pieces capable of creating pressure from different spots.That means Prescott may not have the same time to operate that he has enjoyed during portions of the first three weeks. The other reason to sell Prescott this week is simply that the Texans’ defense is good enough to force Dallas into some uncomfortable situations. If the Cowboys fall behind early, Houston’s pass rush could become even more important because Dallas would have fewer opportunities to lean on Javonte Williams and the running game. Again, this isn’t a prediction that Dak is going to have a bad game. It is simply a recognition that the combination of Houston’s defensive front and the Texans’ ability to pressure the quarterback makes this a week where Prescott may have to work considerably harder for the same level of production he has produced during the first three games. If he still puts up 300 yards and three touchdowns, so be it. But this feels like a week to temper expectations, even if Lamb has a great game, that could be the only avenue for consistent production against a still fierce defense. Buy: CB Joey Porter Jr. There is obviously some projection involved here because Joey Porter Jr. has not played a game for the Cowboys yet or any game in 2026 for that matter. But sometimes a team makes an addition that changes the way you view an entire position group, and this feels like one of those moves. Dallas acquired Porter from Pittsburgh on Wednesday in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick. The 26-year-old corner has 41 career starts across 47 games, along with 165 tackles, 31 pass breakups and three interceptions in his first three seasons. The Cowboys did not make this move because they were satisfied with their cornerback room. They made it because injuries and inconsistent play had created a legitimate problem on the outside, with Cobie Durant dealing with a hamstring issue and Shavon Revel appearing on the injury report with knee and ankle concerns. Porter should immediately give Dallas something it has been missing: a proven outside corner with the size, physicality and experience to handle quality receivers without requiring the defense to constantly manufacture help. And, frankly, the talent gap between Porter and what Dallas has had available at corner makes this an easy buy. That does not mean Porter is guaranteed to walk into Houston and shut down Nico Collins or whoever else the Texans put across from him. He has had only a few days to learn Christian Parker’s defense, and communication is particularly important for a secondary that has already had its share of issues. But Porter is talented enough that he should be able to make an impact even while learning the finer details of the scheme. The Cowboys don’t need him to become an All-Pro on Sunday. They need him to be better than what they had available before the trade, and given Porter’s experience and track record, there is a strong reason to believe he can be. 2025 Joey Porter Jr. Welcome to the Dallas Cowboys. pic.twitter.com/tvZ7Ty8rxO — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) October 1, 2026 Sell: Cowboys pass rush This unit is becoming increasingly difficult to defend. Through three games, the Cowboys have recorded two sacks. That’s it. Two sacks in three games is tied for 30th in the NFL, while Houston has already produced 11. Dallas also has zero interceptions, meaning the defense has not been creating many negative plays through either pressure or takeaways. The Cowboys knew coming into this season that the pass rush would be one of the biggest questions on the roster. Rashan Gary was brought in to help replace some of the production lost when Micah Parsons was traded, while Donovan Ezeiruaku and the rest of the young edge group were expected to develop into meaningful contributors. Three games into the season, that group has not done enough. This isn’t simply about the sack total, either. Sacks are obviously the most visible measurement of a pass rush, but a defense can still be effective without piling up sacks if it consistently pressures quarterbacks, forces hurried throws and creates opportunities for the secondary. Dallas has not consistently done that, and that becomes particularly concerning against Houston because C.J. Stroud has thrown for 794 yards through three games without an interception. The Texans have struggled to turn those passing yards into enough points, but Stroud has shown that he can make defenses pay when he has time to operate. The Cowboys have just acquired Porter, which should…

title: College football’s top Cowboys draft targets in Week 5
summary: It’s never too early to prep your draft board as we look at the best college football matchups, where a future prospect lurks that could be on the Cowboys radar.  Alabama at Mississippi State Alabama and Mississippi State enter this game with 4-0 records, making their first meeting in three seasons much more interesting than […]
full_text: Photo by Jason Clark/Getty Images | Getty Images It’s never too early to prep your draft board as we look at the best college football matchups, where a future prospect lurks that could be on the Cowboys radar. Alabama at Mississippi State Alabama and Mississippi State enter this game with 4-0 records, making their first meeting in three seasons much more interesting than the rivalry’s recent history would suggest. Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell is coming off his best performance of the year, while Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor has thrown 14 touchdowns. That should place both secondaries under genuine pressure. Alabama: Zabien Brown, Cornerback Brown entered the season as one of the leading cornerbacks in the 2027 class and has done little to weaken that reputation. His game is built around patience and route recognition. Brown rarely panics when a receiver gains a small advantage early in the route. He stays close to the receiver’s hip and uses his timing to challenge the ball at the catch point. He is comfortable in press coverage but does not need to place both hands on a receiver to remain connected. Why The Cowboys Care Dallas’ secondary has already been stretched by injuries. DaRon Bland has been the only healthy established starting corner at times, while Shavon Revel Jr. has has injury issues. Caleb Downs can cover the slot, but his versatility is most valuable when the coaching staff is free to move him rather than using him to solve one permanent problem. And we have no idea what the future of Joey Porter Jr. in Dallas will be. Brown projects as an outside corner who could handle difficult assignments without constant safety help. His ability to play both man and zone coverage would suit Christian Parker’s defence, and his calm technique could bring stability to a group that has been forced to change combinations too often. Mississippi State: Kelley Jones, Cornerback Jones is one of the most physically unusual cornerbacks in the class. At 6-foot-4, he has the length of a safety while retaining the movement skills to remain outside. He became a full-time starter in 2025 and finished second in the SEC with 11 passes defended. That length changes the space available to a receiver. Jones can disrupt a release at the line of scrimmage and reach passes that would be safe against a smaller defender. He is at his best when he can stay square early and use the boundary as an additional defender. Why The Cowboys Care Jones offers the size and developmental upside Dallas has often valued at cornerback. Revel gives the Cowboys one long outside defender, but his injury history makes it risky to assume the position is settled. Porter Jr. may be here past this season, or he may not. Adding Jones would allow Dallas to match bigger receivers without asking Downs or a safety to handle the assignment. He may also be more realistic for the Cowboys than Brown. Jones has first-round physical traits, but his tackling and zone technique could keep him available beyond the opening round. Dallas could use a second-day selection on a corner with starter potential, then give Parker and the defensive staff time to improve the details of his game. Ohio State at Iowa Ohio State travels to Kinnick Stadium for its first road conference game against an Iowa team coming off a dramatic victory at Michigan. It is the first meeting between these programs since 2006 in which both have been ranked inside the AP top 15. Iowa’s offensive line will try to control the game and protect quarterback Hank Brown, while Ohio State’s defensive front must respond after allowing Illinois to run for 199 yards last week. Ohio State: Kenyatta Jackson Jr., Edge Rusher Jackson is a fifth-year senior with an NFL frame at 6-foot-6 and 263 pounds. He recorded 11 tackles for loss and 6.5 sacks in 14 games for Ohio State’s top-ranked defence in 2025, then returned for another season and was voted a team captain. His length and first-step quickness give offensive tackles two problems to solve. Jackson can threaten the outside shoulder and then convert speed into power. He can also use his reach to keep his chest clean and set a firm edge against the run. That combination makes him more complete than a pass-rush specialist who must leave the field on early downs. Why The Cowboys Care Dallas has invested heavily at edge rusher but so far this season that unit has only registered two sacks. Pass-rush depth remains valuable because the best defensive fronts rotate several players and create pressure without relying on one star. Jackson would give the Cowboys a long, powerful defender capable of playing in an even front or standing outside the tackle. He could enter the rotation rather than being forced to start immediately, contribute against the run and develop his counter moves behind experienced players. Iowa: Trevor Lauck, Offensive Tackle Lauck is a 6-foot-5, 314-pound left tackle who became a full-time starter in 2025. He allowed only six pressures and no sacks across 303 pass-blocking snaps during that first season in the lineup, helping Iowa win the Joe Moore Award as the nation’s best offensive line. He wins with control rather than spectacular athleticism. Lauck keeps his weight underneath him and mirrors defenders without crossing his feet. His hands arrive with purpose, and once he establishes his grip he is difficult to separate from. In the running game he plays with leverage. Why The Cowboys Care Offensive tackle remains unsettled in Dallas. Terence Steele’s future is wildly uncertain and rookie Drew Shelton provides a depth option, but the Cowboys should not assume that the long-term answer is Shelton right now. Lauck could compete at tackle without requiring the coaching staff to rebuild his technique. His experience in Iowa’s physical running game would fit an offence that wants to remain balanced, and his disciplined pass protection would help reduce the quick losses that place Dak Prescott under immediate pressure.

title: Broncos defense faces another major challenge in San Francisco offense
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! Another week, another test for the Denver Broncos defense. While it hasn’t been pretty at times for this typically dominant unit, similar to Bo Nix and the offense, it finds a way to make the plays when it matters most. In the comeback win over the Los Angeles Rams, we saw […]
full_text: DENVER , CO - SEPTEMBER 27: Talanoa Hufanga (9) of the Denver Broncos sacks Matthew Stafford (9) of the Los Angeles Rams during the fourth quarter of the Broncos' 30-26 win at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado on Sunday, September 27, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! Another week, another test for the Denver Broncos defense. While it hasn’t been pretty at times for this typically dominant unit, similar to Bo Nix and the offense, it finds a way to make the plays when it matters most. In the comeback win over the Los Angeles Rams, we saw that in spades late in the game, especially from safety Talanoa Hufanga. The stats may not look pretty at the moment, but the Broncos bend but don’t break. The fact that the defense held Matthew Stafford and the Rams to field goals is a huge reason Denver was still in the game. Now comes Brock Purdy, Christian McCaffrey, and Kyle Shanahan’s San Francisco 49ers offense. Through the first three games, this unit is clicking on all cylinders right now. For the Broncos to get the road upset today, the defense will have to make plays and get stops. “They have a good thing going,” Broncos cornerback Pat Surtain II said to the media earlier this week. “They’re off to a hot start offensively. I think they lead the league in third-down percentage. They throw a lot of stuff at you offensively. It starts with McCaffrey in the backfield, and what he is able to do not only in the run game, but in the pass game as well. He’s definitely a threat coming out of the backfield. “Then you have (tight end George) Kittle, and (receiver) Deebo (Samuel Sr.) and all of those guys making plays for them. They also have good perimeter players. It will be a good challenge on the horizon for us. It’s the same system that we’ve been facing these past two weeks, that same Shanahan and (Rams head coach Sean) McVay system. We just have to be ready and understand how they will try to attack us.” Ready for a tough test on the road. 😤 #DENvsSF pic.twitter.com/zgsUSDzwDR — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) October 3, 2026 In those first three games, Purdy has yet to be sacked. On top of finding a way to contain McCaffrey in both the running and passing game, getting pressure on Purdy is paramount. However, the key is not to lose containment on the pocket since he can beat defenses with his legs. “He’s playing at a real high level, very decisive,” Broncos head coach Sean Payton said to the media earlier this week. “You never feel … He’s through his progressions fast. Kyle and those guys have done a great job, whether he’s under center or in the gun. The mix of run, play, pass, and dropback is impressive. You see in three weeks, not only no sacks, first in third down, first in red zone, very efficient. He’s making all the throws.” The biggest challenge for the Broncos defense is McCaffrey and the San Francisco running game. Given Denver’s struggles in the Monday Night Football opener against Kenneth Walker III, you may start to twitch at the thought of this game. The Broncos have to control the line of scrimmage and tackle. “He is a Hall of Fame player, and he’s still playing really well, not just in the running game, but in the passing game,” Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph said to the media earlier this week. “I think the third downs, he’s the leading receiver in the first couple breaks. So that’s always tough to have a plan to cover a runner on third downs. Again, they do a great job with scheme to free him up and to get him on those matchups they like. So it’s our job to kind of find the right matchup and have the right calls intact to leverage him. “With bringing Deebo back to San Fran, they do a great job of kind of swapping those guys. Deebo’s the halfback sometimes; he’s the receiver. So to adjust your coverages and adjust your fronts accordingly to those formations is going to be key for us to win this game. It goes through him obviously, and he’s a fabulous player.” Added Payton: “He does so many things well. His football I.Q. is high, his skill set as a receiver, as a runner, all the things that you’re looking for in a good football player, but a really good running back. A lot of it goes through him. When we talk about it, he has those Joker traits, and you wouldn’t just … elite at running, but also receiving, and feel relative to what they’re asking him to do.” Then, if the Denver defense can force turnovers and steal some possessions for Nix and the offense, that’s a recipe for a victory today. Just as Hufana did against the Rams, which has been the priority for him and the defense since the offseason. “I think everyone talked about it in general,” Hufanga said to the media. “That is more of a self-reflection. I went back and watched every single snap of every single game. I left a lot out there last year, so for this year, it was a real attack on what I wanted to get done. I spent a lot of time on the JUGS (machine) out here and inside, and I’ve still dropped a few. “It’s not the most exciting part when you have two that you think can really change the game early on and not put us in that spot. But to be able to finish it out during a time where I haven’t really caught anything yet as a Bronco, it definitely felt pretty good.” Broncos links

title: Ultimate Fan: Defensive pressure is the key
summary: Ultimate Fans, it seems as though Broncos Country has been rewarded for its devotion to this team with two — TWO — thrilling comeback victories. I have said it so many times on MHR throughout the years, but nothing feels better than a fourth-quarter comeback win in the final seconds, especially on a big final […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - OCTOBER 27: Denver Broncos defensive end Zach Allen (99) and linebacker Nik Bonitto (15) have a word on defense in the fourth quarter during a game between the Carolina Panthers and the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on October 27, 2024 in Denver, Colorado. I have said it so many times on MHR throughout the years, but nothing feels better than a fourth-quarter comeback win in the final seconds, especially on a big final play. Hufanga’s interception in the end zone to seal the Broncos’ come-from-behind win over the Rams gave me John Mobley SB32 vibes, and I always love to be reminded of that. So the question is whether we will be rewarded again this week? Either way, we are being rewarded right now with this UFG. EmpeyFM is not only a new addition to the UFG crowd, he’s a young and relatively green fan of the Orange and Blue. So give him a welcome to Broncos Country and enjoy this preview that, of course, predicts a win! GO BRONCOS! Ready for a tough test on the road. 😤 #DENvsSF pic.twitter.com/zgsUSDzwDR — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) October 3, 2026 Week 4: Broncos at Niners MHR – For the second week in a row, the Broncos waited until the second half – and mostly the fourth quarter – to get hot. How mad were you watching the first half and how nervous/excited were you watching the second half? EmpeyFM: I was certainly frustrated watching the first half! That being said…I also certainly thought they would come back! I wasn’t very nervous for most of the second half (until the Rams got down to the 19 to perform an… idk… ordinary prayer?). I WAS very excited to see Hufanga catch some picks!! AND house one! MHR – Davis Webb says Denver needs to run with more “conviction,” and Sean Payton admits the ground game hasn’t been good enough in the first half of any game this year. Do the Broncos have the personnel on the field and on the sidelines to make this run game legit ? EmpeyFM: Silly rabbit, running is for the weak! I kid; I do think they have the line and backs to do it, but I think this team will always be pass-first as long as Sean is somewhat involved. I don’t think they can be as good as the top running teams, but certainly effective enough to get the safeties to come down. MHR – Bo Nix has been the leading hero in the comeback wins, but he has had some costly turnovers. Against the Niners, a team averaging almost 33 points a game, the Broncos can’t afford a turnover that will give up points and make it too easy for Brock Purdy & Co. on a short field. How confident are you that Nix and the offense can get a fast start and stay out in front of Purdy and his offense? If the Broncos are playing catch-up, can the fourth quarter heroics happen a third week in a row? EmpeyFM: Unfortunately I cannot in good faith predict a fast start… but I can predict a jogging start! Perhaps not enough to stay in front of the ‘9ers, but at least be a score behind them. If they are playing catch-up like they were against the Rams, they will lose this game. If they are playing catch-up down a field goal or TD, they can – and WILL – win this game! MHR – What are your thoughts on the offensive line? In Week 1, Nix seemed to be running for his life most of the game, and while that has improved, the Broncos’ running game has not yet taken off this season. With a guy like Fred Warner on the other side, how crucial is O-line play this Sunday? Empey FM: I think the right (and center…) of the line is the weakest link. I have seen wayyy too much of McGlinchey getting beat, or Powers not going to the right guy. However, Nix hasn’t had super great pocket presence either at times, so! O-line play is always crucial, and it very much will be this week as well. I need BLOCKS! I need no GARRETT HOLDS… or MIKE MCFLINCHEY! I think this will be the point where they start to get things going, since they had so few preseason snaps. MHR – Jaylen Waddle didn’t produce many fireworks last week, but he did have one elite catch at a crucial moment to get a very necessary two-point conversion. What are your expectations for him on Sunday? Empey FM: I expect him to catch any ball that isn’t thrown at his feet! He has been disappointing to this point, but man is he a play machine when he does catch in front of the LOS! The flashes are at least there, so I think it should only become better as the season wears on. As for this game specifically, I could see a three-reception, 30 to 50-yard type game, maybe even a similar statline to last week. MHR – When the ball isn’t going to Waddle or Courtland Sutton, Nix has a slew of pass catchers, from Pat Bryant and Troy Franklin to Nate Adkins and Evan Engram, to choose from. How important is it to spread the ball around to keep defenses honest? Who gets the most targets, yards and scores on Sunday? Empey FM: It is integral! Nix should be throwing to anyone that’s open! I think Sutton and Waddle get the most targets, as that has been the trend, but I think the other receivers will be overall more “productive” than those two. I am going to go with Sutton and Engram catching a TD this week. From The Insiders on @nflnetwork : In #Broncos – #49ers , how well SF can protect Brock Purdy will go a long way in deciding the game. pic.twitter.com/sPVrcb1RYN — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 2, 2026 MHR – Brock Purdy has a 133.1 passer rating, nine touchdowns, one interception, and hasn’t been sacked. The Niners are the first team in 12 years to go three games without allowing a sack. The Broncos are still without Jonathon Cooper and haven’t had as much sack success in the first three games. Can that change this Sunday? How important is Nik Bonitto? EmpeyFM: Sacks are a fact of life, and I don’t think the ‘9ers have faced the greatest of d-lines or pass rushers, but obviously it is still very impressive and worth considering. I think that can absolutely change. I don’t think they’ll tally more than 3, but I have to think they’ll get him once, even if it’s in the last moments of the game. Nik Bonitto is important no doubt, but the group as a whole is a more important factor. If Nik is the only guy getting pressure I will be very very worried. As long as they can get pressure and tackle whoever has the ball, I think things will be OK. MHR – Which Niners’ offensive player – Brock Purdy, Christian McCaffrey or Geoge Kittle – scares you the most for our defense? EmpeyFM: All of them equally, so far as they are all effective guys to lean on. Especially if McCaffrey gets involved in the pass game… oh god! Singleton will still be turning around as he reaches the endzone! They are all extremely effective, so I hope VJ has a killer gameplan for whatever situations they are thrown in. Almost like that’s his job… MHR – Which ONE player on offense and defense has to be an MVP on Sunday for this game to end with a check in the W column? EmpeyFM: Nix and Allen! Nix is the guy who gets the ball to its destination, so if he’s bad at that…then things will go south. Allen is a force, and when he’s not getting held, he WILL make it to the QB. If those two guys are effective, there’s no reason they can’t beat the 49ers. MHR – What is one word to describe the season so far? For the for this team for the rest of the season? EmpeyFM: So far…“ugh.” For the rest of the season? I hope it’s, “Yay!” #BoNix weighed in on having a more balanced offense. Is this the week the #Broncos turn the page and figure it out? 🤔 pic.twitter.com/R8D29uV11q — Mile High Huddle (@MileHighHuddle) October 2, 2026 Predictions Stats for BO NIX? 18/25 completions, 287 yards, 2 TDs Stats for each Broncos RB? Dobbins: 8 carries, 36 yards; Harvey: 9 carries, 73 yards, 4 receptions, 25 yards, 1 TD; Badie: 2 carries, 3 yards, 1 reception, 4 yards Number of yards…

title: Broncos vs. 49ers: 3 Players to Watch in Week 4
summary: The Denver Broncos battle the undefeated San Francisco 49ers on Sunday. Riding the highs of back-to-back comebacks, the Broncos are in pursuit of a third straight win. However, the 49ers present a big challenge for Denver given how good they are on both sides of the ball. In order to achieve a key road victory, […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - SEPTEMBER 14: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs throws a pass against Jonah Elliss #52 of the Denver Broncos during the third quarter in the game at Arrowhead Stadium on September 14, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos battle the undefeated San Francisco 49ers on Sunday. Riding the highs of back-to-back comebacks, the Broncos are in pursuit of a third straight win. However, the 49ers present a big challenge for Denver given how good they are on both sides of the ball. In order to achieve a key road victory, these three players will need to perform at a high level. Bo Nix — Quarterback Bo Nix boasts a good start to his career. With 26 wins, a dozen game winning drives, and ten fourth quarter comebacks, Nix has certainly outperformed his 2024 NFL Draft peers at the position. He’s arguably the comeback king of the NFL, but fans across Broncos Country are still waiting for more consistency and better starts to games. I have no doubt a much more consistent rushing attack would benefit the third-year signal caller. However, he simply has to play better. This year, there has been significant regression with Nix’s first and third down passing. Last season, Nix did very well on first downs, but this year’s output is less than optimal. Third-and-short to third-and-medium range passing situations continue to be an issue as well. Under the guidance of Raheem Morris, the 49ers sport a sound zone-heavy defense that has done a good job of limiting the impact of opposing offenses thus far. They are winning on early downs. They have playmakers that can cover a lot of ground and do well erasing opportunities in down the field and over the middle. I’ll be watching how Nix performs closely on Sunday—he has to have a good start and be a lot more consistent. Jonah Elliss — Edge Rusher With Jonathon Cooper sidelined to begin the season on the NFL Commissioner’s Exempt list, the Broncos have been banking on the progression and development of edge rusher Jonah Elliss . The former third-round pick has a significant increase in snaps at nearly 65-percent of the defense’s total—up from 38-percent his first two seasons in Denver. Unfortunately, through three games Elliss has struggled a fair bit. He doesn’t have a sack and has registered just two hurries and five pressures. We are seeing a significant drop off in hurry and pressure rate. Additionally, containment and setting the edge has been an issue for the former Utah standout. Though I’ll admit that issue hasn’t just been singular to him. Nobody has been able to sack Brock Purdy thus far. Moreover, the 49ers have one of the best rushing attacks in the league. Will this be the week Elliss steps up and makes some big plays on defense? Denver will need him to play at a high level to keep Purdy, Christian McCaffrey, and Kaelon Black in check. Alex Singleton — Inside Linebacker One player I have major concerns about this game is inside linebacker Alex Singleton. I felt Singleton had a rebound performance in Week 2 against the Jacksonville Jaguars. However, I was less than impressed with his outing against the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday Night Football . The eighth-year pro has 32 tackles on the season. Though none of them are for loss and he is already credited with 8 missed tackles. Moreover, #49’s numbers in coverage don’t look particular good either. That may be a problem going up against a 49ers team that runs the ball well and is extremely efficient through the air. 49ers Head Coach Kyle Shanahan is a master at finding matchups against opposing defenses that play to his advantage. I have a feeling Shanahan has drawn up a handful of plays that feature players like Christian McCaffrey or George Kittle attempting to expose Singleton’s deficiencies. Alongside the aforementioned Elliss, he is another defender I’ll be keeping close tabs on Sunday.

title: Future Broncos: 3 Prospects to Watch in Week 5 of NCAA Football Season
summary: Week 5 of the NCAA football season is here. That means another installment of Future Broncos. Here are three players Broncos Country should keep their eyes on in today’s action-packed slate of games. LJ Martin — Running Back — BYU One position I haven’t discussed any prospects at thus far is running back. Over the […]
full_text: COLLEGE STATION, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 12: Reed Harris #3 of the Arizona State Sun Devils signals first down after play during the first half of a game against the Texas A&M Aggies at Kyle Field on September 12, 2026 in College Station, Texas. (Photo by Joe Buvid/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images Week 5 of the NCAA football season is here. That means another installment of Future Broncos . Here are three players Broncos Country should keep their eyes on in today’s action-packed slate of games. LJ Martin — Running Back — BYU One position I haven’t discussed any prospects at thus far is running back. Over the past two drafts, the Broncos have made investments in RJ Harvey and Jonah Coleman. They also re-upped J.K. Dobbins to a two-year deal, but he hasn’t looked as explosive as he did in the first part of their 2025 gridiron campaign. I think any fan would admit Denver has issues running the ball to start the season. For me, it’s still a relatively mild concern, but definitely not a top-tier need that has to be addressed. I’m not arguing for an early investment at running back. However, a certain prospect I feel would provide an immediate boost to Denver’s rushing woes is BYU senior LJ Martin. I discussed him last year , but he opted to return for his fourth and final season with the Cougars. Martin is coming off an impressive junior campaign where he had 236 rushes for 1,305 yards and 12 touchdowns. He also was a viable receiver out of the backfield hauling in 36 catches for 255 yards. At 6’2” and 220 pounds, Martin is one of the most physical runners in this year’s class at the position group. A throwback runner that wins in between the tackles and gets downhill quickly, Martin has routinely been amongst the best in the nation gaining yards after contact and forcing missed tackles. He doesn’t have elite athleticism or breakaway speed, but his strengths are extremely enticing. There is a long way to go in the season, but I think he could be a Top 100 pick next April. Whether or not Denver has interest remains to be seen, but if their stable of backs continues to struggle, I’m guessing they will be intrigued by the BYU standout. You can catch Martin and the tenth ranked Cougars this evening going up against TCU on the road. Reed Harris — Wide Receiver — Arizona State A few weeks ago, I discussed Rutgers wideout K.J. Duff. The reason for doing so was to find a prospect at the X position for Denver given Courtland Sutton’s age and salary cap situation. As the collegiate season continues, I’ll keep my eyes peeled on prospects that line up with that. Arizona State’s Reed Harris fits the bill. Harris started his career at Boston College back in 2023. He didn’t play much as a freshman but became a full-time starter for the Eagles in 2024 and hauled in 17 receptions for 481 yards and four touchdowns. Yes, you read that right. That’s a 28.6 yard per catch average. In 2025, he notched 39 catches for 673 yards and five touchdowns. For his senior season, he transferred to Arizona State to play for the Sun Devils. Through three games, the wideout has 19 catches for 374 yards and 5 touchdowns and is on pace to break all his collegiate high totals. He is big at 6’5” and 220 pounds and has sneaky agility for a guy his size and the ability to dominate with contested catches. Overall, Harris is just an explosive playmaker with great hands and quality traits. That’s worth monitoring as the season progresses. Everyone knows Head Coach Sean Payton loves big wide receivers. I’m sure once he gets to the prospect evaluation process, he will be a big fan of #3. You can catch Harris in action late this evening when the Sun Devils host Baylor. Quincy Rhodes Jr. — Defensive End — Arkansas The Broncos have invested multiple Day 2 selections the past two drafts to select Sai’vion Jones and Tyler Onyedim to add to their defensive front seven. It’s still early in their careers, but we honestly haven’t seen anything at all from them to date. That’s a little bit worrisome even with Denver’s depth at the position group. A player I was high on last year, but also opted to return to college for his senior season was Arkansas defensive end Quincy Rhodes Jr . At 6’6″ and 275 pounds, Rhodes boasts tantalizing size and an elite wingspan that helps him with his pass rush and getting after opposing quarterbacks. Last season, he led the Razorbacks with 8 sacks and 15.5 tackles for loss—proving he is a disruptive force against the run and the pass. His alignment versatility is one of the reasons I like him as a fit for Denver in Vance Joseph’s defense. He has played all over Arkansas’ defensive front and been extremely disruptive. Rhodes still isn’t the sum of all his parts, but he has elite physical traits that are worth betting on. So far, he already has two sacks on the season. If he continues to develop, he seems like an easy bet to hear his name called in the Top 64 picks next April. I can imagine a lot of NFL defensive line coaches pounding the table for a prospect who has a lot of untapped potential. You can catch Rhodes in action this evening when the Razorbacks head on the road to face Texas A&M in an SEC matchup.

title: Sean Payton gives high praise for 49ers coaching staff ahead of Week 4 matchup
summary: After decades of coaching in the National Football League, Denver Broncos Head Coach Sean Payton has seen a lot of coaches come and go. During his time with the New Orleans Saints in the NFC South—Payton became quite familiar with Kyle Shanahan and Raheem Morris—who will be leading the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday. Those […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - AUGUST 9: Head Coach Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers with Head Coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos after the game at Levi's Stadium on August 9, 2025 in Santa Clara, California. The Broncos defeated the 49ers 30-9. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images After decades of coaching in the National Football League, Denver Broncos Head Coach Sean Payton has seen a lot of coaches come and go. During his time with the New Orleans Saints in the NFC South—Payton became quite familiar with Kyle Shanahan and Raheem Morris—who will be leading the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday. Those two men, as well as a quality roster of players, stand in the way of the Broncos’ pursuit of third straight victory. Under their guidance, the 49ers are undefeated to start their 2026 season. San Francisco sports both a Top 5 offense and defense and appear to be a championship caliber squad. Yesterday after practice, Payton had a lot of praise for Shanahan, who is in his tenth season leading the 49ers. “There are so many things he does well. He—like his father—it started with an elite run-game plan. That hasn’t changed. Some of the play-actions that come off of that run game, I can recall snaps in Atlanta where Matt Ryan is extending the ball, and then all of the sudden pulls it up, and you look down the field and there’s somebody wide open,” recalled Payton with respect to memories of Shanahan over the years. “That’s just one element of what makes him special. I think that balance relative to run and pass. We had a number of years together in the division, and then over the years as he’s become a head coach and you’re at Owners Meetings and Combines. I’m close with his father. We have a great relationship.” Shanahan has done well calling plays and leading the 49ers’ offense. They are near the top of the league in points scored and have been incredible on third down and in the red zone. When it matters most, Shanahan’s players have been executing at a high level. As Payton mentioned, the running game is front and center of Shanahan’s offensive game plans. This year, they have one of the best ground games in the NFL with Christian McCaffrey and rookie third-round pick Kaelon Black. If Denver hopes to win on the road, they can’t let McCaffrey and Black run wild over their defense. On top of that, their passing offense has been incredibly efficient too. Bringing back Deebo Samuel was a good choice by their front office. Moreover, adding Mike Evans at wide receiver has really opened things up for fifth-year quarterback Brock Purdy in the passing game. Purdy leads the NFL with 9 touchdowns and only one interception and has yet to be sacked through three games. What Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph has in store to contain the 49ers’ high-powered offense is anyone’s best guess. Without question, it will certainly be quite the chess-match for Joseph, who has had his fair share of battles against Shanahan over the years. On offense, the Broncos are still trying to find their way. They’ve looked much better in the second half in their back-to-back comeback victories. Unfortunately, their overall efficiency and productivity have been hampered by slow starts. Denver hasn’t been able to run the ball well consistently, are struggling converting third downs, and have had too many penalties and turnovers early on in games. It’s not a recipe for success and something the Broncos will have to figure out in short order to be top-tier competitors the rest of the season. This Sunday, Payton and Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb hope to establish an operable game plan that can combat one of the league’s best defenses coached by Morris. The 49ers allowed just 20 points in their first two contests but had issues stopping the run and getting pressure in their Week 3 win against the Cardinals. “He’s done a real good job defensively. They’re playing real good red-zone defense. They present a lot of problems,” remarked Payton. “There’s so much more film that we’re all looking at. We all see it. The defense was different. This goes all the way back to when he was at Tampa. I’ve known Raheem for ages. Joint practice here with the Rams. He was in Atlanta. He’s a tremendous coach with great juice,” added Payton. Sunday’s matchup will be a huge test for the Broncos. The 49ers a well-coached team with a roster stacked with quality players all across the board. In order to achieve a victory, Payton and his staff are going to be at their best. Which coaching staff will come up with the better game plan? You’ll just have to tune in and find out.

title: Detroit Lions, Sam LaPorta cut extension talks with no new contract
summary: According to a report from Ian Rapoport, the Detroit Lions and tight end Sam LaPorta have stopped contract negotiation talks after trying for weeks to get an extension done. Per Rapoport, talks extended through this weekend, but LaPorta’s camp wanted to break off conversations if they couldn’t result in a deal after four weeks into […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 17: Sam LaPorta #87 of the Detroit Lions reacts against the Buffalo Bills during the fourth quarter of the game at Highmark Stadium on September 17, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to a report from Ian Rapoport, the Detroit Lions and tight end Sam LaPorta have stopped contract negotiation talks after trying for weeks to get an extension done. Per Rapoport, talks extended through this weekend, but LaPorta’s camp wanted to break off conversations if they couldn’t result in a deal after four weeks into the season. “With LaPorta wanting to fully focus on the field, the sides decided that any new contract would wait until the offseason after a push on Friday and Saturday did not result in a deal,” Rapoport wrote. However, in the same story, Rapoport correctly notes that Detroit has a history of in-season negotiations for extensions (see: Alim McNeill), and it’s possible talks resume later this year. “The Lions continue to negotiate deals in-season and there is, at least, a chance they make another attempt at a deal that would make LaPorta one of the NFL’s highest-paid tight ends,” he wrote. It’s unclear how close the sides are or what is keeping them from reaching a deal. This offseason has been particularly lucrative for young tight ends. Packers’ Tucker Kraft signed a four-year, $75 million deal right before the start of the regular season, Raiders’ Michael Mayer received a three-year, $45 million deal, and Falcons’ Kyle Pitts inked a three-year, $54 million extension. Publicly, the Lions general manager Brad Holmes has expressed an interest in extending all four of Detroit’s top picks in the 2023 NFL Draft class. They’ve already levied deals for Jahmyr Gibbs (three years, $67.5M) and Jack Campbell (four years, $81M), but with both LaPorta and safety Brian Branch coming back from season-ending injuries, it’s not surprising to see both of those negotiations drag on. We’ll see if the two sides recommit to talks or if negotiations will be put on hold until the end of the season. If LaPorta doesn’t receive an extension, he will be an unrestricted free agent in 2027. However, the Lions do hold the option to use the franchise tag on him, which is currently projected to be a one-year deal worth about $17.5 million .

(Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to a report from ESPN’s Adam Schefter, the Carolina Panthers are likely to be without their top receiver against the Detroit Lions on Sunday night. Schefter is reporting that wide receiver Jalen Coker is “unlikely to play” in Week 4 due to a quad injury that had him limited in practice this week. It’s worth noting that the Panthers also elevated receiver Ja’seem Reed from the practice squad—another sign Coker may not be ready to go this week. Coker has been the Panthers’ most productive receiver through three games, hauling in a team-leading 18 catches for 222 yards and two touchdowns. The Panthers are in a bit of a tight spot when it comes to their receiving corps. Not only is Coker trending toward missing this game, but 2024 first-round pick Xavier Legette was placed on injured reserve this week. That said, the Panthers still do have 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year Tetairoa McMillan (12 catches, 193 yards this year), John Metchie III (two catches, 19 yards, TD), and Brycen Tremayne (four catches, 83 yards). Additionally, the Panthers sport an impressive trio of tight ends in Darren Waller, Tommy Tremble, and Mitchell Evans, who have combined for 22 catches, 240 yards, and two touchdowns this season. The Lions have notoriously struggled against tight ends through three weeks, allowing a league-high 351 receiving yards and six touchdowns. Still, this is fortunate break for a Lions secondary that has struggled to defend the pass more than any other team thus far. Detroit ranks dead last in passing yards allowed per game (299.3) and are 27th in passer rating allowed (110.2). Meanwhile, the Panthers offense ranks first in passing offense (295.7 yards per game) and 16th in passer rating (95.6)

title: Detroit Lions vs. Carolina Panthers preview: 4 key stats
summary: This will be the third meeting between the Lions and Panthers in the Dan Campbell era and the first in primetime. Neither of the previous two matchups was decided by fewer than two touchdowns, and Dave Canales, hosting his first primetime game at the helm, will already be the third different Panthers head coach Detroit […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NC - DECEMBER 24: Detroit Lions offensive tackle Penei Sewell (58) during an NFL football game between the Detroit Lions and the Carolina Panthers on December 24, 2022, at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte, N.C. (Photo by John Byrum/Ic on Sportswire) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images This will be the third meeting between the Lions and Panthers in the Dan Campbell era and the first in primetime. Neither of the previous two matchups was decided by fewer than two touchdowns, and Dave Canales, hosting his first primetime game at the helm, will already be the third different Panthers head coach Detroit has faced during that span. The Panthers may sit at only 1-2, with losses to the Bears and Browns, but they’ve seen some improved play early from to-be-determined franchise quarterback Bryce Young, Jameson Williams’ former quarterback at Alabama, and cannot be taken lightly. After all, Carolina has more recently made the postseason and won its division than Detroit. The Panthers have finished top five in total free-agent guarantees handed out to defensive players in each of the past two offseasons, committing more than $225 million guaranteed to defensive additions over that span. Yet, despite all that spending and being under the siege of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero, they’re still playing like a bottom-10 unit. The Lions, already playing their second road primetime game of the season, will look to reverse their fortunes from Buffalo and potentially put together their most complete performance yet during Alim McNeill’s homecoming. While some rain is expected, much of the analysis consists of passing statistics given the tendencies and personnel of both teams. With that, let’s get into my four key stats and matchups for Sunday night’s game. Note: Unless otherwise indicated, all statistics are sourced from NFL Pro, FTN Fantasy, Pro Football Reference, SumerSports, or Pro Football Focus. Cheaper By the Dozen The Panthers, in Year 4 of Young, made the switch from head coach Dave Canales to offensive coordinator Brad Idzik as the primary offensive playcaller and have placed more of the load on Young’s shoulders. They’ve had success against the Bears and Falcons defenses but struggled against the Browns. Through three weeks, the Panthers’ 67.9% pass rate ranks third-highest in the league, with Young leading the NFL at 313 passing yards per game. He’ll face a Lions pass defense that ranks dead last with 299.3 passing yards allowed per game, 27th at +0.16 EPA/pass, and 24th with a 48.5% pass success rate allowed. The Panthers have had even more passing success when they go to 12-personnel, mixing in combinations of Darren Waller, Tommy Tremble, and Mitchell Evans to go along with Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker at wide receiver. This season, passing from 12-personnel, the Panthers are 20-for-27, a 74.1% completion percentage (8th), for 317 passing yards (2nd) and 11.7 yards per attempt (2nd), with strong analytical metrics as well: a 10.76-yard aDOT (5th), 63.0% success rate (4th), and +0.35 EPA/play (7th). The Panthers’ pressure rate allowed, which overall sits at 52.6% and ranks last in the NFL, drops to only 40.7% (20th) when passing out of 12-personnel. It’s been an added element that Idzik has brought to their offense this season after they didn’t have nearly as much reliance or success with it last year. The most common targets for Young when passing from 12-personnel have been Tremble (8 targets, 6 catches, 61 receiving yards), Coker (4 targets, 4 catches, 106 receiving yards), McMillan (5 targets, 3 catches, 62 receiving yards), and Waller (3 targets, 3 catches, 43 receiving yards). It’s a potent condensed passing attack for the Detroit Lions to defend. The Lions defense, which has prided itself on its preference for base defense throughout the majority of the Dan Campbell era—running more of it than anyone last season—has been worked as a pass defense this season, both overall and specifically against 12-personnel. The Lions pass defense has been getting shredded against 12-personnel: 33 dropbacks (30th, 3rd most) 29 pass attempts (30th) 21 completions (31st) 291 passing yards (32nd) 72.4% completion percentage (26th) 8.8 yards per pass (25th) 4 passing touchdowns (t-31st) 8.41 aDOT (21st) 55.2% passing success rate (19th) +0.38 EPA per play (25th) Teams have given the Lions a heavy dose of 12-personnel, and they haven’t had answers, all while the Lions’ pressure rate and sack rate are also lower against 12-personnel than they are overall. Kelvin Sheppard will need to equip his defense with better answers against the Panthers. And while the Lions’ cornerback group has been much maligned, having success in coverage against Carolina’s 12-personnel passing attack will also be reliant on improvement from the spine of the defense, with linebackers Jack Campbell, Derrick Barnes, and perhaps Trevor Nowaske or Malcolm Rodriguez, along with safeties Chuck Clark and Christian Izien, needing to execute better. Young and the Restless The one area where the Panthers’ passing offense has faltered, as mentioned in the last section, is allowing a league-high pressure rate. Much like Jared Goff and his elite-level processing skills have continued to pick apart the blitz, Bryce Young has found a higher level of success against the blitz so far this season. When defenses don’t bring those additional pass rushers, however, that’s where the Panthers’ prowling passing attack has been declawed. The Panthers’ yards per pass drop from 8.3 (4th) against the blitz to 6.1 (18th) with no blitz, while their EPA per pass plummets from +0.35 (6th) to -0.09 (21st). Not only does the passing production drop, but the heat applied to Young actually increases. Against the blitz, the Panthers’ pressure rate is 39.5% (t-11th) and their sack rate is only 2.3% (5th). With no blitz, their pressure rate climbs to 45.3% (32nd), while their sack rate jumps to 7.0% (21st). Young and the offense operate more efficiently when he’s sped up and can attack the vacancies left behind in coverage. The Detroit Lions’ defensive front has shown some teeth early this season, generating a 36.8% pressure rate (3rd) and 6.9% sack rate (12th) when not blitzing. The Panthers were already dealing with backup offensive tackles in Rasheed Walker and rookie Monroe Freeling, and with the injury to left guard Damien Lewis, they’ll be left to play 2024 UDFA Corey Bullock and his 55 career offensive snaps in the first start of his career. It could be the perfect recipe for disaster for Aidan Hutchinson, Alim McNeill, and company to maul the Panthers and leave their passing offense to die in the wilderness—if the coverage behind them can hold up. It’ll also be on Kelvin Sheppard to calculatedly call off the dogs, rush four, and ask questions later. Lion Kings of the Jungle The Carolina Panthers are playing light boxes (six or fewer defenders) on a league-high 40.2% of plays. While defensive tackle Derrick Brown is an imposing player in the middle, the Panthers have been leaving prized free-agent signing Devin Lloyd and Bobby Okereke—a player exposed by Jahmyr Gibbs against the Giants last season—out to dry in the run defense this season. They’re also relying on undrafted rookie Aaron Hall and fellow rookie Lee Hunter as the two defensive tackles trying to hold down the fort next to Brown on the interior. Against Man/Duo run concepts, the Panthers have allowed 132 rushing yards on 16 carries and rank league-worst in all of the following: 8.3 yards per carry, four rushing touchdowns, and +0.45 EPA per rush. Meanwhile, on such runs this season, Gibbs has 12 carries for 61 rushing yards (5.1 yards per carry) and a rushing touchdown, along with an impressive 58.3% rushing success rate. Look for the Lions to go big-on-big, take advantage of the light boxes, and allow Penei Sewell and the re-engineered Detroit People Movers to mash bodies and control the line of scrimmage, giving Gibbs downhill running room…

The following Sunday, Green Bay will most likely see either […]
full_text: The Green Bay Packers are 1-2, but they are likely to face a pair of backup quarterbacks over the next two games. This coming Sunday, they will play the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who will start undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels due to Baker Mayfield’s dislocated thumb. The following Sunday, Green Bay will most likely see either Case Keenum or Tyson Bagent for the Chicago Bears as starter Caleb Williams continues to work back from a hamstring injury. This week, we asked APC’s readers what you expected to see in terms of results in those two games — specifically, to predict the Packers’ record after Week 5. There is understandable pessimism among the fan base, however, especially after the Bears went and dominated the Philadelphia Eagles 27-7 on Monday Night Football with Keenum under center. As a result, a slight plurality of fans expect the Packers to go 1-1 in these two games, and this writer would bet that most of the fans who voted that way are anticipating the win to come this Sunday in Tampa. That group consists of 42 percent of Packers fans surveyed; however, a very similar number, 39 percent, expect the Packers to lose BOTH of the next two games. Here’s a look at the results of this survey: Meanwhile, Packers fans are understandably feeling dismal about the team’s overall direction right now. That’s a reasonable reaction after a 1-2 start that could have easily seen the team go 0-3. However, most of these survey responses came in before the Packers signed Kevin Zeitler on Wednesday. Is that enough to move the needle on some of these responses? We may just have to wait and see how the team performs in Tampa this Sunday. Here are this week’s confidence results, which predictably express a great lack of confidence: As of now, the Packers’ odds of making the NFC playoff field are significantly worse than they were to start the season. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , Green Bay’s odds of making it to the postseason have dropped to +240, a significant fall from the -150 or so that the team sat at heading into Week 1. The Packers absolutely need at least one win in these two games to give themselves even a plausible shot at making the postseason. Let’s see if they get one this Sunday in Tampa.

title: Packers-Buccaneers Preview: Green Bay travels to Tampa Bay
summary: The Green Bay Packers (1-2) visit a 0-3 Tampa Bay Buccaneers team on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET as a 4-point favorite, and the matchup is defined by one injury: Baker Mayfield is out with a dislocated right thumb, so undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels makes his first NFL start. Through three weeks, the Bucs have […]
full_text: (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers (1-2) visit a 0-3 Tampa Bay Buccaneers team on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET as a 4-point favorite, and the matchup is defined by one injury: Baker Mayfield is out with a dislocated right thumb, so undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels makes his first NFL start. Through three weeks, the Bucs have the league’s worst offense by EPA/play (-0.23) and a top-six defense (-0.14), per SumerSports. That split is the whole preview. Tampa’s defense is good enough to keep a broken Packers offense from finding easy answers, especially on the ground. Tampa’s offense, now without its starting quarterback behind a line that has already allowed 13 sacks, is the softest unit Jonathan Gannon’s defense will see this season. The Packers win this game by refusing to hand Tampa short fields, because the Bucs have been undone by turnovers and special teams far more than by their defense. Key Losses WR Mike Evans (49ers) LB Lavonte David (retired) CB Jamel Dean (Steelers) Edge Haason Reddick (free agency) DL Logan Hall (Texans) RB Rachaad White (free agency) OC Josh Grizzard (fired) QB coach Thad Lewis (fired) DL coach Charlie Strong (fired) DB coach Kevin Ross (fired) ST coordinator Thomas McGaughey (fired) Offensive consultant Tom Moore (retired) Key Additions OC Zac Robinson (ex-Falcons) Passing game coordinator T.J. Yates Offensive assistant Ken Zampese ST coordinator Danny Smith (ex-Steelers) LB Alex Anzalone (2 years, $17M) DL A’Shawn Robinson DL Rakeem Nuñez-Roches Edge Al-Quadin Muhammad RB Kenneth Gainwell (2 years, $14M) Edge Rueben Bain Jr. (draft) LB Josiah Trotter (draft, 2nd round) WR Ted Hurst III (draft) CB Keionte Scott (draft) QB Jalon Daniels (undrafted) Note: Bowles still calls the defense; no DC hired Efficiency, 2026 through Week 3 (per SumerSports) Offense EPA/play: -0.23 (32nd) Offense EPA/dropback: -0.33 (31st) Offense EPA/rush: -0.06 (~14th) Offense success rate: 37.6% (30th) Offense rush success rate: 48.9% (7th, after Week 2) Defense EPA/play allowed: -0.14 (6th) Defense EPA/dropback allowed: -0.08 (12th) Defense EPA/rush allowed: -0.22 (4th) Defense success rate allowed: 37.6% (5th) Defense rush success rate allowed: 2nd-lowest in NFL Efficiency, 2025 Offense dropback EPA/play: 0.06 (18th) Offense rush EPA/play: -0.09 (24th) Offense EPA/play, Week 7 on: -0.089 (26th) Defense EPA/dropback allowed, Week 10 on: 0.280 (27th) Not publicly available: pass success rate (either side) and 2025 success-rate splits 2025 in review: 6-2 to 8-9 Tampa Bay started 6-2 and finished 8-9, missing the playoffs for the first time since 2019 and losing the NFC South to Carolina on a tiebreaker on the final day. The collapse began right after the Week 9 bye: losses to New England, Buffalo and the Rams (by a combined 106-62) started a stretch where the team went 2-7 the rest of the way. The offense regressed under first-year coordinator Josh Grizzard. Liam Coen’s 2024 unit ranked top-five in nearly everything. In 2025 the Bucs averaged 22.4 points (18th), 320.4 yards (21st) and 5.2 yards per play, a full yard below 2024. Dropback EPA was 0.06 per play (18th) and rush EPA was -0.09 (24th), per a Yahoo Sports team preview. From Week 7 on, the offense ranked 26th in EPA/play (-0.089). The run game is the mechanism worth knowing. Tampa stayed with a gap-heavy scheme, and Bucky Irving went from a 1,122-yard rookie season to 3.4 yards per carry on 173 attempts. SumerSports has his 2025 success rate at 34.7% (95th among backs) with a 12.1% tackle-for-loss rate. Injuries made it worse: third-string guards played stretches and Tristan Wirfs missed games. The defense held up against the run and collapsed against the pass. Opponents ran for 99.1 yards per game (5th), but the pass defense ranked 27th and the pass rush produced its lowest sack total in Bowles’ seven seasons in Tampa, per the team. From Week 10 on, the Bucs allowed 0.280 EPA per dropback, 27th in the league. That pattern (stout run front, leaky coverage, thin pass rush) is exactly what the offseason tried to fix. Bucaneers 2026 weeks 1-3 so far All three losses were one-score games, and in each the Bucs gave away points outside of normal defensive play: fumbles in Cincinnati, red-zone failures against Cleveland, a punt-return touchdown and penalties against Minnesota. Tampa has allowed a league-high 30 points off turnovers. Week 1 at Cincinnati. The offense actually moved the ball: Mayfield was 23-of-28 for 216 yards and the Bucs never punted. Three straight first-half fumbles produced 21 Bengals points, one returned for a score, and another fumble killed the comeback. Josiah Trotter became the first player in NFL history with a pick-six and a sack in his debut, but his was the only sack on Joe Burrow. Week 2 vs. Cleveland. Tampa scored on five possessions but only once in the end zone, with Chase McLaughlin hitting from 59, 45, 31 and 31. The run defense dominated (Quinshon Judkins: 12 carries, 21 yards), yet Deshaun Watson completed 80% of his throws, including a 55-yard TD to Denzel Boston and the go-ahead score late. A 132-minute lightning delay split the game. Week 3 vs. Minnesota. The defense played its best game: Kyler Murray went 15-of-29 for 168 yards, and the Bucs had four sacks plus an A’Shawn Robinson interception. The offense posted a 28% success rate and -0.24 EPA/play per Sharp’s advanced box score, with eight penalties for 81 yards. Mayfield finished 17-of-34 for 217 yards, a TD and an INT, then left with the thumb injury; Daniels went 0-for-3 with an interception in relief. Receiver Jalen McMillan also left with a knee injury. The read for Green Bay: Tampa’s defense is not the reason it is 0-3. Its yardage allowed ranks 6th (282.7 per game), but its scoring allowed ranks 23rd (26.3), and the gap is almost entirely turnovers and special teams. Keys for the Packers Punish Bowles’ blitz with timing, not the run game. Tampa blitzes 43.4% of the time (3rd) but gets home on only 32.6% of those blitzes (28th), and its overall pressure rate is fourth-lowest, per Sharp and FantasyPros. That is a profile Green Bay can attack even with a battered line. The catch is Jordan Love’s own pressure numbers: pressured on 44.7% of dropbacks, 18-of-50 with no TDs and two INTs under pressure, and a 2.45-second average time to throw (third-longest). Quick game and hot answers against a defense playing single-high 71.7% of the time (2nd) is the mechanism, not a hope that the line holds. Do not script a run-game rebound. Green Bay’s rush EPA (-0.41) is the league’s worst and the backfield produced 17 yards in Week 3. Tampa allows -0.22 EPA per rush (4th) and the second-lowest rushing success rate. Screens and quick perimeter throws are the run game this week. Gannon’s problem is containment, not coverage. Daniels averaged 4.8 yards per attempt under pressure in 2025 with a 12.9% red-zone interception rate, but he scrambled on 11.3% of preseason dropbacks and ran a 4.46. Rushing lanes and a spy or rush-and-retrace front matter more than exotic coverage. Tampa’s line has already allowed 13 sacks with a quarterback who extends plays. Make Tampa drive the length of the field. The Bucs’ scoring has come from short fields and McLaughlin’s leg (league-leading 14 makes of 50+ since the start of 2025). Green Bay’s -37 second-half point differential and league-high 32 penalties are the self-inflicted version of Tampa’s problem; whichever team cleans that up likely wins. Respect the weapons. Egbuka, Godwin, Otton, Irving and Hurst give Daniels real targets. With McMillan’s knee and Evans gone, the Bucs’ receiver depth is thinner than the names suggest.

On Friday, head coach Matt LaFleur said that Brinson, who had been battling a calf injury since warmups […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers placed defensive lineman Warren Brinson on the injured reserve on Saturday, just one day after they ruled him out of Week 4’s action against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers with calf and groin injuries. On Friday, head coach Matt LaFleur said that Brinson, who had been battling a calf injury since warmups of Week 2 of the preseason, was injured in a non-contact fashion — leading to his groin injury — when he returned to practice this week. He said that Brinson’s injury is expected to take a “ significant amount of time ” to recover from. So far, Brinson hasn’t been designated to return from the injured reserve. The Packers are allowed to designate eight players to return from the IR in an individual season (the number goes up to 10 if the team makes the postseason). Both receiver Savion Williams and edge defender Collin Oliver have been designated to return in 2026, while offensive tackle Zach Bako-Bewele and receiver Jayden Reed are in the Brinson camp — yet to be designated to return. PUP list players like Micah Parsons, Luke Musgrave and Jordon Riley do not count toward the IR-DFR count. Brinson has yet to play in a regular-season game due to his calf injury, and the Packers entered the 2026 season “oversigned” at the position, as they carried seven interior defensive linemen on their initial 53-man roster — despite the team regularly rostering just five players at the position on their 48-man game-day roster. Green Bay also announced that linebacker Edgerrin Cooper has fully cleared the NFL’s concussion protocol and was removed from the team’s injury report . That leaves the following players with statuses: LG Aaron Banks – OUT RG Jacob Monk – OUT DL Anthony Campbell – OUT OL Jager Burton – Questionable The Packers only have to make four scratches against the Buccaneers, since they only have a 52-man roster at the moment. Three of them are obvious, as three players have already been ruled out, and the final scratch will likely be an offensive lineman (it’s rare for NFL teams to carry more than eight active linemen on the game-day roster) — be it Jager Burton, who is dealing with a quadricep issue, or another option on the roster.
