title: Remembering a Random Packers Game: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers
summary: Each week during the 2026 season, I’m taking a look at a previous game between the Green Bay Packers and their opponent for that week. I’m letting a random number generator decide which game I cover, and so far, it’s been a mixed bag. Last week was a fun one as I covered the 28th […]
full_text: Credit: Scott Halleran /Allsport | Getty Images Each week during the 2026 season, I’m taking a look at a previous game between the Green Bay Packers and their opponent for that week. I’m letting a random number generator decide which game I cover, and so far, it’s been a mixed bag. Last week was a fun one as I covered the 28th overall meeting between the Packers and Falcons. This week, we’re talking about the Buccaneers, whom the Packers have played a total of 59 times. The random number? 37. The 37th overall matchup between the two former division rivals took place on September 1st, 1996. Let’s dig in. Entering the Game It was Week 1 of the 1996 season, and the Packers were coming in as one of the teams to beat. After an 11-5 first place finish in the NFC Central, and a Pro Bowl/All-Pro/MVP season from QB Brett Favre, how could they not be? Favre was hitting his prime heading into his age-27 season. DE Reggie White had just had another double-digit sack year. The team was also putting together a nice little group of weapons for Favre, which included WRs Antonio Freeman and Robert Brooks, and RBs Dorsey Levens and Edgar Bennett. It was time to step it up after a disappointing NFC Championship loss to the Dallas Cowboys. Key Moments After starting the game with the ball, the Buccaneers quickly gave it to the Packers when QB Trent Dilfer was intercepted by DB Mike Prior, already in Bucs territory. This would be the first of six Buccaneers turnovers. Their next turnover would come later in the first quarter, when RB Jerry Ellison fumbled, and Reggie White swiftly recovered. Already deep in Buccaneers territory, it took less than a minute for Brett Favre to find TE Keith Jackson in the endzone. Midway through the third quarter, with the Packers leading 27-3, they stole the ball yet again when DB Craig Newsome forced an Alvin Harper fumble, recovered by DB Doug Evans. The Packers scored yet again on their next drive, making the score 34-3. This would be the final score of the game, but the turnovers were just getting started. During the next offensive drive for the Bucs, Trent Dilfer was picked off by future HOF S LeRoy Butler. Butler would pick Dilfer off yet again during their next drive, and this one was returned for 50 yards. Dilfer would throw one more pick in the fourth quarter, to Lamont Hollinquest, to cap off the day. The Outcome The Packers came out of Week 1 with a 1-0 record after their 34-3 win. Brett Favre finished 20/27 with 247 passing yards and 4 TD passes. Edgar Bennett led the team on the ground with 62 rushing yards on 13 attempts. The Packers defense picked off Trent Dilfer 4 times, and caused 3 total fumbles. Pure dominance. The 1996 Packers would go on to win 13 total regular season games, tied with the Denver Broncos for the league’s best. Brett Favre would win his second consecutive MVP award, while leading the league with 39 TD passes. The Packers then proceeded to steamroll their way through the playoffs, winning the Divisional Round 35-14, and the NFC Championship 30-13. They then won their first Super Bowl since 1967, when they beat the New England Patriots 35-21. The Packers take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium on Sunday afternoon, during the day’s early slate of games. With a revamped offensive line, the 1-2 Packers are looking to right the ship against a struggling 0-3 Bucs team. Can they get the job done?
author: Sam Kallien

title: Packers film room: Flush/loop stunt
summary: As Jonathan Gannon prepares the defense each week, layers and layers are added to build a versatile defense capable of handling any situation. The layering includes adding new ways to generate pressure without sending five or more. One way Gannon accomplishes this is through a defensive line stunt. A stunt is a pre-planned pass rush […]
full_text: As Jonathan Gannon prepares the defense each week, layers and layers are added to build a versatile defense capable of handling any situation. The layering includes adding new ways to generate pressure without sending five or more. One way Gannon accomplishes this is through a defensive line stunt. A stunt is a pre-planned pass rush where defensive linemen trade their usual rush lanes after the snap. One rusher attacks first as the penetrator, trying to get the adjacent blockers to commit, while a teammate follows as the looper and wraps behind him into the space that reaction creates. A stunt doesn’t try to win with raw strength. It attacks the offensive line’s communication: blockers have to recognize the movement, pass rushers off from one lineman to another, and keep the pocket connected. “Flush” describes what the stunt is trying to do rather than one universally defined call, and teams name their line games differently. A flush stunt is built to make the quarterback leave his spot. A sack is a bonus, not the main goal. The Packers front is aligned with five across the line of scrimmage, forcing the offense into a 5-0 protection call. In a 5-0 protection call, the five offensive linemen are responsible for the five most dangerous rushers. Often this is man protection (“big on big”), with the center or quarterback identifying the Mike linebacker to set the count. The design usually collapses the area where the quarterback wants to step up, which forces him to bail out of the pocket in a direction the defense has already planned for. A loop into the middle can close the space the quarterback expected to step into, and the looper doesn’t need a clean sack to succeed if he pushes the quarterback off his spot, speeds up the throw, or flushes him toward another defender. Here, Edgerrin Cooper is the MIKE linebacker and aligned as an interior rusher over the center. The interior rushers crash hard toward the guards with the two penetrators on the left side of the defensive line slanting inside to the opposite gap. Brenton Cox Jr. and Lukas Van Ness collapse the right side of the offensive line to the middle of the pocket. Cooper loops around the perimeter and works wide to cut off one escape lane. The only way out is to the other side, where a contain rusher, a spy linebacker, or a defender dropping into the throwing lane is waiting. Some four-man games slant both ends inside to occupy the tackles while the tackles loop outside to attack the edge, a setup designed to flush the quarterback out of the pocket or force a quick throw. The payoff is subtle. Timing-based passing games depend on the quarterback hitting the top of his drop and throwing on rhythm. Force him to move, and receivers are running routes that no longer match his timing, while throwing lanes shift. Offenses have answers. Linemen who communicate and pass stunts off cleanly shut them down before they start. Quick passing takes away the time a stunt needs to develop, since loopers take an extra beat to arrive. Screens and draws punish defensive linemen who are rushing on angles rather than playing their gaps. A mobile quarterback who escapes toward the defense’s intended trap and still throws on target turns the stunt into a big play for the offense.
author: Rich Madrid

title: Packers film room: What went wrong on the Falcons 55-yard run
summary: Bijan Robinson’s 55-yarder against the Green Bay Packers in week three was the play that turned the game. It came on first down after a roughing the passer penalty on edge rusher Brenton Cox on third down that would have forced the Falcons to punt and given the Packers another chance to add to their […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WI - SEPTEMBER 24: Bijan Robinson #7 of the Atlanta Falcons celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Green Bay Packers during an NFL football game at Lambeau Field on September 24, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bijan Robinson’s 55-yarder against the Green Bay Packers in week three was the play that turned the game. It came on first down after a roughing the passer penalty on edge rusher Brenton Cox on third down that would have forced the Falcons to punt and given the Packers another chance to add to their 7-0 lead. The Packers took a 7-0 lead when Christian Watson came uncovered on a play-action pass with 5:13 left in the first quarter. Penix had also thrown an interception on Atlanta’s opening drive, so the Falcons’ offense looked out of sync. The drive that included the run nearly stalled too. Atlanta started at its own 15 and picked up a first down on an 8-yard pass to Kyle Pitts and a 6-yard Robinson run, but Lukas Van Ness forced Penix into an intentional grounding penalty that left Atlanta facing third-and-11. That was a likely punt situation, and Green Bay’s defense was winning. Instead, Brenton Cox Jr. was called for unnecessary roughness, which gave the Falcons a first down. Atlanta capitalized right away. On the very next snap, Robinson broke a 55-yard run to the Green Bay 5. The timing mattered as much as the yardage. A defense that has just given away a first down on a penalty is often a step slow to reset, and Robinson turned that moment into a huge gain. Going from backed up at the 15 to first-and-goal at the 5 within a couple of plays was the biggest field-position swing of the first half. The play call from Atlanta was an outside zone run concept to the offense’s left side behind their tight end Charlie Woerner and Drake London in tight to the formation. The Packers countered the Falcons formation with a 5-2 front and two deep safeties behind it. Playing two deep safeties versus the run is risky but the Packers have been excellent defending the run from two high shells the last couple of seasons and Gannon specializes in it. In fact, the Packers had it bottled up really well initially. Edgerrin Cooper (No. 56) is the edge setter on this play as the defensive end backdoor slants inside. Cooper is the spill/force player responsible for spilling the ball back inside. Zaire Franklin (No. 44) is the back side leverage player who’s job it is to clean up any open gap and the run if it spills back inside. On the perimeter, Brandon Cisse (No. 2) is the front side leverage player and secondary force. As Cooper comes down, Woerner blocks him and pancakes him to the ground. Cooper plays the inside shoulder and leaves Cisse on an island if Robinson bounces outside. Sure enough he does as Franklin moves with Robinson’s movement and flashes color in the gaps. Cisse dives for the tackle and misses. The rookie did not have a great night. A tackle here would have went for a one or two yard gain. Poor gap responsibility ultimately doomed the defense on this play. Robinson later scored on a 3-yard run two plays later, tying the game at 7 with 1:32 left in the first quarter. From there, Atlanta took over. The Falcons scored 27 straight points, turning a 7-0 deficit into a 27-7 lead in the fourth quarter. The run was also the first sign of how the night would go on the ground. Robinson finished with 194 yards and two touchdowns on 29 carries, one yard short of his career high of 195 set against the Rams in 2025. Green Bay managed almost nothing running the ball by comparison. The Packers ran nine times for just 17 yards.

title: Remembering the Packers’ best performances against the Buccaneers
summary: The Green Bay Packers head to Tampa, Florida this weekend for a date with their old NFC Central opponents, the Buccaneers.  Setting aside our memories of the 2020 NFC Championship, there were plenty of great matchups between the Packers and Buccaneers over the years, and they produced quite a few high-end statistical performances. Here are […]
full_text: MILWAUKEE, WI - SEPTEMBER 12: Lynn Dickey #12 of the Green Bay Packers looks to pass against the Los Angeles Rams during an NFL football game September 12, 1982 at Milwaukee County Stadium in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. Dickey played for the Packers from 1976-85. (Photo by Focus on Sport/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers head to Tampa, Florida this weekend for a date with their old NFC Central opponents, the Buccaneers. Setting aside our memories of the 2020 NFC Championship, there were plenty of great matchups between the Packers and Buccaneers over the years, and they produced quite a few high-end statistical performances. Here are some of the best, with links throughout to some highlights that are just about guaranteed to give you a jolt of nostalgia. Most passing yards – 418 ( Lynn Dickey, 1980 ) Packers fans should have plenty of good memories of great passing days against the Buccaneers — five different Packers quarterbacks have broken the 300-yard mark against Tampa! But the greatest of them all isn’t Aaron Rodgers or Brett Favre or even Don Majkowski. It’s Lynn Dickey, who rolled up 418 yards in a game the Packers thoroughly dominated , but didn’t win. Despite outgaining the Buccaneers by more than 300 yards (569 to 262), two turnovers and three missed field goals prevented the Packers from coming out on top. Instead, the game ended in a 14-14 tie, which remains the only tie between these two teams in their relatively long history together. Most rushing yards – 169 ( Ahman Green, 2001 ) Ahman Green’s 169 yard day would be more impressive if he could have hung onto the ball. Really, turnovers were the entire theme of the Packers’ 2001 home matchup against their NFC Central opponents — the last time they’d play their division rivals at home before the Buccaneers headed off for the NFC South. Green’s fumble was one of three turnovers by the Packers that day and came smack in the middle of a seven-drive series of remarkable futility. After scoring a touchdown on their first drive of the game, the Packers’ next seven drives went like so: punt, interception, punt, fumble, missed field goal, interception, punt. Yet thanks in part to Green, who scored on a 63-yard scamper in the third quarter, the Packers’ still hung around long enough for one big play to turn the tide later. More on that in a bit. Most receiving yards – 169 ( Sterling Sharpe, 1989 ) In a funny historical coincidence, the Packers’ single-game receiving yardage high against the Buccaneers is the same as their single game rushing yardage high, and somewhat predictably, it belongs to Sterling Sharpe. Sharpe had 130 or more receiving yards against the Buccaneers four different times, but never put up a bigger yardage number than he did in an eight catch, 169 yard, two touchdown performance against the Buccaneers in 1989. Sharpe’s performance was the first of three times a Packers player would have 150 or more receiving yards against the Buccaneers, and the other two guys to do it pulled it off in the same game. In 1999 , both Bill Schroeder and Antonio Freeman surpassed 150 receiving yards ; Schroeder had seven catches for 158 yards, while Freeman had seven catches for just 152, but added two touchdowns, the second a 21-yard strike that gave the Packers the win. Christian Watson and Matthew Golden: your targets are set for Sunday. Most points – 24 ( Sterling Sharpe, 1993 ) Remember earlier when I mentioned Sterling Sharpe had four different games where he put up more than 130 receiving yards against the Buccaneers? Yeah, that 169-yard game was arguably not his best. In 1993, Sharpe caught 10 passes for 147 yards and scored four touchdowns — three of which came in the first half. The Packers cruised to a 37-14 win behind Sharpe’s massive day. Most sacks – 4.5 ( Bryce Paup, 1991 ) Big days aren’t limited to the offense, of course. En route to a 15-13 Packers’ win , Bryce Paup and the rest of the defense put Vinny Testaverde in hell, sacking him seven times, with Paup accounting for 4.5. One of Paup’s sacks came in the end zone, giving him the first (but not only) points of his NFL career. Most solo tackles – 10 (two players tied) Here’s a chance to think about two guys who probably haven’t crossed your mind in a while. The Packers’ high water mark for solo tackles against the Buccaneers is 10 and it’s happened twice. Jude Waddy did it first, taking down 10 players by himself in 1999. Tyrone Williams did it two years later, racking up 10 solo tackles in the same game where Ahman Green ran for 169 yards. Most interceptions – 2 (eight players tied) Eight different players have had two interceptions in a game against the Buccaneers, so we’ve got a bunch of different performances from which to choose if we’re looking for a highlight. How’s this one for you? LeRoy Butler intercepted two passes in the Packers’ 1996 season-opening win over the Buccaneers, setting the tone for their Super Bowl journey. Oh, and since I have a contractual obligation to mention tight ends whenever possible, Keith Jackson scored three touchdowns that day. Let’s see it again, Tucker Kraft! Honorable mention: Allen Rossum scores on a punt return to beat the Buccaneers I mentioned earlier there were some heroics that delivered the win for the Packers in the game where Ahman Green ran for 169 yards, and here they are. After the Packers’ defense forced a punt late in the fourth quarter, Allen Rossum ripped off a 55-yard punt return for a touchdown to give the Packers a 21-20 win over the Buccaneers in 2001. Was it a pretty game? Certainly not. But Rossum’s effort gave the Packers an exciting win over Tampa in their last meetings as divisional rivals, and that’s always going to be worth remembering.

title: Weekend Musings: The Houston Texans’ coaching staff on the hot seat?
summary: It is early. It is early. It is early. That is the caveat with this discussion. That being said, the Houston Texans’ recent 0-3 start wasn’t on a lot of bingo cards. As such, you are starting to hear a few rumblings about job security. While others like the Bucs, Jets and Commanders have coaches […]
full_text: It is early. It is early. It is early. That is the caveat with this discussion. That being said, the Houston Texans’ recent 0-3 start wasn’t on a lot of bingo cards. As such, you are starting to hear a few rumblings about job security. While others like the Bucs, Jets and Commanders have coaches who are likely leading the charge, you might start finding Ryans’ name, along with some on his staff, on that roll-call. Again, it is early, but it is starting to populate the internet. On one hand, losses to the Bills and Bengals, two playoff contenders, would not in and of itself be horrible. The Colts loss doesn’t look great, but it was a road game. Also, the Texans under Ryans don’t get off to the best of starts. This is the second straight year that the Texans started 0-3 and the 3rd season in Ryans’ 4 that the squad started at least 0-2. You’re probably tracking that the 2026 Texans will attempt do what their 2018 and 2025 counterparts did (make the playoffs) after an 0-3 start. Yet, this was a team that saw itself among the elite of the NFL. Two losses at home against contenders and a division loss at Indy. Again, early, but now Houston is down in some critical tiebreakers. The running game hasn’t lived up to its promise over three games, as the team in 30th in rushing. Stroud has been sacked 10 times and again among the leaders in QBs under pressure on drop-backs. These were two big problems coming into the season, and thus far, they don’t seem fixed. Then you have the defense. Expected to be the best in the game, their first three games haven’t shown it. They got shredded something fierce against Buffalo, and while the performances have improved over the next two games, they are still not closing out games like they did last season. They forced three turnovers against the Colts, but also allowed that team to convert over 53% of its 3rd/4th Down attempts. Likely the defense will get itself back into shape, but can they carry the team like they did last season? Additionally, the team has taken some major injury hits. While some are out for the year (Higgins), players like, Nico Collins, Branden Smith, Kayden MacDonald, Eg Ingram and Henry To’oTo’o should be back in the lineup before too much longer. That will help, but will their return be enough, or too little, too late? Oh, and matters may not be helped if Al-Shaair, off-and-on out of the game against Indy, can’t go against Dallas. If the team doesn’t overcome its usual slow start, what’s next? This is not a league known for patience. As Jerry Glanville famously quipped “This is the NFL, which stands for ‘Not For Long.’ I’ll be bagging groceries”. While coaches like Ryans probably won’t be applying at HEB for that gig anytime soon, job security is not really that in this day and age. Already, some sports pages are ramping up the Hot Seat Rankings. Ryans appears in some of them, and he wasn’t dead last in the standing. Unless Houston collapses to 3-4 wins, Ryans should be safe. He is in good standing with the McNairs, and, in theory, he’s bought himself some major credit with three double-digit winning seasons with two division titles and three playoff wins. Is he perfect and make people think of peak Lombardi/Belichick? No, he is not. His seat is not the hottest in the league right now. Granted, if there is increased dissent in the locker room and if Ryans’ in-game decisions continue to backfire, that could quickly change. As for the coordinators…that could be a different story. The most likely guy that will need a LinkedIn update pronto is offensive coordinator Nick Caley. He showed enough improvement after a horrid start to his inaugural season as OC that he was retained. However, some of the trends have returned, and not in a good way. Major short-yardage and red zone issues, especially against the Bengals, returned in force. If the offensive line and running game can’t get on-track, Caley may not make Year 3. He assuredly does not have a lot of defenders here, and there is even some possible discontentment from the players’ side. Coming into this season, defensive coordinator Matt Burke seemed in a great spot. After last season’s successes, especially once he took over defensive play-calling, Burke was on the short list for several head coaching gigs. Then this season started. Even facing Josh Allen and Joe Burrow, the defense has not come close to playing to standard. Not all of that is on the coordinator, but there have been some questions on coverage schemes and play-calls. Should the defense fail to rebound to the standard of the past two seasons, that “NFL” moniker could come for Burke. Remember, previous OC Bobby Slowik went from hot head coaching candidate to practically fired in one season. Frank Ross is arguably the best special teams coordinator the franchise history. Yet, when a team starts 0-3, and when some mid-to-bad special teams play contributes to that start, a lot of that credit gets burned up. As seen with Slowik, it may not take much to go from top of the world to bottom of the heap. However, what might help Ross is that he survived multiple regime changes and if the squad isn’t the root cause of too many losses, he should remain if he so desires. That, and like Caley, he is part of the Caserio circle. Speaking of which, Nick Caserio can lay claim as the primary architect for this iteration of the Texans. Going from a nothing team to three consecutive double-digit winning seasons and three appearances in the Divisional Round in 5+ seasons is not a bad resume header. Yet, the expectations are the highest they’ve been in Houston for years. He’s spent a lot of money and draft capital to improve the squad and fix issues. Given the start to this season, you could say that those efforts haven’t be rewarded. He has a strong relationship with the McNairs as well, but eventually, the team has to get to the championship rounds. He can jettison coordinators and if need be, jettison the head coach. However, how much longer can Caserio stay above the fray? Of course, IT.IS.STILL.EARLY. Freed of the influence of the Easterby, Cal McNair has been a bit more measured in his decisions about the team, but should he feel impatient or too disappointed, or most critically, Hannah decides that a change is needed, then bank on that change happening. Should the team fall to 0-4 or worse, the outcry will only grow louder and the respective Texans’ leaders will only move further up on those “next-to-be-fired” rankings. The team can improve, and they have recent history on their side. However, past performance is no guarantee of future results. Again, all of this is caveated with “it is still early”. However, there is a sense that it is also getting late early. Some wins would really help change this narrative, like starting this weekend.

title: Where to Watch: Colts and Commanders clash in London for Week 4
summary: The Indianapolis Colts (1-2) take on the Washington Commanders (1-2) in London at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium at 9:30 AM EDT for those who didn’t make the trip to ‘The Big Smoke.’ For those looking to watch, it can be viewed on NFL Network nationally, with Dave Pasch (play-by-play), Kurt Warner (analyst), and Jason Kelce (analyst). […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - OCTOBER 30: Jonathan Taylor #28 of the Indianapolis Colts rushes for yards as Rachad Wildgoose #37 of the Washington Commanders looks to tackle him in the third quarter at Lucas Oil Stadium on October 30, 2022 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Dylan Buell/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts (1-2) take on the Washington Commanders (1-2) in London at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium at 9:30 AM EDT for those who didn’t make the trip to ‘The Big Smoke.’ For those looking to watch, it can be viewed on NFL Network nationally, with Dave Pasch (play-by-play), Kurt Warner (analyst), and Jason Kelce (analyst). Streamers can watch on YouTubeTV and NFL+, etc. The NFL Week 4 TV map can be found here . Regarding the Colts fans tuning in, it will be aired on 93.5 and 107.5 The Fan / 97.1 Hank FM, featuring Matt Taylor (play-by-play), Charles Arbuckle (analyst), and Larra Overton (sideline) on the call as usual. For those Sirius XM subscribers, the Horseshoe Faithful can listen in on Channel 813. The Colts come in after arguably a season-saving win, where placekicker Spencer Shrader nailed a 53-yard game-winning field goal attempt with just 16 seconds left to avoid an 0-3 start. The Colts currently rank 15th in points scored (24.0 avg. ppg), while surrendering the 29th most points at 30.3 avg. ppg), with a slight improvement in their defensive ranking from being previously ranked 32nd following Week 2. The Colts are very banged up at wideout with Alec Pierce (heel) already on injured reserve and veteran wideout Keenan Allen (groin) also declared out for this one, as well as fellow wide receiver Ashton Dulin’s status (ankle) still questionable for Sunday regarding his immediate availability. The Colts elevated wideout Nick Westbr00k-Ikhine from their practice squad for additional depth at the wide receiver position for Sunday. Meanwhile, the Commanders will see veteran backup Marcus Mariota make a consecutive start in relief of starter Jayden Daniels (elbow). The veteran backup actually surprisingly played pretty well last weekend against the Seattle Seahawks defense and will be looking to keep that magic going against the Colts. He could be without top Commanders wideout Terry McLaurin (hamstring), a former local Cathedral High School standout, who’s officially designated as “questionable” headed in. The Commanders rank 13th in points for offensively (25.0 avg. ppg.) and 31st in points surrendered (30.7 avg. ppg.), so Indianapolis actually plays an opposing defense early on that’s fared worse than their own to-date. The officiating unit will be lead official Alan Eck and his officiating crew. Regarding London’s projected weather, it’s expected to be warm, bright, and dry with pleasant temperatures around 68 to 70 degrees, which is a bit different than some of the Colts prior games in Europe, where weather conditions have always seemed to be foggy or rainy regarding my memory. The Colts lead the all-time series 21-13-0, with the Commanders winning the last time these two teams met, 17-16, at Lucas Oil Stadium on October 30, 2022, in a much anticipated battle between backup quarterbacks Sam Ehlinger and Taylor Heinicke. Colts Injury Report: WR Keenan Allen (groin)- Out and WR Ashton Dulin (ankle)- Questionable. Commanders Injury Report: S Percy Butler (concussion)- Questionable; WR Terry McLaurin (hamstring)- Questionable; and running back Rachaad White (shoulder)- Out.

title: The Colts’ Strength of Schedule is evolving.
summary: We all know that preseason strength of schedules are not an exact science. They are most often based on the previous year’s record, while sometimes someone will look at projected win totals for the coming year. Those projected win totals are tricky with the .5 associated to each team. What we can say, is that […]
full_text: We all know that preseason strength of schedules are not an exact science. They are most often based on the previous year’s record, while sometimes someone will look at projected win totals for the coming year. Those projected win totals are tricky with the .5 associated to each team. What we can say, is that based on records for this year, our schedule has toughened up slightly. We started out with the 5th easiest schedule, based on the records from last year having a .465 winning pct. It hasn’t changed a ton, but this year our opponents now carry a .472 winning percentage. This leaves 10 teams who play an “easier” schedule, based on this year’s record, than the Colts. Most who watch the Colts with vigor, would say that we have a better offense than defense. That is where our schedule could play out in our favor. We got torched twice for 500+ yards, but those offenses currently rank 2nd and 6th in YPG. Over our last 14 games, we do not play another top 10 offense, based on that metric. The Cowboys come in at #12 and then there are a bundle of mid level teams in the Texans (14), Bengals (15), Steelers (16), followed by the Jaguars (18) and Commanders (19). Of course these rankings are going to change as the season moves along and with the Colts ranking 25th themselves, it doesn’t suggest that we are going to win shootouts. We do play the three teams that currently reside as the bottom three in Minnesota, Tennessee X2, and the Giants. I know that stats can be manipulated to tell most any story that you want to tell, so I am not basing my entire optimistic attitude towards the Colts on these numbers, but if you are out there looking for that ray of hope, this could satisfy your desire. Some will say that all this says is that good teams will still beat us. Teams that fit the profile of a “good team”, might be the Bengals, Eagles, and Jags, as I have a hard time putting the Browns, Giants and Vikings in that group, although Flores does have the Vikings D ballin. So as far as the schedule goes, games are there for the taking. It will be that final nail that many are looking for in Ballard’s coffin, if the Colts can’t produce 11 wins against this schedule. That would mean going 10 – 4 the rest of the way. Those who poo pooed the 8 – 2 start a year ago, will certainly point this year’s schedule as the driving force for such a run. The two games against the Jags might have the final say in our season win total this year. The first step is going 2 – 2 and beating Washington. They appear to be down a few players and will turn to an old Colts adversary in Mariota to try to even their record as well. If we truly are better, we need to show it in the way that we did against lesser teams last year and win convincingly. It will only be one game and will take on less of a “must win” feel than last week’s game, but attitude can be a valuable asset. The more wins that you can put together, the further in the rear view mirror you can put a 9 game losing streak. I believe that our D will ride last week’s better game all the way to London and perform well again. I’m looking for three turnovers to bring the season total to four in four games. You would think that you could cause one per game by accident? If we play with the lead, it will be a long day for the Commanders. Their defense is pretty good against the run, so teams are content to throw against them. If they stack to slow JT, we should be able to make them pay. It would also be nice to get someone behind the defense for a couple of attempts. I have us winning convincingly at 31 – 21.

title: 5 Questions with Hogs Haven: The Tea on Colts vs. Commanders in London
summary: In Week 4 of 2026 our Indianapolis Colts will travel to London to take on the Washington Commanders. Knowing the party was crossing the Atlantic I sat down with Andrew York (eboracum) of Hogs Haven, SB Nation’s Washington Commanders blog. We swapped questions and answers about both the Commanders and Colts and what follows is […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 27: Sonny Styles #52 of the Washington Commanders celebrates his play against the Seattle Seahawks during the second quarter at Northwest Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images In Week 4 of 2026 our Indianapolis Colts will travel to London to take on the Washington Commanders. Knowing the party was crossing the Atlantic I sat down with Andrew York (eboracum) of Hogs Haven , SB Nation’s Washington Commanders blog. We swapped questions and answers about both the Commanders and Colts and what follows is what I’ve learned about this week’s enemy. You can find my answers to his questions here. Chris Shepherd: Based on the first three weeks of the season, if you were an offensive coordinator tasked with creating a game plan to attack the Commanders defense, what does your plan look like? What areas of the field are you attacking, what weaknesses are you targeting? How do you beat this Commanders defense? Andrew York: Well, I’ll start by saying the defense is run by Daronte Jones (not Dan Quinn) and borrows primarily from the Brian Flores defense of the Vikings. It features lots of blitzing, lots of simulated pressures, misdirection, and a complex zone coverage that allows players from any part of the field to either blitz or drop back into coverage. You might normally expect such a defense to be best against the pass, but it is actually strongest at stopping the run, as the last-minute movements and misdirection play havoc with run-blocking keys. As a result, the Commanders are allowing the 3rd-fewest rushing yards (just ahead of the 4th-ranked Vikings) and no rushing TDs so far this season. Where the defense has been weak is against explosive passing plays. I think this is for a few reasons:. 1) the DBs are probably the team’s weakest position group, 2) the complex and shifting zone responsibilities lead to coverage busts by players new to the system, and 3) the scheme just prioritizes sending more people at the QB, which leaves less help on the backend. Due to all of this, my gameplan to attack this defense would be to air out the ball as much as possible. Play 3- or even 4-WR sets (forcing Washington’s worst personnel on the field) and layer their routes to hit all areas of the field, expecting a coverage bust somewhere. I’d particularly target Mike Sainristil in coverage, who has had a rough season and has been relegated to primarily slot CB responsibility. The trick here is to protect your QB well enough to enable him to have time to throw. Dallas and Seattle had good enough pass protection that they could air out the ball to the tune of 279 passing yards and 379 passing yards against us respectively. As a primarily zone defense, the Commanders can also struggle against running QBs, as Jalen Hurts demonstrated in week 1. I know Daniel Jones can make plays with his legs, so using some read option might make sense too. Chris Shepherd: Last week Washington turned in the most surprising upset of the season so far, beating the reigning Super Bowl Champion Seattle Seahawks, 33 to 31. Just looking at the stats of that game, the average person might assume Sam Darnold’s 379 yards passing and four touchdowns would have propelled Seattle over Marcus Mariota’s 183 yard, three touchdown performance but the final score tells a different story. How did the Commanders pull off the upset and do you think those results will be repeatable with Mariota at quarterback? Andrew York: Well the biggest reason is that Washington didn’t give up any turnovers while securing three turnovers that got converted to TDs (including a pick six). It’s a lot easier to score TDs on a short field set up by your defense and that accounted for 20 of Washington’s 33 points (there was a missed extra point). To add a bit more depth to the answer, despite several key injuries, players were executing at a higher level than in previous weeks, which I mostly attribute to good coaching and players on both sides of the ball being more comfortable in new systems. It is also worth noting that both of Washington’s playcallers (OC David Blough and DC Daronte Jones) are new to playcalling in the NFL and I think they’ve had a bit of a learning curve. Although the team lost Jayden Daniels to injury the previous week, Marcus Mariota is one of the better backup QBs in the NFL and has a similar playstyle to Jayden (mobile QB who can read the field well), so the playbook didn’t have to change much to accommodate him. The turnover differential may have been a bit flukey, but I do have confidence in Mariota to continue to play well and lead the team to victory if the defense can continue to keep games within reach. Chris Shepherd: Given that Jayden Daniels might miss week four’s game, I was curious about Washington’s ground game without him. In total the Commanders have rushed for a very solid 396 yards (8th most) on 96 attempts, good for 4.1 yards per carry (ranked 16th in the league) in the first three weeks of the season. If you remove Daniels’ 100 yards on 12 carries, the Commanders drop to 296 rushing yards on 84 carries and a rough 3.5 YPC. Last week’s win over the Seahawks saw the Commanders rush 32 times for 82 yards (a 2.6 YPC average). Is this a concern for Washington’s offense moving forward or did the Seahawks just do a good job bottling up an otherwise decent rushing attack? Andrew York: It’s a bit of a concern and I think there are a few things going on here. First, the OL is decimated by injury right now. LT Laremy Tunsil tore his triceps in Training Camp, forcing the team to move LG Brandon Coleman to LT and weakening both positions. Also, RG Sam Cosmi has been out with a concussion sustained in week 2 (he will not fly to London either). To account for Cosmi’s injury, C Nick Allegretti has moved to RG and Lucas Patrick (signed to the team 2 weeks ago) is starting at Center. So not only has the OL lost its two best players to injury, but 4 players are having to shuffle around to accommodate it. They have still played as a well-coached unit, but that much change has to hurt the run blocking. In addition, it’s not like Washington has sunk a lot of resources into the RB room. The two RBs likely to play significant snaps are Jacory Croskey-Merritt (goes by Bill Merritt) and Rachaad White. Bill is an explosive between-the-tackles runner, but weak in pass protection and as a pass catcher and was a 7th-round pick in 2025, so understood to be a bit of a developmental player. White is a much better pass-catching and pass-protecting back, but used a lot less between the tackles and not great at running through contact and a bit of a journeyman RB. So neither are complete backs or difference makers by themselves and can be a bit easy to gameplan against. Worth noting the team just signed RB Austin Ekeler. It’s unlikely he’ll play this week, but he’d add an explosive element while also being a good pass catcher and pass protector if he is ready to suit up. Chris Shepherd: Can you give me one player on offense and one on defense that Colts fans might not be familiar with who you expect to have an impact on Sunday night? Andrew York: On offense, I’ll go with RT Josh Conerly Jr. He was the 29th pick of the 2025 NFL draft and although he had a bit of an up-and-down rookie season, he got better as the season went on. He’s continued to build on that momentum and has looked like the best player on the OL right now (with Tunsil and Cosmi sidelined). He didn’t allow a single pressure against a great Seahawks pass rush and looks like the best healthy run blocker on the OL. On defense, I’ll go with CB Amik Robertson. He’s a 5’9″ stick of dynamite who flies all over the field making plays and had 6 total tackles, 4 passes defended, and a critical forced fumble against the Seahawks last week. He gave up 3 catches for 46 yards and a TD against Jaxon Smith-Njigba, but didn’t allow a single catch against any other Seahawks…

title: A look back at the Colts’ international game history
summary: The Colts are heading overseas again. Indianapolis will face the Washington Commanders in London in Week 4, marking the franchise’s fourth regular-season international game and its third trip overseas in the last four seasons. What once felt like a rare event has quietly become a fairly regular part of the Colts’ schedule. The franchise has […]
full_text: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 02: Members of the armed forces hold the national flags of the United Kingdom and the United States before the start of the during the NFL game between Indianapolis Colts and Jacksonville Jaguars at Wembley Stadium on October 2, 2016 in London, England. (Photo by Dan Istitene/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Colts are heading overseas again. Indianapolis will face the Washington Commanders in London in Week 4, marking the franchise’s fourth regular-season international game and its third trip overseas in the last four seasons. What once felt like a rare event has quietly become a fairly regular part of the Colts’ schedule. The franchise has played internationally before in the preseason, including a 2005 American Bowl matchup against the Falcons in Tokyo, but the more interesting history begins with the regular-season games. The Colts have already played in London, Frankfurt and Berlin, and they enter this weekend with a 2-1 record outside the United States. Here is a look back at how those regular season games played out before Indianapolis returns to London. 2016: Jaguars 30, Colts 27 — London The Colts’ first regular-season international game came in 2016 against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Wembley Stadium. Indianapolis fell behind 23-6 before making a late push, scoring three touchdowns in the fourth quarter and getting within three points. Andrew Luck threw for 234 yards and two touchdowns, but the comeback fell short as Jacksonville held on for a 30-27 win. It was also an AFC South game, which made the stakes a little different from the usual international matchup. The Colts were technically the road team and left London at 1-3 after a frustrating start to the season. The NFL’s international operation was still much smaller at the time. London games were becoming more common, but Germany had yet to enter the rotation and the league had not expanded its overseas schedule anywhere close to what it looks like today. For the Colts, it was their first taste of regular-season football abroad, and it ended with a loss. 2023: Colts 10, Patriots 6 — Frankfurt Seven years later, the Colts finally returned overseas, this time to Germany. The result was much better, even if the football itself was not particularly memorable. Indianapolis beat New England 10-6 in Frankfurt in one of the stranger games of the 2023 season. Gardner Minshew threw for only 194 yards, the Colts scored one touchdown and the two teams combined for just 16 points. Jonathan Taylor scored Indianapolis’ only touchdown, while the defense did most of the work. The Colts intercepted Mac Jones late in the fourth quarter before New England eventually turned to Bailey Zappe for its final possession. It was not pretty, but nobody asks how an international win looks afterward. The victory gave the Colts their first regular-season win outside the United States and evened their international record at 1-1. 2025: Colts 31, Falcons 25 (OT) — Berlin The Colts did not have to wait another seven years for their next trip. Indianapolis faced Atlanta in Berlin last season, playing in the first NFL regular-season game ever held in the German capital. Unlike the previous two international games, the Colts were the designated home team. This one was easily the most entertaining of the three. The game went to overtime tied at 25 before Indianapolis finished it with a touchdown to earn a 31-25 victory. The win improved the Colts to 2-1 internationally and gave them consecutive victories in Germany after the 2023 win in Frankfurt. It was also part of what has become a much larger NFL push into Europe. Germany has quickly become one of the league’s biggest international markets, and the Colts have now been involved in games in two different German cities. For a franchise that went seven years between its first and second regular-season international appearances, the trips have suddenly started piling up. 2026: Back to London If the previous three trips are any indication, expecting another close game would make sense. Every Colts regular-season international game has been decided by six points or fewer. They lost 30-27 to Jacksonville in 2016, beat New England 10-6 in Frankfurt and needed overtime to beat Atlanta 31-25 in Berlin last season. The settings have changed, the opponents have changed and the quality of football has certainly varied, but the Colts have never had an easy afternoon overseas. Even the 2023 Patriots game, which was not exactly an offensive showcase, stayed undecided until the final minutes. There is also an element of unpredictability that comes with these games. The travel schedule is different, the routine during the week changes and both teams are playing in an environment they do not normally experience during the season. That does not automatically make every international game close, but the Colts’ history suggests they have rarely been comfortable either way. Indianapolis comes into this one trying to build off its win over Houston after an 0-2 start, so another one-score game would hardly be surprising. The Colts have already played two tight games in the last two weeks, and their international history has followed the same pattern. Ten years after their first London trip, the Colts are back in England with a 2-1 regular-season international record and a chance to make it three straight wins overseas. Based on how their previous trips have gone, they may have to sweat through another one to get there.

title: Let’s Argue: This current Chiefs roster can win the Super Bowl
summary: In our “Let’s Argue” series, Mark Gunnels considers the hot takes, wacky predictions and unpopular opinions of Kansas City Chiefs fans from all over the world. Chief Among Them says: This a good team that can win a Super Bowl with the current roster as is. I’ve been saying it — this Chiefs team is […]
full_text: (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images In our “Let’s Argue” series, Mark Gunnels considers the hot takes, wacky predictions and unpopular opinions of Kansas City Chiefs fans from all over the world. Chief Among Them says: This a good team that can win a Super Bowl with the current roster as is. I’ve been saying it — this Chiefs team is absolutely good enough to win it all. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes finally has a legit running game with running back Kenneth Walker, the weapons around him are better, and tight end Travis Kelce still looks like he has plenty left in the tank. Defensively, they haven’t even played their best football yet, and they’re still 3-0 with a top-five defense in EPA per play. If the young guys on defense keep developing and this team stays healthy, there’s no reason KC shouldn’t be right there at the end. IndianolaChiefsFan says: The massive upgrade at RB is enough to get us in the playoffs, and Mahomes is enough to get us past most/all of the AFC teams. I think Buffalo is the only real challenge in the AFC. I agree the Buffalo Bills are the biggest threat because Josh Allen will always make them dangerous, especially in January. But I’m not sleeping on the Jacksonville Jaguars either — they’ve got enough talent on both sides of the ball to be a real problem in the AFC. That said, if the Chiefs get to the postseason healthy with Mahomes, an improved running game, and a defense that keeps developing, I’ll take my chances against anybody. MTChief says: Tyreek Hill will sign with the Chiefs and have 750 total yards and 7 touchdowns. Is that hot enough? It’s hard for me to put numbers on Tyreek because we still don’t know exactly when — or even if — he’ll be available. If I had to guess, I’d say sometime in early-to-mid November, and at that point you’re talking about joining a team halfway through the season. I don’t know if he gets to 750 yards, but if he’s healthy, I absolutely believe he could still give the Chiefs another explosive element for a playoff run. And with the way this offense is already playing, they wouldn’t need him to come in and be the old Tyreek Hill.

title: Chris Jones thinks the arrow is pointing up for Sack Nation
summary: Star defensive lineman and CEO of Sack Nation, a defensive subsidiary of their parent company, the Kansas City Chiefs, which specializes in security infiltration, spoke to media members Thursday afternoon. Jones admitted the early returns haven’t been what the company hoped for this fiscal year; so far this season, the Chiefs have accumulated only four […]
full_text: (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images Star defensive lineman and CEO of Sack Nation, a defensive subsidiary of their parent company, the Kansas City Chiefs , which specializes in security infiltration, spoke to media members Thursday afternoon. Jones admitted the early returns haven’t been what the company hoped for this fiscal year; so far this season, the Chiefs have accumulated only four sacks. Jones acknowledged that Sack Nation has faced a unique set of circumstances while trying to achieve its ultimate goal: tackling the quarterback behind the line of scrimmage while he still has the ball in his hand. “We’re close, statistically-wise,” Jones told reporters. “You look at the numbers, the quarterback has been getting rid of the ball [in] 2.3 seconds. I don’t care how good of a pass rusher you are, when they’re throwing the ball that quick, it’s tough for anyone,” Jones explained. To make matters worse, he added that when the opposition holds onto the ball to take a shot downfield, they keep extra men back to bolster their line and prevent any incursion. “You got seven, eight men in there protecting,” Jones said. “So, it’s like, the opportunity is going to come. I think don’t waver from what we’ve been doing. We’ve done a lot of good. We put a lot of good on film. I think we stay committed to that and just find ways to get sacks out of it so y’all can stop writing about us in the media.” Chiefs DT Chris Jones on the D-Line's pressure and sack stats so far this season: "It gives y'all another week to write the Chiefs defensive lineman suck." #ChiefsKingdom pic.twitter.com/XNEPZCmg8y — Rob Collins (@RobCollinsTV) October 1, 2026 The job doesn’t get any easier this week, when Jones and his team take on the Las Vegas Raiders . The Raiders have only allowed five sacks through three games this season and are tied for the NFL lead in passing touchdowns with nine. Part of the Raiders’ success is also due to their quarterback, Kirk Cousins, getting the ball out of his hands quickly this season. Through Week 3, Cousins has the seventh-fastest time to throw in the NFL in 2026 at 2.58 seconds. The Chiefs will need to get home and pressure Cousins to disrupt his rhythm in the passing game. Not just because it will help Sack Nation improve its bottom line, but also because the alternative is another week of media stories about Sack Nation underperforming. “It’ll just give you another week to write about the Chiefs defensive linemen suck and why did you all pay me and George (Karlaftis).”

title: The Rams tried to get you to stop talking about special teams
summary: The Los Angeles Rams feigned a newfound commitment to special teams this offseason. Through three games the curtain has been pulled back on a unit that is structurally still the same. Kicker Harrison Mevis is reliable, although he lacks range and all kickers miss field goals. He’s a low-aimed shot and underscores the complacency across […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 15: Wide receiver Xavier Smith #19 of the Los Angeles Rams returns a punt in the fourth quarter in an NFL preseason game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams feigned a newfound commitment to special teams this offseason. Through three games the curtain has been pulled back on a unit that is structurally still the same. Kicker Harrison Mevis is reliable, although he lacks range and all kickers miss field goals. He’s a low-aimed shot and underscores the complacency across the third phase. Punter Ethan Evans has held his job for four years without ever really being challenged. He hasn’t earned this right. It was effectively handed to him even when his production screams worthy of an upgrade. Evans has a big leg sure, but that does little to help the team if he cannot consistently take advantage. LA tried to distract us with special teams additions during free agency. They told us last year that their field goal unit struggles were really the long snapper’s fault. Maybe that is true. At least they did their best to fix it by bringing in veteran Joe Cardona. The Rams also signed Grant Stuard to be a special teams ace. He’s just one guy on a unit of either 10 coverage players or protectors. How much can that realistically move the needle? Very little it turns out. The most confusing decision of all was the election to stay put with their return man Xavier Smith. The Rams asked for a do-over this week when they waived Smith and named Alex Bachman as his new replacement. If only someone saw this issue coming . It was all a magic trick. A sleight of hand. The Rams grabbed our attention over here while their special teams infrastructure was still crumbling from within. A new coat of paint does not fix the structural issues. They are still there. LA’s special teams will continue to struggle until they make an overhaul a true priority. Free agent signings alone aren’t enough. Most teams reserve the later rounds of the draft for players who are not equipped to contribute on offense or defense right away and instead focus on roles in the third phase. The Rams have not taken that approach for the better part of the last decade. It shows. We cannot continue to fall for the misdirection. There were no real signs that special teams were going to improve this season, outside of a couple superficial changes. The problem is the approach. It’s something the team will need to revisit next offseason. They botched the most recent opportunity.

title: Rams and Eagles enter Sunday in rough shape
summary: Sunday’s matchup between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Los Angeles Rams is an important game in the NFC conference. It could realistically be a playoff preview. Neither team is at full force. The Eagles have an injury list that is a mile long. The Rams’ is shorter, although that’s because they ruled out multiple key […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 11: Puka Nacua #12 of the Los Angeles Rams is tackled in the first quarter of the NFL football game against San Francisco 49ers at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) | Getty Images Sunday’s matchup between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Los Angeles Rams is an important game in the NFC conference. It could realistically be a playoff preview. Neither team is at full force. The Eagles have an injury list that is a mile long. The Rams’ is shorter, although that’s because they ruled out multiple key players on a longer term basis. Rams injuries: Puka Nacua returns. He has missed the last two games after fighting through a training camp injury in Week 1. Questions remain regarding how often we will see Nacua, whether he will be the focal point of the passing game, and if he looks like the same dominant performer. On a less encouraging note, LA will be without Aaron Donald. Jaylen Watson also joins him on the defensive side of the ball. The Rams were already missing Myles Garrett. They now lose two of their other star newcomers for this week. At least Kamren Kinchens is set to play after missing the last two games. The secondary needs all the help it can get after Josh Wallace struggled in replacement of Watson. On offense, TE Colby Parkinson is questionable for the second week in a row. He was very limited in the last game against the Denver Broncos. Terrance Ferguson was placed on injured reserve and will now miss the next month at a minimum. If Parkinson is limited again, we may see some of second-round rookie Max Klare. Eagles injuries: Philly will be without three key pass catchers for this game: DeVonta Smith, Dallas Goedert, and Hollywood Brown. At receiver, this leaves Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon, Elijah Moore, Darius Cooper, and Britain Covey. The Rams will see a former teammate in Johnny Mundt to replace Goedert along with EJ Jenkins. Veteran Zach Ertz was signed to the practice squad and could be a contributor. On the defensive side of the ball, the Eagles are missing Zack Baun and safety Marcus Epps. Baun is a pain for opposing offenses. He is flexible as a coverage player and physical against the run. Sean McVay will not be disappointed to evade him this week. What a win means for each team The NFC West is more competitive than the NFC East. The Eagles at 2-1 are currently tied with the Giants for the division lead, although New York does not have a quarterback and it would be surprising to see them keep pace with Philly. Meanwhile the Rams are already losing ground to the San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks. The 49ers are unbeaten. Seattle dropped a surprise game to the Commanders. LA is tied for last with the Arizona Cardinals. So, in other words, the Rams need a win to get back to .500. They’ll have an uphill battle without several key contributors, although the rest of the roster remains talented enough to get the job done. Their healthy star players need to perform at their expected levels. Both teams are short-handed. The Rams need a win more. Will that be on display Sunday?

title: College football game day: Tell the forum who you like
summary: Undefeated teams are down to 21 and the season hasn’t reached the mid-point as of yet. Four head-to head matchup’s this weekend amongst teams that have yet to be beat. These are the 10 games TST will be monitoring, but feel free to weigh in on any game or prospects that strike your fancy. All […]
full_text: I have Notre Dame safety Adon Shuler rising on my draft board (Photo by Michael Miller/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images Undefeated teams are down to 21 and the season hasn’t reached the mid-point as of yet. Four head-to head matchup’s this weekend amongst teams that have yet to be beat. These are the 10 games TST will be monitoring, but feel free to weigh in on any game or prospects that strike your fancy. All times PDT #3 Notre Dame (4-0) @ North Carolina (2-1) 9 am on ESPN Eyes on: The Fighting Irish secondary is filled with high-end talent. Corners Leonard Moore, DJ McKinney, and Christian Gray. At safety, Tae Johnson and Adon Shuler. North Carolina wants to control the game with the run and short passes, but TE Jelani Thurman is a live one for the NFL draft. #7 Alabama (4-0) @ #16 Mississippi State (4-0) 9 am on ABC Eyes on: You have to go back to the Dak Prescott days since Mississippi State has been a challenge to ‘Bama. Freshman QB Kamario Taylor is the NCAA darling right now for the Bulldogs. He works behind a big offensive line anchored by G DJ Chester and C Canon Boone. Alabama answers with sophomore QB Keelon Russell. For the Tide defense E Yahonzae Pierre DT Devan Thompkins, and CB Zabien Brown all draw long looks from scouts. Central Florida (3-1) @ Houston (3-1) 9 am on ESPN2 Eyes on: UCF wants to run the ball behind Duke Watson and Landen Chambers, but QB Alonza Barnett can sling it as well. WR Josh Derry and TE Dylan Wade are his go-to guys. Houston is triggered by QB Conner Weigman throwing to Amare Thomas and Trent Walker. Makhi Huges handles the ground game. #5 Ohio State (4-0) @ #14 Iowa (4-0) 12:30 pm on CBS Eyes on: The Buckeyes have a deep secondary. Corners Jermaine Matthews, Cam Calhoun, and Devin Sanchez team with safeties Earl Little, Jaylin McClain, and Terry Moore. The Hawkeyes are once again strong on the offensive line, boasting two Round 1 probables, Cade Pieper and Trevor Lauck. #8 Florida (4-0) @ #25 Missouri (3-1) 12:30 pm on ABC Eyes on: Gators aren’t getting a lot of publicity, but Jaden Baugh is the best running back in the college game. A three-tight end rotation of Amir Jackson, Lacota Dipper, and Luke Harpring can block and catch. Missouri has Austin Simmona at QB, he was the starter and was injured at Ole Miss, opening the door for the rise of Trinidad Chambliss. Tiger star RB Ahmad Hardy is still recovering from a gunshot, but backup Jamal Roberts can tote it. Auburn (3-1) @ #17 Tennessee (3-1) 12:30 pm ESPN Eyes on: Which of these teams is for real? Tigers new head coach Alex Golesh brought his fast-paced offense and a grip of players with him from South Florida, So far, dual threat QB Byrum Brown hasn’t lit up scoreboards, still, he’s fun to watch. Tennessee has a pair top-tier running backs, Desean Bishop and Daune Morris to compliment dual threat QB Faizon Brandon. #4 Miami (4-0) @ Clemson (3-1) 4:30 pm on ABC Eyes on: Miami is loaded with talent, so I’ll mention some sleepers— T Mike McCoy, TE Elijah Lofton, CB Ethan O’Conner, and E Marquise Lightfoot. Clemson boasts some top talent as well, E Will Heldt, ILB Sammy Brown, and CB Ashton Hampton are all early round draft candidates. Washington (3-1) @ #18 USC (4-1) 4:30 on NBC Eyes on: Huskies QB Demond Williams can beat you running and throwing. Soph WR Dezman Roebuck is a star in the making. T Drew Azzopardi and the Hatchett brothers, Gieran and Landen power the offensive line. USC fell apart in the final eight minutes of the Oregon game and needs to rebound. QB Jayden Maiava must show scouts he can come back from adversity. RB’s King Miller and Wayman Jordan will have to do the same with the Trojans WR corps hurting. #6 Indiana (4-0) @ Rutgers (1-3) 5 pm on BIG10 Network Eyes on: QB Josh Hoover has arguably as good or better background coming into the Curt Cignetti-led Hoosiers program than Fernando Mendoza and Kurtis Rourke. It will be interesting to see how much his draft stock will raise (or fall) as the season progresses. Rutgers is struggling with their QB’s and had two close losses, but WR KJ Duff and RB Antwan Raymond are the real deal. Cincinnati (4-0) @ Arizona (3-1) 8 pm on FOX Eyes on: Let’s close the night with a shootout, both teams have wide-open offenses. Bearcat QB JC French is a senior transfer that can throw/run. RB’s Gi’Bran Payne and Cole Tabb form a potent one-two punch. S Antwan Peek and CB Jacob Finley are tough in the secondary. Arizona QB Noah Fifita is small, but mighty. He’s thrown for over 10,000 yards in his career. WR Tre Spivey is a real sleeper.

full_text: Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford (9) readies to snap the ball against the Philadelphia Eagles (Photo by Kyle Ross/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Looking to even the ledger after a 1-2 start to the season, the Los Angeles Rams travel across country to the east coast to do battle with the 2-1 Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday October 5. Kickoff is set for 10 a.m. PDT at Lincoln Financial Field in South Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The fall weather will be much more temperate than a winter date. Although full clouds are expected and a 60 percent chance of rain is forecast, temperatures are expected to be in the mid-60’s with mild wind conditions, 7 to 14 miles per hour. It was 1937, when the Rams were based in Cleveland that the series with Philly had its origins. The pair have squared off 47 times over that span with the Eagles holding a 26-20-1 advantage and have out-scored L.A. 983 to 961. Since Sean McVay took the Rams reins in 2017, Philadelphia has been the bane of his coaching existence, winning six of the seven matchup’s and the last four in a row. Both teams have been bitten by the injury bug early and several starters have been ruled out of Sunday’s tilt. For the Eagles, tight end Dallas Goedert and receiver’s Devonta Smith and Hollywood Brown will be absent from an offense that is in the NFL’s Bottom 10 in scoring and total yards. Defensive starters designated as out are linebacker Zach Baun and safety Marcus Epps. Tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle), cornerback Jaylen Watson (shoulder), and defensive tackle Aaron Donald (back) won’t play for the Rams, while tight end Colby Parkinson and edge Josaiah Stewart are questionable. Ferguson will join edge Myles Garrett and offensive linemen Justin Dedich and Keagan Trost on the Injured Reserve List, all were expected to be prominent pieces in the 2026 season. L.A. also waived their primary kick returner, Xavier Smith, earlier this week. Here’s how to follow the game! Location: Lincoln Financial Field in South Philadelphia, Pa. title: Puka Nacua expected back Sunday for Rams, Aaron Donald out
summary: The Los Angeles Rams are expected to have Puka Nacua back in the fold, but just as they perhaps get Nacua back, Aaron Donald is out. The Rams will have to find a way to overcome with or without Donald, and they still won’t have Myles Garrett. It’s another example of this team not playing […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams are expected to have Puka Nacua back in the fold, but just as they perhaps get Nacua back, Aaron Donald is out. The Rams will have to find a way to overcome with or without Donald, and they still won’t have Myles Garrett. It’s another example of this team not playing the way so many envisioned before the start of the season. The idea was a team of star players all playing at together. That hasn’t happened yet. There’s still time, but in the NFL there’s never enough time. The Rams need to get healthy fast, and they need to win faster if they want to make the postseason. Talk of the “superteam” is no more. Rams’ Aaron Donald to miss Week 4 game vs. Eagles, Puka Nacua’s status updated (cbssports) “Donald unretired this offseason, returning to play for his former team after initially retiring in 2023. The three-time Defensive Player of the Year’s return has not been as smooth as he or the team had hoped. He sat out the opener when the Rams fell to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia, and Sunday will mark his second missed game of the season. Head coach Sean McVay said Donald felt soreness in his back after the team’s Week 3 loss to the Denver Broncos . “He’s working as hard as he can to get himself feeling as good as possible. And we’re hopeful and optimistic that good days are ahead,” McVay said. When Donald is healthy, he is an offense’s worst nightmare. The 35-year-old’s resume includes a Super Bowl win, eight first-team All-Pro nods and 10 Pro Bowl selections. He has 547 tackles, 111 sacks, 24 forced fumbles and seven fumble recoveries over 11 seasons in his career.“ Rams DT Aaron Donald, TE Terrance Ferguson ruled out vs. Eagles (ramswire) “The Los Angeles Rams will be missing several key playmakers against the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday afternoon. Sean McVay told reporters on Friday that Aaron Donald and Terrance Ferguson have both been ruled out due to injuries. Donald is dealing with a sore back and Ferguson injured his ankle last week against the Denver Broncos . Additionally, Jaylen Watson has been ruled out, as expected. Donald’s injury seemingly came out of nowhere. McVay said on Wednesday that he had a sore back and would not practice, but it didn’t appear to be anything serious. It’s unclear when or how the injury occurred. Ferguson went down twice in last week’s loss to the Broncos, injuring his ankle in the first quarter and then again in the second after returning.“ Sean McVay speaks on special teams updates, keys to beating the Eagles, Puka Nacua’s return & more (therams.com) “Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay shares an update on special teams, wide receiver Puka Nacua’s Week 4 practice reps, discusses keys to beating the Philadelphia Eagles, and more.” Rams players share favorite Spanish phrase in hilarious video ahead of Eagles matchup (sports.yahoo) “While the cameras caught a lighthearted moment at practice, the Rams are likely locked in for Sunday’s game . The Eagles are coming into the Week 4 matchup off a surprising loss to the Bears, who deployed backup quarterback Case Keenum with Caleb Williams out with a hamstring injury. Likewise, the Rams lost a game that was seemingly over by halftime as LA led the Broncos, 16-0. But as Rams fans likely want to forget, Denver scored all of its 30 points in the second half to orchestrate an improbable comeback against the preseason Super Bowl favorites.“ Rams Cut Ties With Fourth-Year Wide Receiver After Blunt Message (sports.yahoo) “”I would say, overall, he’s been inconsistent. We need to do a better job of tracking the ball, judging the ball, fielding the ball when necessary, not fielding it in other situations. He knows that, and hopefully we’ll get the improvements that we need in that area,” Ventrone told reporters on October 1, saying there were “no” thoughts of replacing Smith. “We have a lot of trust in X. I really do. He’s put in a lot of time and effort in training camp, then, obviously, moving into the season. I think that he’ll do the necessary things to be able to sustain at that position for us.” Sean McVay is 0-4 against Nick Sirianni (nbcsports) “Rams coach Sean McVay has had tremendous success since becoming a head coach in 2017. Against one specific coach, McVay has struggled. Via NBC Sports research, McVay has an 0-4 record against Eagles coach Nick Sirianni. McVay gets his next chance to get his first win over Sirianni on Sunday in Philadelphia. The 1-2 Rams desperately need to avoid falling to 1-3. In 2023, the Eagles and Sirianni beat the Rams and McVay in L.A., 23-14. The next year, the Eagles won again in L.A., 37-20.“ Los Angeles Rams Among 3 NFL Teams In Desperate Need Of Week 4 Win (sports.yahoo) “No one expected the Los Angeles Chargers to start off 0-3, and yet, that’s where Jim Harbaugh’s squad finds itself heading into Week 4. To make matters worse, the 2026 schedule won’t get any easier. On Sunday, the Chargers will take on the Seattle Seahawks on the road. They’ll be serious underdogs for that matchup – and rightfully so. If the Chargers are going to save their season, they’ll need Justin Herbert to put on his Superman cape this weekend.“ Are the 0-3 Houston Texans already cooked? Plus, the emergence of Greg Rousseau and Dallas Turner (nfl.com) “The Houston Texans have climbed out of the grave multiple times during DeMeco Ryans’ tenure to ultimately claim a playoff berth. The team’s resilience, toughness and unwavering self-belief helped it overcome an 0-3 start in 2025 to finish at 12-5 and reach a third straight Divisional Round. One year later, Houston is back at 0-3. And this Sunday , the team plays host to the similarly disappointing (and desperate) Dallas Cowboys. Given the firepower the 1-2 ‘Boys possess, it’s not hard to imagine them leaving Reliant Stadium with the win. That would most likely represent a death blow to the Texans. Just look at this note from NFL Research: Since 1990, 109 teams have started a season at 0-4, and only one has gone on to make the playoffs. That lone outlier? The 1992 San Diego Chargers. They actually won 11 of their final 12 games to take the AFC West, providing a modicum of hope for the modern-day Texans. But do I actually believe Houston is poised for such a dramatic turnaround? Color me skeptical — HIGHLY skeptical. The Texans need to right the ship right now . They must immediately fix their biggest issues and lean into the rugged identity that has helped them bludgeon opponents in recent seasons. When this team’s at its best, the hard-hitting defense sets the tone for a roster that excels at complementary football. At the moment, Houston is nowhere near that brand of ball.“ NFL Week 4 bold predictions: Brock Bowers cooks Chiefs; Zay Flowers leads all fantasy scorers (nfl.com) “The Rams and Eagles treated the football world to one of the best games of the 2025 season , a 33-26 thriller that saw Eagles nose tackle Jordan Davis return a blocked field goal 61 yards for a touchdown as time expired. This Sunday, it’s déjà vu at The Linc. The gargantuan Davis finds the end zone again, this time on a scoop-and-score off a strip sack of Matthew Stafford .“ Eagles’ loss of Devonta Smith and supporting cast is only for the Rams gain after Aaron Donald’s out ruling (sports.yah00) “Just two days after the Rams announced that wide receiver Puka Nacua was back with the team practicing, head coach Sean McVay took the podium before practice and announced the team will be without three-time Defensive Player of the Year winner Aaron Donald. Donald, who is out with back soreness , has not had the post two-year retirement renaissance that he had hoped for. He has yet to log a snap playing alongside Myles Garrett — who is on the team’s injured reserve due to a knee injury he suffered in Week 1 against the San Francisco 49ers. Donald has also only made four tackles this year, despite still being a factor in the team’s pass rush, as PFF has him ranked with a 74.8 grade .“ Comment of the Day: “Stafford has…
