title: College Football 2026: Draft prospects for the NY Giants in Week 5
summary: Good morning New York Giants fans! Happy Saturday and welcome to Week 5 of the college football season! We’re really starting to get into the meat of the college season, with more matchups between ranked opponents and divisional games starting to become more common. These matchups of “good against good” give us some of our […]
full_text: Good morning New York Giants fans! Happy Saturday and welcome to Week 5 of the college football season! We’re really starting to get into the meat of the college season, with more matchups between ranked opponents and divisional games starting to become more common. These matchups of “good against good” give us some of our best games must-watch scouting tape, and I’m here for it. This week we have a match-up between Alabama and Mississippi State that could be a preview of the 2028 and 2029 first overall picks. And while I encourage everyone to watch that game, I won’t be spotlighting it. As usual, we’re using the draft as a lens through which to view the Giants, and there are intriguing players at positions of need at other schools. And as usual, use this as your discussion post for all of today’s games. So let’s get to it. North Carolina vs. (3) Notre Dame ESPN – noon Player spotlight: DJ McKinney (CB, Notre Dame) I’ll keep it real with everyone: If I was going to recommend one game to watch in the noon slot, it’s (17) Mississippi State vs. (7) Alabama. The two young quarterbacks in that game are absolutely electric and ‘Bama is well stocked with future NFL talent. But I want to take the opportunity to highlight one of the very best secondaries in college football in Notre Dame. Pretty much everyone will be watching star CB Leonard Moore, who has the upside to rival Pat Surtain II… But the hope is that the Giants won’t be anywhere near bad enough to draft him. Instead, I want to focus on his teammate, DJ McKinney. McKinney has good size at 6-foot-1, 190 pounds and the traits to be a press-man corner in the NFL. He started his college career at Oklahoma State before transferring to Colorado for the 2024 and 2025 seasons, and finally finishing his career at Notre Dame. He already has 4 total tackles, 2 passes defensed, and a Pick-6 on the season. McKinney may be overshadowed by Moore, but he’s an interesting player to keep an eye on as a Day 2 prospect for the Giants. (14) Iowa vs. (5) Ohio State CBS – 3:30 p.m. Player spotlight: Kade Pieper (OC, Iowa) The Giants’ tackle and guard spots are solidified for the foreseeable future, however we don’t know if John Michael Schmitz will earn a contract extension. If he doesn’t, it’s tough to go wrong with offensive linemen from Iowa. Pieper is probably the best natural interior lineman in this draft class, and while he’s undersized at 6-foot-3, 298 pounds, he’s a tough, tenacious blocker. It’s also worth noting that John Harbaugh has had some decent success with undersized but athletic Iowa centers… Tyler Linderbaum measured in at 6-foot-2, 296 pounds, with 31-inch arms. Pieper typically blocks with the kind of technique we’ve come to expect from Hawkeyes’ linemen, and his athleticism fits well in zone schemes as well as man-gap schemes that ask the center to pull. That could make him an intriguing fit in Greg Roman’s multiple (but power-centric) run schemes, as well as a capable pass protector. I also want to call attention to the potential matchup between Iowa DB Zach Lutmer and star WR Jeremiah Smith. Smith is, pretty universally, considered the best player in the country and is generally considered in the “Calvin Johnson and Julio Jones” tier of wide receiver prospect. This is a fantastic opportunity for Lutmer to raise his profile, and could also give us some great tape on Smith. Clemson vs. (4) Miami ABC – 7:30 p.m. Player spotlight – Ahmad Moten Sr. (iDL, Miami) Regardless of how well the Giants’ defensive line plays over the rest of the season, the Giants need to continue to add to the unit in 2027. The good news is that if they don’t go the free agent route, this looks like a talented defensive line class. We’ve already talked about a few defensive linemen in this class, and now I want to bring up one who could be an option on the second day of the draft. Moten has solid size at 6-foot-3, and roughly 310 pounds, with an explosive lower body and powerful upper body. He has enough strength to stand up offensive linemen and control gaps, as well as the athleticism to shoot those gaps and disrupt in the backfield. He also uses his strength well to discard blocks and make plays on ball carriers. The Giants need more from their interior pass rush, and Moten’s explosiveness, technique, and wide-open motor make him a disruptive defender on passing downs. The Giants’ defensive line has been more stout than some anticipated. However it needs more long-term answers, as well as players who can disrupt and prevent quarterbacks from stepping up into the pocket.
author: Chris Pflum

title: Giants vs. Cardinals: Which Arizona team is the real one?
summary: With the New York Giants facing the Arizona Cardinals this week we turn to Seth Cox of SB Nation’s Revenge of the Birds for our weekly ‘5 questions’ segment. Ed: Which is likely the more realistic version of the Cardinals. The team that lost 31-7 to the Seattle Seahawks or the team that pushed the […]
full_text: Jeremiyah Love taking the field. | Getty Images With the New York Giants facing the Arizona Cardinals this week we turn to Seth Cox of SB Nation’s Revenge of the Birds for our weekly ‘5 questions’ segment. Ed: Which is likely the more realistic version of the Cardinals. The team that lost 31-7 to the Seattle Seahawks or the team that pushed the San Francisco 49ers in a 36-30 loss? Seth: That is the million dollar question for the Arizona Cardinals. We knew the defense would be an issue, more on that later, but we expected a little more from the offense. The Cardinals threw the ball 52 times for 280 yards against the Niners. Again, the stats 280 yards and two passing touchdowns are good, but their pass game is basically a really good run game. They are the second-worst team in explosive plays and they almost play not to lose, as opposed to make big plays and put pressure on the opposition. It also tends to coincide with big deficits, so teams are willing to allow them to beat them with a death by thousand cuts, because it runs so much time and they know their own offense will go in and score immediately. Ed: The Giants drafted Saquon Barkley No. 2 overall in 2018, and as great as he was there were also mixed feelings about that. How do fans feel about the selection of Jeremiyah Love, and does it look like he will justify being the third overall pick in the draft? Seth: This is a little hard to explain. I think 95% of fans are positive in the sense that Jeremiyah Love was a blue chip prospect and looks like he will be very good to great in the NFL. However, I feel like it is 50/50 at best if fans agree with the usage of that pick for that position, when you are looking at maybe the worst defense in the NFL that is not actively trying to tank like the Dolphins. Arvell Reese, Sonny Styles, heck even Caleb Downs may have helped more in the immediate, but I don’t think that means anyone is overthinking it right now, but they are definitely going to continue to monitor things. Ed: If you could take one player off the Giants’ roster and put him in Arizona’s lineup, who would it be? Why? Seth: Well, now that Brian Burns is gone, I think it would be Jermaine Eluemunor. The Cardinals desperately need help at the right tackle position and Eluemunor has not only a claim as the best right tackle in the NFL, but maybe as the best tackle overall. That would help the above problem with the pick of Jeremiyah Love and the lack of explosive offensive plays… right? Ed: What are your early thoughts on Mike LaFleur as a head coach? Does he look like a guy who could be Arizona’s coach for a while? Seth: Unfortunately for the Cardinals, LaFleur is on the clock as soon as he starts. The average tenure of a Cardinals head coach since they moved to Arizona is three years. Not many coaches get past that, and the ones that do usually flame out very early into their second contract, if they even start that second contract. That being said, outside of procedural/pre-snap penalties, LaFleur looks more than capable of being a really good head coach in the NFL. So much so that you feel at times like this could be the coach that bucks the trend of misfortune for the Cardinals head coaches. But they need to clean things up, and then show they can compete within their own division for him to have any real shot as being the long-term answer. Ed: The Cardinals are a slight favorite. If the Giants are going to win, what would that look like? What weaknesses can the Giants exploit? Seth: Does your team have a quarterback/running back/offensive talent? If so, then this could be your lucky day, as the Cardinals defense has been mostly bad, and sometimes downright atrocious this season. Think about this stat from the Cardinals 36-30 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, the Cardinals ran 31 more plays and possessed the ball 17 more minutes than the Niners… and the 49ers outgained them by 72 yards. That is really unfathomable. So, if the Cardinals defense doesn’t find a way to slow down what has been an impotent offense of the Giants since the injury to Jaxson Dart, I don’t know how they can stop any team’s offense. And also, I don’t see them stopping the Giants offense. They did okay against the Chargers, but I think with how well the Giants are coached, and how much they can run the ball, something the Cardinals cannot stop, it will be an interesting game. Stop the short passes by Jacoby Brissett, make him stand in the pocket and try and push the ball down the field and live with the results. On offense, hand the ball to Cam Skattebo and Najee Harris and work the play action game. If you do all of that, the game will be competitive and the Giants as home dogs may look silly. Good luck and good health in this one.
author: Ed Valentine

title: New York Giants mailbag: J.J. McCarthy, cornerback help, Arvell Reese, more
summary: Lawrence Kenney asks: With the trade for McCarthy, we assume his rookie contract, but does it include his option year? Assuming we can help rehabilitate his career, this could be an attractive trade chip.  Ed says: Yes, the Giants also get the fifth-year option. It is part of the standard rookie contract for first-round picks. […]
full_text: Lawrence Kenney asks: With the trade for McCarthy, we assume his rookie contract, but does it include his option year? Assuming we can help rehabilitate his career, this could be an attractive trade chip. Ed says: Yes, the Giants also get the fifth-year option. It is part of the standard rookie contract for first-round picks. Jim Eggers asks: Please explain to me how Nubin can look so absolutely clueless playing safety in the NFL. He had a great college career at Minnesota. Senior year 1st team All American with 13 career interceptions and was a tackling machine. A plug and play guy for sure, right. Not exactly. In the NFL he has no coverage skills, he is very slow, no situational awareness, just overmatched. No coaching will help this guy. Ed says: Jim, I think you are being a bit harsh. Tyler Nubin has clearly not been the player the Giants hoped he would be when they drafted him. He has been below average, and has not been the ball-hawking playmaker the Giants thought they were getting. You make it seem as though he doesn’t belong in the league. I’m not willing to go there. Rob Stolzer asks: With Burns now out for the year, will we be seeing Reese shifted over to the edge position for more plays? Ed says: Rob, it is an option. Pro Football Focus says Reese has aligned outside on 30 of 177 snaps (16.9%). Maybe that ticks up some based on situations. There have been times when Reese and Abdul Carter have switches, simply to get Carter pass rushing over a guard. Reese, though, will remain primarily an inside linebacker. Honestly, the pass rush remains an underdeveloped area of Reese’s game. Per PFF, he has rushed just 17 times so far. His 5.9% pressure rate is 137th out of 200 grades off-ball linebackers or edge defenders. That is a small sample size, but perhaps an indication that Reese is a work in progress as a pass rusher. I think the Giants signed Jihad Ward to be their third edge defender. Kölnerbigblue asks: Ed, I probably missed it but I don’t remember much hype about Holland in the off season other than the Leadership Council and the contract extension. There were other players (e.g. Carter, Reese, and Sisi) I remember people talking about but not so much Holland. He’s emerging as a leader on and off the field. What did I miss? Ed says: Kölner, you didn’t miss anything. Holland didn’t make a lot of plays for the Giants a year ago, and since his career-high in interceptions for a season was two entering this year there was doubt he would become a big-time playmaker. Well, he has. Chase Baldwin asks: We traded for J.J. McCarthy in the wake of this I saw BBV split between this is horrendous, and he’ll be taking over starting soon. A few people sat in the middle and think he’s a fine #2. My question is word got out Monday afternoon, J.J. has to get from Minnesota to NY what does that look like ? Does he just hop on a plane with a few belongings and ship his stuff to NY? Do teams trading a player usually give them a heads up it could happen and to maybe pack up their things ? Just curious about the logistics of him actually getting settled in NY. Ed says: Chase, per the Collective Bargaining Agreement, teams are required to pay travel and moving expenses when they acquire a player. Teams also generally provide players with short-term living arrangements until they are able to find their own places. Teams often help arrange travel plans for new players. Players find out about trades when they get traded. Teams don’t give players a heads up that they might get traded, although players can often figure that out on their own. Chris Milner asks: What’s your sense of the progress that the Giants are making in building a playoff and championship contender? Are they moving the needle, or are they just struggling to get by with all the injuries? Ed says: Chris, the answer is actually in your question. They are “building” a championship contender. They are not, and never were going to be, a championship contender this year. The injuries put them in survivial mode for this season. But, the culture that has been established, the quality young players they have added, and what John Harbaugh learns about what this team needs going forward are all part of the process. Jason Zalewski asks: Why do you think we’ve been so poor at drafting early round CBs? Feels like we’ve been in CB purgatory since our SB wins. The jury is still out on Tae Banks. Ed says: Jason, have the Giants been bad at drafting early-round cornerbacks? It is way too early to judge Colton Hood. Dru Phillips, a third-round pick, is a good player. Cor’Dale Flott played well last year. It really isn’t fair to go back beyond Joe Schoen’s tenure as GM. Schoen has one miss in Banks, and even that might still be salvaged. Fletcher Wyman asks: Cutting through all the JJ noise and looking at a specific position of need I’ll ask you directly what you think of the possibility of trading for Riley Moss, mimicking a feed post I made today. He’s a 26yo starter that will be a UFA in 2027. He is very good against the run and plays opposite of Surtain so he’s targeted at a very high rate. He’s considered grabby but is middle of the pack for penalties vs targets. Denver may be interested in gaining assets before he has the opportunity to test the market. Ed says: Fletcher, I won’t claim to have studied Moss. The Broncos are a Super Bowl contender, though. Why would they trade a starting player off their defense when they are in win-now mode? I am in favor of adding good players. What’s the cost, financially and in draft capital? You don’t trade for him without giving him a long-term contract? Does acquiring him get in the way of letting Colton Hood develop? I’m not sure I see this one as realistic. Roy Koeslag asks: I know with all of the injuries to key players at the Giants, the thoughts on how we can solve the season must be ongoing. Trading for QB McCarthy seems like a risk because we don’t have a lot of picks next year. Signing a veteran QB with a similar profile as Dart would have been a better option in my opinion. Do you think they will try to add a veteran CB to help out? That seems like a much more urgent hole in our team. Ed says: Roy, the Giants traded for McCarthy because they believed he has more upside than anyone they could have signed as a free agent or taken off a practice squad. I appreciate the aggression. Will it pay off? Nobody knows. As for cornerback, I think it’s a wait-and-see deal. Can Greg Newsome keep playing well? What will Tae Banks provide when he is is healthy again? How will Colton Hood develop? Will Paulson Adebo help when he returns? I think the Giants need to be very careful about giving away draft assets. The focus still has to be on the future. Giving away assets that compromise the future for short-term fixes that — maybe — help you win one or two more games this year doesn’t seem like a good plan. Stephen Goodyear asks: Understand and agree with the aversion to a Porter acquisition. But it seems we have CB issues. First, injury updates on Adebo and Banks please? Secondly, Newsome seems OK. Holland seem positioned improve by playing. Then what? If either Holland or Newsome gets injured. Jones? Washington? Ed says: Another cornerback question. Stephen, I think Banks might play this weekend. Adebo is on IR. He can’t return until at least Week 6. I don’t know if he will. Jevon Holland is a safety, so he shouldn’t be part of the conversation. In the short term, I think the Giants just have to ride with Colton Hood and let him develop. He is being forced to play more than anticipated due to injuries. In the long run, that might help him. Could the Giants trade for a cornerback? If they do, I would think they would be looking for a player who would be a multi-year acquisition. They might just have to get by the best they can, and then try to address it in the offseason. Brian Scott asks: In past years we’ve seen various members of the front office — Joe Schoen and Brandon…

title: NY Giants news: Malik Nabers, J.J. McCarthy, more
summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know about as the Giants look to stay atop the NFC East with a win this Sunday. NFL Week 4 preview | ESPN.com The Giants seem to know they’re not facing the Titans’ offense again this week. It was mentioned several times […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know about as the Giants look to stay atop the NFC East with a win this Sunday. NFL Week 4 preview | ESPN.com The Giants seem to know they’re not facing the Titans’ offense again this week. It was mentioned several times that the Cardinals are “very similar” offensively to the Rams — who dismantled the Giants two weeks ago — which DC Dennard Wilson noted because of Arizona coach Mike LaFleur’s ties to Sean McVay. New York knows it’s going to be a difficult challenge, particularly stopping rookie RB Jeremiyah Love, who it had ranked as a top-three player in the 2026 draft. Can Jameis Winston hold off JJ McCarthy? Where’s the pass rush? What to watch for in Giants-Cardinals | The Athletic A weak Arizona Cardinals pass defense should provide the streaky Winston an opportunity to find his groove. But if Winston struggles again and the Giants lose, the focus immediately will shift to his job security. A key variable will be how quickly McCarthy learns the offense. He only has 10 career starts and the Giants’ offense puts a lot on the quarterback’s plate. Rushing McCarthy into action before he’s ready would be a huge mistake. But there’s an understanding that McCarthy won’t be able to fully get up to speed on the offense midstream. With an upcoming stretch against the 1-2 Cardinals, the 1-2 Commanders, the 1-2 Saints and the 0-3 Texans, the Giants’ best bet to building momentum is Winston turning things around. If the 2-1 Giants can’t string some wins together now, it will be asking a lot for McCarthy to save the season when the schedule stiffens after their Week 8 bye. New Giants QB candid about if he can thrive amid fresh start: ‘Nobody knows’ | NJ.com McCarthy said he’s attacking the new offense day-by-day, but said he feels he’s picking it up pretty quickly. When asked how close he is to being ready to go into a game, McCarthy said, “At the end of the day, I’m just focused on watching this practice, learning from it and making sure I get this game plan down. I’m really just focused on being in the present moment and going from there.” McCarthy wasn’t interested in dwelling on what went wrong in Minnesota. “There’s a multitude of things you can think of, but at the end of the day, it’s all in the past,” he said. “All I care about is what’s important now — that next rep, that next meeting, that next game. That’s really all I’m focused on.” Giants rookie Colton Hood ‘baptized by fire’ by intense NFL initiation | New York Post Initiations into the NFL don’t get any more difficult than defending Matthew Stafford throwing to Davante Adams in your first career start. But Hood also allowed Wan’Dale Robinson’s touchdown last game. Hood has allowed 11 catches on 15 targets for 106 yards and two touchdowns over three games, according to NextGenStats. Opposing quarterbacks have a 132.2 rating when throwing at him. “I’m encouraged by, just watching the film, none of it is, ‘This guy is just better than me and beat me,’ ” Hood told The Post. “It’s more just seeing things for the first time and processing things post-snap. It’s just that I’m at a different level and learning how to combat those things. The routes in the league are different, you have to adjust to the depth. And the coverages, you have to understand not just your job but the people around you’s job so you can play tighter.” Rush to judgment as Giants defense promises to crank things up on QBs | The Record The New York Giants have looked in the mirror. They’ve studied the tape and scoured the stat sheet, only to be left incredibly disappointed with what they have seen. DC Dennard Wilson thinks Jihad Ward can be ‘good factor’ in Giants defense | SNY.tv Ward appeared in all 17 of Tennessee’s games (starting 12 of them) and he recorded career-highs in defensive snaps (708), quarterback hits (22), and sacks (5.0). “Haddy is a guy that played extremely well for me,” Wilson said. “He brings versatility to play on the edge, he brings versatility to play in the middle of the defense if we need, and he can be an interior rusher if we need, too. Haddy’s going to be ready when his number is called. We’ll see how it plays out from today going forward to Sunday and the weeks after that — but he’s an ultimate professional, and he’s going to be prepared. He’s been in camp with the Vikings, he’s in shape, so we’ll see how the chips fall here — I feel that Haddy could be a good factor in our defense moving forward.” Scouts: Giants Unlikely To Find Buried Treasure In McCarthy | FOX Sports “There’s no doubt McCarthy has talent,” one scout told me. “He’s probably a good fit for what they want to do, too. But honestly, if the Vikings were willing to dump their one-time franchise quarterback for a fifth-round pick, you really got to wonder what they know. Teams don’t usually dump young quarterbacks like that, especially ones they took 10th overall.” “Think about that,” one NFL assistant told me. “He couldn’t beat out Murray or Wentz. That doesn’t happen to a high first-round pick. That’s what happens with late-round and practice squad-type guys. So that tells you everything about what Minnesota thinks of him. Maybe a change of scenery will help. But O’Connell is pretty good with quarterbacks. If he couldn’t get anything out of the kid, I don’t know if anyone on the Giants can.” From Big Blue View Despite McCarthy-mania, Matt Nagy reminds that Jameis Winston is the Giants’ QB No Giants’ players with injury designations heading into game vs. Cardinals Malik Nabers still learning to trust his knee after surgery Giants vs. Cardinals: Arizona offense poses challenges for New York Giants vs. Cardinals: Arizona defense presents an opportunity It’s an underdog weekend for the NFC East Giants vs. Cardinals, NFL Week 4: News, injuries, analysis, more This week’s opponent Cardinals Defense Prepares For Jameis Winston Experience | AZCardinals.com Cardinals Deep Dive: 3 Problems Standing Between Them and 2-2 | SI.com Will the Arizona Cardinals take advantage of an ailing New York Giants? | Revenge of the Birds Rip The Band-Aid Off: Why Cardinals WR Marvin Harrison Jr. Needs A Career Reset | FOX Sports BBV mailbag Have a Giants-related question? title: Jets vs Bears Pre-Game Ball
summary: Plenty of people hand out game balls after the game. That’s easy. Watch the game, see who does well, give them the game ball. We’re doing something a little different. We’re handing out a pre-game ball. Before we watch the game, let’s settle on a player or players we think might be a decisive advantage […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 13: Dane Belton #6 of the New York Jets during the National Anthem prior to the game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Chris Carter/Getty Images) | Getty Images Plenty of people hand out game balls after the game. That’s easy. Watch the game, see who does well, give them the game ball. We’re doing something a little different. We’re handing out a pre-game ball. Before we watch the game, let’s settle on a player or players we think might be a decisive advantage for the Jets in the upcoming game. Occasionally we might hand out a pre-blame ball. If we think the Jets are going to get slaughtered, we’ll try to identify a prime culprit. One caveat: the quarterback is off limits. Nothing personal against quarterbacks, but they are obviously the most important players on the field. We could give out a pre-game or pre-blame ball to the quarterback virtually every week, but that would be boring, so we’re not going to do it. We’ll try to identify somebody besides the quarterback for the glory or the ignominy. This approach comes with the obvious drawback that predictions are difficult, especially about the future. We’re destined to get many of these wrong. No matter. We’ll have some laughs along the way. Let’s get to it. The Jets pre-game ball for the Jets game against the Chicago Bears goes to (drum roll please) – Minkah Fitzpatrick and Dane Belton. Our first shared pre-game ball! The Jets are a bit of a mess on offense going into this game. They are missing starting running back Breece Hall, starting guard Dylan Parham, four (!) receivers – Adonai Mitchell, Omar Cooper Jr, Arian Smith and Tim Patrick – and tight end Mason Taylor on offense. All of this makes the Jets’ offense carrying the day a bit unlikely. I don’t expect a Jets win if this game develops into a shootout. Consequently the team may need the defense to step up and control the game on their end. Fortunately for the Jets the Bears are missing some pieces as well, including starting quarterback Caleb Wiliams. The Bears are expected to start Tyson Bagent in Williams’ place. The inexperienced Bagent presents an opportunity for the Jets defense. He hasn’t seen meaningful NFL action since his rookie year of 2023, when Bagent started four games for the Bears. Bagent’s performance in 2023 was far from stellar. Bagent threw for just three touchdowns while chucking six interceptions, including back-to-back multiple interception games. While Bagent has presumably developed since then, the lack of NFL game experience should provide some opportunities to confuse the young quarterback. Bagent does not have a huge arm, and he will likely be looking to get the ball out quickly. Tight ends Cole Kmet and Colston Loveland will likely be a big part of the Bears game plan, and Jets safeties Fitzpatrick and Belton will need to step up and limit the Bears tight ends in the passing game. In addition, the Bears currently boast the NFL’s #1 running game. The Jets are unlikely to completely shut down the Bears running game, but they might be able to slow them down and limit chunk plays. As the last line of defense for the Jets, Fitzpatrick and Belton will be instrumental in this regard. If the Bears are able to run the ball at will and exploit the Jets secondary in the passing game this will be a long day for Jets fans. But let’s not dwell on that possibility. We’re Jets fans. Let’s envision Jets success. This week, that vision probably will require a big game out of the safeties. And dare I say it, an interception or two? Minkah Fitzpatrick and Dane Belton, come on down! Let’s see you plug the holes in the running game and limit the Bears’ short passing game. You get your opportunity on Sunday. Run with it. What about you? Who would you give the pre-game ball to? Let us know in the comments.

title: Do the Jets have an Isaiah Williams problem?
summary: Isaiah Williams was one of the bright spots for the New York Jets in a very dreary year in 2025. He was signed by the Jets in week 2, and played 15 games as the Jets’ primary punt returner and secondary kick returner. As a punt returner Williams was superb, returning 28 punts for a […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 20: Isaiah Williams #18 of the New York Jets is tackled by J. Michael Sturdivant #87 of the Green Bay Packers during the first quarter of the game at MetLife Stadium on September 20, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images Isaiah Williams was one of the bright spots for the New York Jets in a very dreary year in 2025. He was signed by the Jets in week 2, and played 15 games as the Jets’ primary punt returner and secondary kick returner. As a punt returner Williams was superb, returning 28 punts for a total of 396 yards, two touchdowns and a sparkling 14.1 yards per punt return. There wasn’t a lot to cheer for on the Jets in 2025, but Williams was definitely one. Williams is only 25 years old. It looked like the Jets might have found a great returner for the next several years. Then came this year. It started off fine. On opening day against the Tennessee Titans Williams returned two punts for 29 yards and 14.5 yards per return. It looked like he was picking up right where he left off in 2025. Then came the Jets second game of the season against the Green Bay Packers. The game was played in a steady rain, making the conditions less than ideal to catch the ball. On Williams’ first three punt returns he fumbled, returned a punt for two yards, then fumbled again and was called for an illegal fair catch signal penalty. All this happened in the first quarter of the game. It was a disastrous start to the game for Williams, though the Jets fortunately did not turn the ball over on either of the fumbles. What has happened since for Williams has been somewhat concerning. In the first five quarters of football played by the Jets in 2026, the Jets’ opponents punted 10 times and Williams returned five of them, including the two fumbles. That 50% return rate is right in line with his 2026 campaign, when Williams returned 28 of 57 punts. In the seven quarters of football the Jets have played since Williams’ fumbles, Jets opponents have punted five times. Williams has not returned any of them. This is a tiny sample, so we shouldn’t read too much into it. Nonetheless, to me he has looked a little gun-shy out there since the fumbles. That’s a subjective opinion. Maybe others see things differently. But there are other aspects of Williams’ performance thus far that raise questions. In 2025 Williams ranked 6th among punt returners with 16+ returns with 14.1 yards per return. In 2026 he ranks 20th among punt returners with 3+ returns with a miniscule 6.2 yards per return. In 2025 Williams was 13th in the NFL with 13 fair catches. In 2026 he ranks 1st in the NFL with two. In 2025 Williams ranked 5th in the NFL in returns with 28. In 2026 he ranks 12th with five. In 2025 Williams had zero return fumbles. In 2026 he is the only returner in the NFL with multiple fumbles. In 2025 Williams returned 48+% of opponents’ punts. In 2026 he has returned 33+%, and 0% after his two fumbles. Again, the 2026 numbers represent a tiny sample, too small to draw any definitive conclusions. Nonetheless the numbers should raise at least a modicum of concern. Do the Jets have an Isaiah Williams problem? It’s too soon to tell, but probably not too soon for this to be on the Jets’ radar. If Williams doesn’t pick up his performance as a returner soon, the Jets have another option. His name is Jamaal Pritchett, and perhaps it’s not entirely a coincidence the Jets signed him off the practice squad last week. If Williams doesn’t come out of his early season funk relatively soon, we may see Pritchett get a shot in the punt returner role.

title: Three things I’m looking for in the Jets vs. Bears game
summary: It’s time for some New York Jets football! I’m praying that we’re all still getting amped for games in December because the last two years have been torturous. The fanbase is sharply divided between those who are excited/impressed by the “progress” of losing by one score and those who aren’t happy about losing at all. […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - DECEMBER 14: Isaiah Davis #32 of the New York Jets runs the ball against the Jacksonville Jaguars during the fourth quarter at EverBank Stadium on December 14, 2025 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Rich Storry/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s time for some New York Jets football! I’m praying that we’re all still getting amped for games in December because the last two years have been torturous . The fanbase is sharply divided between those who are excited/impressed by the “progress” of losing by one score and those who aren’t happy about losing at all. I’ll let you guess which one of those I am. Regardless of which way you feel, what should be clear to all of us is that the Aaron Glenn Jets need to dramatically(!) improve their 2-minute drill and late-game efficiency. Did you know that the last time the Jets have scored any points to end a half was the game-winner in Week 13 of last year against Atlanta!? In the 16 halves of football AG has coached since then, his Jets have had the ball in the last two minutes of 14 of them and have scored zero times. Zero. That is a streak I’d love to see end this weekend, and there’s another one I’m hoping to see end (more on that later) en route to a New York Jets win. I promise you, we won’t remember anything but the wins. Losing by three to the Bears (or any team) is not an accomplishment, so let’s try to win! I’ll have my eyes on these things: Running Men Speaking of winning, Breece Hall has scored a touchdown on 14 of the Jets’ last 15 wins. We are 28 days away from the two-year anniversary of the last time the Jets won without him scoring a touchdown. It was Halloween vs. the Texans, and he still put up 86 yards on 17 touches while Davante Adams and Garrett Wilson found the end zone. In this game, Breece is out, so does that automatically doom our chances of success? The short answer is no. While they’re certainly lower without Breece, we have seen a game where Braelon had 81 yards on 15 touches, and Isaiah Davis had 67 yards and a touchdown on 13 touches in the same game. Aaron Rodgers added 339 yards of his own and 1 passing touchdown en route to an OT loss against the Dolphins in Week 7 of 2024. Competitive loss, though! I can’t lie, Braelon Allen has only had 60+ total yards in one other game besides that Dolphins one, despite playing in 23 others. Isaiah Davis has had 60+ total yards in three other games, including 109 yards (65 rushing, 44 receiving) against the Bengals in last year’s 39-38 win. Davis also has the distinction of having the highest yards per carry in the room (5.6). Of course, Davis has only 73 career carries compared to 129 for Allen and 806 for Hall, but there were several full games where they called his number, and he delivered. I won’t be anywhere close to the field, but if I were in charge of calling numbers on Sunday, I wouldn’t hesitate to make Davis my top option in the run game. In my opinion, he is a more complete back who has great burst, steady hands, and underrated vision and football IQ. He makes plays that impact games but don’t show up on the stat sheet, like this one . It makes absolutely no sense that he hasn’t played an offensive snap yet, but that better change this Sunday. Chicago is allowing the second-most rushing yards per carry in the NFL so far (5.1), which is great news because the Jets have been averaging the third-worst rushing yards per carry at 3.3. With the Jets’ offensive line struggling and down a starter, the craftier, wiser running back should get the first cracks at setting the table for the offense. Of course, Braelon could make me eat my words, and I’d love to see him have a great game, but with this fanbase starved for a win, I think Davis is the best bet to make that happen and replicate Breece’s impact on the game. Meatball Subs Anyone? Fun fact: As Jets fans, we are the only fanbase in the NFL to not witness an interception during our team’s games so far this season. Not so fun fact: half of the reason for the first fact is because the Jets are one of four teams without an interception forced this season. Please don’t get it twisted though, the Jets have no peers in this area. Before Aaron Glenn became a head coach, over 100 seasons of NFL football were played and no team ever went a full season without catching an interception. 12 game seasons, 14 game seasons, 16 game seasons, there was always at least one. Aaron Glenn’s Jets had 17 games and couldn’t muster an interception. With zero heading into Game 4, the Jets’ unprecedented run of infamy has extended to 20 consecutive games. Is there an end in sight? The Bears have former Aaron Glenn colleague Ben Johnson running the show in Chicago and you may be surprised to hear it didn’t take him multiple seasons to take his terrible team to a playoff win. You could choose to say “he had a quarterback!” but then I’d be curious to hear your response to seeing 38-year-old Case Keenum carve up a talented Eagles defense for 247 yards, 2 touchdowns, and 0 interceptions on 70.6% completion. The Eagles hadn’t allowed a 200-yard passer leading up to that point and for you bettors out there Keenum’s passing yards line was at 170.5. He specifically thrived against the blitz, diagnosing plays pre-snap and getting ball out at an average 2.41 seconds per throw (2nd fastest in the NFL in Week 3). For Glenn and his love of exotic blitzes, will those disguised looks be enough to trick Keenum? Or will those quick looks be too much to overcome? Luckily for Keenum, the responsibility isn’t solely his. The Bears are the only team in the NFL rushing for more than 175 yards per game, a whopping 184.3 yards on 35 attempts (5.3 yards per attempt). Both the Bears and the Jets emphasize the run game, the Jets’ 28.3 attempts per game are 10th in the league, but we already mentioned how they have the second-worst yards per carry. The Bears have been the platinum standard of rushing the football, and if they continue to have their way, this entire section becomes obsolete. Step A is stopping the run, which the Jets were able to do nicely against Tony Pollard and the filth of the Packers’ running back room, but Jahmyr Gibbs was a different story. 99 yards on the ground, 65 more through the air, and Jared Goff had the easiest time dicing up the defense. Swift’s 84 yards against the Eagles were crucial in giving Case the openings he needed to dice up their defense. If the Jets have any hope of ending this interception streak at 20, it starts with making D’Andre Swift look like D’Andre Slow. Double Duty? Or Double Trouble I was watching the Jake Asman show on YouTube and I saw in the live comments the legendary Connie Carberg raise the point of Isaiah Williams playing wide receiver much more often this year than last year. She hypothesized that since he’s so much more involved in the offensive gameplan, he is not as fresh or readily available to be the superstar kick returner that he was last year en route to being voted Team MVP. Clearly, Isaiah hasn’t been the same so far in the return game. In the Packers game specifically, his hands were a massive liability, which I thought was a weather issue but Skyy Moore of the Packers played in the same weather conditions and didn’t drop the ball once. Last year he was third in punt return yardage, scored 2 touchdowns, and only called 12 fair catches in 15 games. Needless to say, he hasn’t come close to these ranks this year but in three games played he already has 30% of the catches and 32% of the yards he had last year. According to footballguys.com, Williams’ usage as a WR has only increased, going from 60% in Week 1 to 82% in Week 2 and 89% in Week 3! As far as skill position players go, only Geno Smith and Garrett Wilson have played more snaps. Compared to the aforementioned Skyy Moore, he was only out for 6% of snaps Week 1, 36% in Week 2, and 52% in Week 3. There are more than five Packers skill position players with more snaps than Moore. Last year,…

title: Shocking numbers expose Aaron Glenn’s Biggest Flaw
summary: Before you come for my neck, this isn’t intended to bash Aaron Glenn – it’s intended to highlight a clear, much-needed area of improvement. You may have heard people criticize his timeout management, the inefficiencies of his 2-minute drills, but have you been able to quantify these late-half gaffes against other teams? I did some […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 20: Head Coach Aaron Glenn of the New York Jets reacts during the fourth quarter of the game against the Green Bay Packers at MetLife Stadium on September 20, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images Before you come for my neck, this isn’t intended to bash Aaron Glenn – it’s intended to highlight a clear, much-needed area of improvement. You may have heard people criticize his timeout management, the inefficiencies of his 2-minute drills, but have you been able to quantify these late-half gaffes against other teams? I did some digging and looked at the end of every single half the Jets have played under Aaron Glenn so far. I specifically looked at all the halves where the Jets had the ball for more than one play with less than 2 minutes left. There were 35, but I disqualified two because they were second halves where they were in victory formation instead of driving down the field. That left 33 halves to review, and the results were astonishing. First of all, the New York Jets are scoreless in their last 14(!) attempts with two minutes or less. In the six halves played this year, they’ve had the ball five times, scored zero times, and fumbled once. I could’ve added a 34th entry, the OT game, but left it to strictly when the clock read 2:00 or less. By comparison, Saleh’s Titans scored a field goal in the last two minutes of each half against the Eagles this year. The Bills, obviously a very good team, have only had the ball in the last two minutes of three halves this year. They scored a touchdown all three times for a 100% score rate and a healthy average of seven points per 2-minute drill. Buckle up for this next paragraph: In the 33 halves in which Aaron Glenn’s Jets have had the ball with two minutes left, they have scored only six times . They average less than 1 point per attempt, which makes sense since they’re currently on a streak of 14 consecutive scoreless attempts. They have lost the ball via interception or fumble just as frequently as they’ve scored (6). If we just limit it to this year, the Jets are 0-5. No scores, one fumble. 0% score rate, 0 points per attempt. Let’s compare those horrific 2-minute drill numbers to some winless teams this year: We’ve already established the Titans have scored multiple times. The Dolphins have scored two field goals and a touchdown for a respectable 3/5 score rate (60%) and 2.6 points per attempt. The Buccaneers have been horrible this year (but still better at this than the Jets), with a 1/4 (25%) score rate and 0.75 points per attempt. The Chargers have been even worse, allowing a safety on one attempt, but still have a 1/4 score rate and 0.25 points per attempt. I hope I’ve numerically illustrated just how awful Aaron Glenn has been at ending halves this year and throughout his entire run as Jets head coach. If I had more time to scan through every team’s schedule and play-by-play records, I’m sure this 20-game run would rank among the absolute worst in NFL history but I was only limited to the data presented in this article so you’ll just have to take my word for it. The point is, even the worst teams in the NFL score points to end halves. Even the worst teams in the NFL catch interceptions. The Jets are the only team in this article that does neither. This roster is certainly better than last year, but that was a requirement, not a wish. When will we see our favorite team get involved in some of the most fundamental and routine concepts of football? Can they end this streak this Sunday? Let’s go Jets!

title: Previewing the Jets’ opposition: Chicago Bears
summary: The New York Jets face their third NFC North opponent in a row on Sunday, as they are in the Windy City to face the 2-1 Chicago Bears. New York beat Chicago 31-10 in the last meeting between these teams back in 2022. Prior to that the Jets had last beaten the Bears all the […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 27: Darrynton Evans #21 of the Chicago Bears gets tackled by a pair of New York Jets players in the first half at MetLife Stadium on November 27, 2022 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Mike Stobe/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New York Jets face their third NFC North opponent in a row on Sunday, as they are in the Windy City to face the 2-1 Chicago Bears. New York beat Chicago 31-10 in the last meeting between these teams back in 2022. Prior to that the Jets had last beaten the Bears all the way back in 2000. Let’s break down the Bears’ roster going position by position: Quarterbacks The situation at quarterback is cloudy for the Bears, who may be about to start their third different quarterback in three weeks. After an inconsistent rookie year, Caleb Williams led the Bears to an 11-6 record last season, and was showing signs of this being his breakout into superstardom when the Bears racked up 59 points in their opener. However, he got injured in week two and the Bears were without him last Sunday, and will be this Sunday as well. Tyson Bagent had been considered the number two, but he missed practice during the week leading up to last weekend’s game, so the Bears prepared for Case Keenum to lead them against Philadelphia on Monday Night Football. Surprisingly, he put together a terrific performance to lead them to an easy win with 247 yards and two touchdowns. Ordinarily, you’d expect them to stick with Keenum after a performance like that. However, head coach Ben Johnson has kept his plans under wraps and Chicago beat writers have suggested it may be Bagent who gets the nod this week. Keenum is obviously more experienced than Bagent, who went 2-2 as a rookie starter in 2023 but has only thrown 15 passes since. Neither offers the same run threat as Williams. Offensive Line The Bears had a solid offensive line last season, with no offensive lineman giving up more than three sacks. Three of the five starters are returning, too, as right guard Jonah Jackson, pro bowl left guard Joe Thuney and right tackle Darnell Wright are back after each starting every game last year. They’ve kept the unit strong, as no offensive lineman was credited with giving up any of the six sacks that have been surrendered so far this season. The center position underwent a change due to Drew Dalman’s sudden retirement but veteran Garrett Bradbury has taken over that role, although he has four penalties in three games. At left tackle, Braxton Jones remains the number one choice, but he continues to be injury prone after missing considerable time in 2023 and 2025. He’s been ruled out again on Sunday but both Theo Benedet and Ozzy Trapilo started several games in his place last season and they remain on the roster. Benedet filled in for Jones for part of each of the first three games so he figures to start. The rest of the bench is low on experience as Logan Jones is a rookie second rounder and Luke Newman and Jordan McFadden have started two NFL games between them. Wright led the Bears with 12 offensive penalties last season. Running Backs The Bears currently have the number one running game in the NFL, although Williams being out affects that. D’Andre Swift is seventh in the NFL in rushing yards while Kyle Monangai is averaging 5.9 yards per carry. They each rushed for 100 yards in the first game, with Monangai doing that in just 10 carries as most of his yardage came on a 61-yard touchdown scamper. Roschon Johnson remains with the team as a backup although his workload has been reducing over the past few years. Pass catchers At wide receiver, the Bears were banking on recent draft picks Rome Odunze and Luther Burden to step up with DJ Moore having been traded after the pair had combined to catch 91 passes last year. However, early on, it’s been ex-Jets receiver Kalif Raymond who has elevated his game. Johnson was familiar with Raymond from his time in Detroit and brought him over this offseason. So far, Raymond’s role has been bigger than expected as he’s caught 19 passes on 21 targets for a team-high 214 receiving yards. Burden is also off to a good start as he has 15 receptions already this year. Odunze, on the other hand, only has eight catches, although he is averaging 17.4 yards per catch. In terms of backups, third round rookie Zavion Thomas and Jahdae Walker each have just one catch for one yard, although Walker’s was for a touchdown. The Bears have also had good production from their tight ends in recent years with Colston Loveland leading the team with over 700 receiving yards last season and Cole Kmet having posted similar numbers in the past. Both are off to a slow start this year, though. The third tight end is rookie Sam Roush, who played for Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich at Stanford. Defensive Line The Bears have more or less returned most of the edge rotation from last year, but their interior line rotation is completely different other than the returning former pro bowler Grady Jarrett. The starter alongside Jarrett is Kentavius Street with Neville Gallimore and third round rookie Jordan van den Berg also getting playing time. The main playmaker on the edge is Montez Sweat, who had 10 sacks last year. The other starter across from him is Dayo Odeyingbo, who already has two sacks after having had just one all year in 2025. The main reserve on the edge is Austin Booker, who had 4.5 sacks last year, with James Lynch also in the rotation. Edge Jamree Kromah and defensive tackle Jayden Loving are also on the roster for depth. Linebackers 2025’s leading tacker Tremaine Edmunds is now with the Giants, so the Bears brought in Devin Bush Jr. to start along with TJ Edwards, who had 67 tackles and five passes defensed in just 10 games last season. D’Marco Jackson also sees playing time when three linebackers are on the field, but Noah Sewell, who was in the rotation last year, is on the PUP list. Fifth round rookie Keyshaun Elliott and special teamer Jack Sanborn round out this unit. Defensive Backs The Bears’ secondary was the key to their winning record last year as they racked up an incredible 23 interceptions. Even more incredible, though, was their decision to get rid of literally everyone who had more than one. Pro bowlers Nahshon Wright and Kevin Byard are gone, along with C.J. Gardner-Johnson. To make matters worse, Kyler Gordon is still on the PUP list and safety Coby Bryant is on injured reserve. It’s perhaps not surprising that they gave up 37 points in their first game of the season with all these changes, but they’ve regrouped well to allow just 16 points in the last two games. At the safety position, they addressed the need by drafting the athletic Dillon Thieneman in the first round and he’s responded by leading them in tackles through three games. According to Chicago’s unofficial depth chart, Xavier Woods is listed as the other starting safety. However, Cam Lewis – listed as the starting nickel – has been playing safety instead of him so far this year. Lewis is listed as doubtful for Sunday, so Woods is likely to make his first start of the year with Elijah Hicks as the third safety and Skyler Thomas available as cover. At cornerback, Jaylon Johnson is hoping to get back to the level that saw him voted to the pro bowl in 2023 and 2024 before he missed half of last year due to injury. The other starter is Tyrique Stevenson, who broke up 10 passes last year. Fourth round rookie Malik Muhammad has been the primary slot cornerback so far. Josh Blackwell and Clark Phillips III are each available for depth. Special Teams Literally a quarter of the NFL has a former Jet as their placekicker right now, and the Bears are one of those teams as Cairo Santos has made his home there. Santos’ only miss of the year so far was a blocked chip shot field goal in the Vikings game where there was an issue with the snap count. Punter Tory Taylor is off to a good start, posting career-best numbers so far with a gross…

title: Eagles Film Preview: Scheme will have to help this team beat the Rams
summary: Each week, I’ll publish two film-room previews: one focusing on the offense and one on the defense. These are primarily film-based, focusing on the schemes, tendencies, and matchups that could shape Sunday’s game, with all statistics coming from the Fantasy Points Data Suite. I also record a video version for Patreon, where I break down […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - AUGUST 04: Philadelphia Eagles offensive coordinator Sean Mannion looks on during the Philadelphia Eagles training camp on August 4th, 2026 at Jefferson Health Training Center in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Each week, I’ll publish two film-room previews: one focusing on the offense and one on the defense. These are primarily film-based, focusing on the schemes, tendencies, and matchups that could shape Sunday’s game, with all statistics coming from the Fantasy Points Data Suite . I also record a video version for Patreon , where I break down the plays in greater detail and where you can further support my work. The Rams have been a very good pass defense through three weeks, but injuries in the secondary could give the Eagles opportunities this Sunday. Of course, the Eagles have their own injury problems, particularly at receiver, so this matchup is difficult to pin down. I like parts of the Rams’ defense a lot. I also think the Eagles have to find ways to attack it, because I have no interest in watching this offense spend another afternoon hoping the defense will win the game for them. It won’t happen this week! Pass Defense Chris Shula’s defense gives you a lot to prepare for. The Rams rank first in EPA allowed per dropback, and the film shows a secondary that can handle several different coverage structures. They play zone on roughly two-thirds of passing snaps, but their Cover 1, Cover 3, and Cover 4 usage is almost evenly split. You cannot build a game plan around expecting the same coverage every time. They can match routes in zone, pass receivers between defenders, and then line up in man coverage when they want to. That flexibility makes them a difficult opponent for an offense still trying to establish any kind of rhythm. Byron Young has been their best pass rusher. His explosive first step stands out immediately, and he keeps working when the initial rush does not get him to the quarterback. He leads the group with 14 pressures. They have a few individual rushers that can win quickly, and the coverage can make the quarterback hold the ball long enough for those wins to matter. Rams' Defense All22 Thread. 1) They have been a very strong pass defense this year. They play a ton of different coverages, so they aren't easy to predict, and they have a few really good pass rushers. Byron Young has been their best pass rusher. He has an explosive first step… pic.twitter.com/zeIXU1LwDI — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 2, 2026 Trent McDuffie is the player I would be most reluctant to build the passing game around attacking. His hip fluidity is outstanding, letting him stay connected when receivers change direction, and he plays the ball extremely well. He has allowed only eight catches for 59 yards on 18 targets, which is obviously very good! The clip below also shows the communication that makes this secondary impressive when everyone is on the same page. Defenders understand where the help is and how their responsibilities fit together. That is a big part of why throwing against them has been so difficult. However, as we’ll see, that might not be the case this week! 2) They have a couple of injuries in the secondary, but still have a very talented group. Trent McDuffie has been lights-out this year. He has outstanding hip fluidity, as you can see here, good man-coverage skills, and is excellent when the ball is in the air. They do a good job… pic.twitter.com/QU95riDe7w — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 2, 2026 The front can also win by rushing four. Braden Fiske provides an interior threat, alongside Kobie Turner and Aaron Donald, while Young gives them speed off the edge. The Rams blitz on only 22.9% of dropbacks, but they can show a crowded front before dropping defenders into coverage. The offensive line still has to identify the rush correctly and pass off movement after the snap. After the protection problems against the Bears, that worries me quite a bit. If I were the Rams DC, I’d test the hell out of the Eagles in pass protection this week. 3) They can win by rushing 4. Outside of Young, they have Fiske (who wins here) on the interior, as well as Kobie Turner and Aaron Donald. The Eagles' offensive line will have to play well, because it's a good pass-rushing group. pic.twitter.com/FS5khhqDqa — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 2, 2026 Donald has played a limited workload since returning, but he still looks very good in those snaps. The speed of his spin move is ridiculous. Myles Garrett is unavailable on injured reserve, which helps, but there is still plenty of talent here. Donald also missed Wednesday and Thursday practices with back soreness, so his availability and workload remain uncertain. I would expect him to play. I would absolutely treat him as someone capable of wrecking a possession. I imagine he will keep getting better throughout the season. 8) Oh yeah, Aaron Donald hasn't played a ton, but he still looks very good in limited time. I don't think it will be long before he dominates. Just check the speed of the spin… pic.twitter.com/RBooWTroFn — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 2, 2026 What I like most about the healthy version of this defense is how well it is coached. There are examples of good zone-match coverage, where defenders react to the routes rather than simply stand in an area, as well as tight man coverage. The Eagles need route combinations that force those defenders to communicate and decide quickly. Motion that changes the strength of the formation, condensed alignments, and crossers at different depths can all make life difficult for the Rams’ secondary. The 49ers showed how an underneath screen threat could draw defenders forward and create space behind them. The Eagles will likely try this, but the screen game has been a disaster through three weeks. The 49ers film does showcase a useful example of making different parts of the passing game work together. 4) It just feels like a well-coached defense and a well-coached secondary. They can play a variety of coverages. They play zone match well but can line up and play man if needed, too. pic.twitter.com/mL0GIILeSe — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 2, 2026 The injuries make this matchup interesting. Jaylen Watson is expected to miss the game after dislocating his shoulder. Kamren Kinchens has missed the previous two games with a hamstring injury, while Josh Wallace is dealing with a shoulder injury himself. When Kinchens has been absent, Quentin Lake has moved from the slot to safety alongside Kamren Curl, with Wallace filling in inside. After Watson was injured against the Broncos, Wallace also played outside, moving into the slot in nickel while Emmanuel Forbes entered outside. That is a lot of juggling, which makes communication tough. They might play more man coverage because of this. Wallace is a reserve being asked to handle multiple jobs, and the communication was less reliable at times against the Broncos. There were plays where the coverage broke down, including a huge late gain on second-and-20. I would want the Eagles to test those connections between defenders early. Changing the formation with motion and sending receivers across the field can force replacements to confirm who is carrying each route. Curl and Lake are good players, but they still depend on the defenders around them executing the same coverage correctly. 5) Josh Wallace has been forced into the lineup after some injuries, and the communication wasn't as good against the Broncos at times. They have a few injuries, and this is what happens! The Eagles need to be aggressive and test the communication, especially if Jaylen Watson,… pic.twitter.com/YwAkMspvNe — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 2, 2026 If Watson is out, I would target the outside corner opposite McDuffie. Wallace struggled with some of those matchups against the Broncos, and the Eagles have successfully attacked…

summary: The Eagles have to rebound from their tough Monday night loss. The good news is they’re at home, the bad news is it’s the Rams, and the worse news is that they are now down some key players on both sides of the ball due to injuries. This will be a tough win if it […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Makai Lemon #9 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on prior to the game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles have to rebound from their tough Monday night loss. The good news is they’re at home, the bad news is it’s the Rams, and the worse news is that they are now down some key players on both sides of the ball due to injuries. This will be a tough win if it is a win at all, and there’s one big way an Eagles rookie can help the team get there. OK, Makai Lemon, let’s see what you’ve got. DeVonta Smith is out. Hollywood Brown is out. Not only does this put unique pressure on Makai Lemon to step up, but also (hopefully) means the Eagles need to use him more like a real receiver. Dontayvion Wicks is having a strong season and will be the Eagles’ top target. I expect Lemon to line up everywhere like he normally has done, but to receive far more looks. With three weeks under his belt, Lemon should be up to speed on the playbook. The question is: how does he fare with defenses not worrying about smith? Can he create separation as a route runner and/or make tough catches against tight coverage? The Eagles offense really needs Sean Mannion to trust him to do more, and for Lemon to show he can do more. Other Storylines With Fred Johnson out, Markel Bell is the Eagles’ swing tackle. If the Eagles want to go really heavy in this game to offset their lack of wide receivers, maybe we see Bell on the field. Eli Stowers is eligible to return from injured reserve after this game. Let’s hope he is ready to contribute at some level since Dallas Goedert is still injured and the rest of the tight ends are providing very little.

title: Eagles roster news: 2 moves announced ahead of Rams game
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced two roster moves ahead of the team’s Week 4 game against the Los Angeles Rams. Here’s an overview: Note: teams are permitted to temporarily elevate up to two practice squad players per game. A player can be elevated up to three times in the regular season and an unlimited number […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Zach Ertz of the Philadelphia Eagles reacts prior to an NFL football game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced two roster moves ahead of the team’s Week 4 game against the Los Angeles Rams. Here’s an overview: TE Zach Ertz and TE Josiah Deguara were temporarily elevated from the practice squad. Note: teams are permitted to temporarily elevate up to two practice squad players per game . A player can be elevated up to three times in the regular season and an unlimited number of times in the postseason. Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. ZACH ERTZ To no surprise, the Eagles are elevating Ertz for the second week in a row. Against the Chicago Bears, Ertz played the second-most tight end snaps for the Eagles with 19. That was seven fewer than Johnny Mundt and six more than E.J. Jenkins. We’ll see if it’s a similar distribution in Week 4 or if the Eagles ramp up Ertz’s workload as Dallas Goedert continues to miss time. Ertz’s sole target in Week 3 produced a nine-yard reception. Ertz has one practice squad elevation remaining. After next week, the Eagles will need to put him on the roster in order for him to play in games. JOSIAH DEGUARA Interesting and unexpected to see the Eagles elevate Deguara in addition to Ertz. This means the Eagles will have four tight ends active against the Rams. With DeVonta Smith out, it seems like the Birds might try to lean into more 12 and 13 personnel packages. As a reminder, Deguara joined the Eagles’ practice squad back in mid-September. Here’s what we wrote at the time : The 29-year-old Deguara was originally a third-round pick (No. 94 overall) by the Green Bay Packers in the 2020 NFL Draft. He notably overlapped with current Eagles tight ends coach and run game coordinator Ryan Mahaffey on the Packers from 2021-2023. Making 12 starts in 77 regular season games, Deguara has logged 66 career targets for 53 receptions, 471 receiving yards, and three touchdowns. His most recent NFL stop prior to this was a three-day stint on the New York Giants’ roster back in late August. NON-MOVES The Eagles did not place DeVonta Smith nor any of the five other players ruled out for this game on injured reserve. Good to see the team is not concerned about them missing at least four weeks. Though there’s the case to made they should be slow-playing Smith’s hamstring injury timeline. Thought the Eagles might look to temporarily elevate Cole Wisniewski to the roster in order to have more depth at safety. With Marcus Epps ruled out, they have just one full-time safety on the roster: Andrew Mukuba. Michael Carter II has been learning safety after previously playing nickel corner and he’ll likely play in Epps’ place in the Eagles’ nickel defense with Cooper DeJean as the guy next to Makuba in base packages. The Eagles did sign Kenny Moore II to the roster and they’re seemingly having him learn to play safety. Thought the Eagles might look to temporarily elevate newcomer Anfernee Orji. With Zack Baun out, the Eagles are entering Week 4 with just three healthy off-ball linebackers: Jihaad Campbell (who spent some time on the injury report this week), Jeremiah Trotter Jr., and Smael Mondon. RAMS MOVES The Rams temporarily elevated two practice squad players: cornerback Cam Lampkin and edge rusher Darryl Peterson III. The latter move doesn’t seem like a good sign for Josaiah Stewart’s chances of playing. Stewart, who has been starting in place of an injured Myles Garrett, was added to Friday’s injury report and ruled questionable to play.

title: Eagles News: Too early to write off Jihaad Campbell
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! In case you missed it, Joe Santoliquito shared the following tidbit on BGN yesterday: According to a couple of Bears’ sources who were on the field against Campbell on Monday, they felt Campbell was a great athlete with a great future […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - AUGUST 07: Philadelphia Eagles linebacker Jihaad Campbell #11 looks on during the Philadelphia Eagles training camp on August 7th, 2026 at the Jefferson Health Training Complex on August 7th, 2026 in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! In case you missed it, Joe Santoliquito shared the following tidbit on BGN yesterday: According to a couple of Bears’ sources who were on the field against Campbell on Monday, they felt Campbell was a great athlete with a great future ahead of him though was also someone right now who “doesn’t know what he’s doing.” I think this assessment sums it up well. Campbell has exciting potential. But he’s yet to fully deliver on that promise because he’s still figuring out the mental part of the game. This isn’t to guarantee he’ll definitely get to that point. But it’s too early to rule it out. Jeremiah Trotter Jr. might be a better linebacker right now. But the Eagles investing in Campbell’s development could pay off in the long term, including later this season. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Roob’s 10 Observations: Why we all need to be patient with Jihaad Campbell- NBCSP DON’T GIVE UP ON JIHAAD CAMPBELL: I get that people are down on Jihaad Campbell right now, and some of the criticism is fair. He hasn’t been great and is not playing like a 1st-round pick, Nakobe Dean is having an all-pro season with the Raiders and it’s impossible not to compare the two since their careers will always be inexorably linked. Drafting Campbell in the first round is why the Eagles couldn’t keep Dean. But a couple things to remember: Campbell is 22 and the 3rd-youngest starting inside linebacker in the NFL. He was considered a steal where the Eagles drafted him last year at No. 31. And he hasn’t been awful. Out of 61 linebackers who’ve played at least 100 snaps, he ranks 23rd in Pro Football Focus with his overall grade, 26th in run defense and 25th in coverage, so a bit above middle of the pack in every category. He hasn’t covered as well as you’d expect, but it’s way too early to even think about calling him a 1st-round bust. He’s a young guy with great size and athleticism, and there’s no reason to think he won’t get better working under ace linebackers coach Bobby King. Remember, when the Eagles drafted Campbell there were significant questions about Dean as he rehabbed a severe knee injury. And he really didn’t blossom as a player until last year, after Campbell was already here. Campbell is the youngest Eagles starting linebacker ever, and he’s the 2nd-youngest defensive player in franchise history to start double-digit games, just a bit older than 1950s defensive tackle Ernie Calloway. Good ol’ Ernie. Maybe Campbell won’t work out. Maybe he won’t pan out as a top-tier linebacker. Maybe a rare Howie miss. Maybe Jeremiah Trotter will play so well against the Rams Sunday Vic Fangio will be tempted to make a switch once Zack Baun is back. But it’s too early to give up hope. Let’s see where Campbell is at the end of this year and even into next year before we write him off. I still think he has a chance to be a player. Eagles-Rams Final Injury Report: DeVonta Smith and Zack Baun among 6 players ruled OUT – BGN Smith is dealing with a hamstring injury that prevented him from practicing this week. Reports indicate he could miss another game or two after this weekend . Not great for the Eagles to be missing their top receiver at all, let alone against some tough opponents. With Smith and Brown out, the Eagles will be down to the following five receivers: Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon, Elijah Moore, Darius Cooper, and Britain Covey. Wicks figures to be the Eagles’ No. 1 target in Smith’s absence. Lemon could also see increased opportunities … just hopefully not in the entirely predictable screen reception variety. Moore played more snaps than Cooper last week despite being a healthy scratch in either of the first two games. The Eagles might trust Moore to play more on offense, even though Cooper has shown potential there. Cooper could still get some more chances than usual while also playing on special teams. Covey is the Eagles’ punt returner. This should be a big week for the Rams defense – Turf Show Times Run defense, however, has been a different story for Los Angeles. While its rushing success rate currently sits 13th in the league, it ranks 26th in rush EPA/play. That tells you that L.A. is allowing too many big gains while being decent on a down-to-down basis. Thankfully for the Rams, this matchup should, in theory, allow them to dedicate more resources to stopping the run while still limiting the passing game. With such a banged up corps of pass catchers, it is likely going to be even more challenging to move the ball through the air for a team that is already struggling to do that (the Eagles are 25th in dropback EPA/play through three weeks). Now, the Eagles have been decent at generating explosive pass plays, but the Rams have trusted their cornerbacks on islands this year, playing man coverage on 29.5% of snaps, the ninth-highest rate in the NFL per Next Gen Stats. Even without Jaylen Watson this week, Los Angeles can probably afford to keep trusting those cornerbacks. It’s important to mention trench play here as well, which is admittedly more concerning with Aaron Donald now out for the matchup. He would have been especially valuable against the Eagles’ offensive line, which has been solid in pass protection this year overall but exceptionally poor at the guard spots in particular. Home Dogs: Can Eagles, Nick Sirianni Spring The Upset & Stay Undefeated Vs. Rams, Sean McVay? – PHLY Sports The Eagles are likely to be without DeVonta Smith and potentially Zack Baun against a high-powered Rams lineup that is expected to get Puka Nacua back. But Nick Sirianni has bested Sean McVay in all four meetings between the two teams. Can he, Sean Mannion and Vic Fangio cook up a special gameplan? The professor Deniz Selman and Brandon Lee Gowton join Bo Wulf, with insight from EJ Smith at the Eagles’ complex to discuss it all. Game Preview – LAR at PHI – Iggles Blitz Both teams have injuries so neither can really use that as an excuse. We’ll see which team has better depth and which coaching staff does the better job in a tough situation. I’m hoping last week’s bad loss will prove to be the wake-up call the Eagles needed. I think you can argue they were out-played in each of the first three games. They were talented enough to win two of them, but the sloppiness caught up wit them in Chicago. Nick Sirianni is usually good at pushing the right buttons to get the most out of his team. That hasn’t been the case this season. Getting embarrassed by the Bears should change things. If that didn’t get the players attention, nothing will. The biggest thing I’ll be watching for in this game is the Eagles level of play. They could lose a tough, competitive game and I’d be okay with that. I’m focused on how they play more than the result. The Eagles have not looked like the team we expected so far. The defense isn’t making plays. The offense is struggling to play with any consistency. That has to change for this team to get where they want to go. Philadelphia Eagles’ defense at an inflection point – ESPN Two of the defense’s top communicators in linebacker Nakobe Dean and safety Reed Blankenship are now in Las Vegas and Houston, respectively. Former first-round pick Jihaad Campbell is still settling in at the starting linebacker spot opposite Baun, and there’s been a rotating cast at safety, with Marcus Epps and Michael Carter II now splitting reps opposite Andrew Mukuba, who has been dealing with a knee injury. The safety spot in particular has become problematic. Interestingly, the Eagles signed former Pro Bowl defensive back Kenny Moore II to the…
